mechanism: Alpha-ketoglutarate promotes GTP loading of RagB and lysosomal translocation of mTORC1, reportedly through prolyl hydroxylase activity
notes: The prolyl-hydroxylase requirement has been disputed and the hydroxylated target is not defined.

mechanism: Amino-acid withdrawal recruits folliculin to lysosomes, where it binds RagA and is held in an inactive lysosomal complex; amino-acid restoration releases it and licenses RagC/D GTP hydrolysis, supporting Rag-dependent recruitment of mTORC1.
notes: Lysosomal residence of FLCN rises when amino acids are withdrawn, whereas its RagC/D GAP activity is exerted when they are restored.

mechanism: Amino-acid sufficiency promotes translocation of mTORC1 from a diffuse cytosolic pool to the lysosomal surface, where it encounters its proximate activator Rheb.GTP

Luminal amino acids act through the v-ATPase, in a manner requiring its ATP hydrolysis, to weaken its interaction with Ragulator at the V1 sector without changing lysosomal pH; this conformational relay is the first step of inside-out signalling to the Rag GTPases.
Arf1 is required for glutamine-induced mTORC1 activation and lysosomal translocation by a route that does not require the Rag GTPases
notes: The Arf1-dependent, Rag-independent glutamine route has been reported by one laboratory lineage (Jewell 2015; Meng 2020) and has not been independently reproduced.

mechanism: Arginine binds CASTOR1 with a dissociation constant of about 30 µM in a pocket at the interface of its ACT2 and ACT4 domains, triggering a conformational change that releases GATOR2.
notes: The measured dissociation constant is about 30 µM (Chantranupong 2016).

sites: substrate pocket in the transmembrane bundle
mechanism: Arginine binds the SLC38A9 transmembrane pocket; the cytosolic N terminus relays amino-acid availability to Rag-associated machinery.
notes: The N-terminal signalling domain is distinct from the arginine-binding pocket.

mechanism: Completed autophagolysosomal degradation replenishes the lysosomal and cytosolic amino-acid pools
Amino acids liberated by autophagic degradation reactivate mTORC1, making the system oscillatory rather than switch-like, a feature with implications for drug kinetics.
C12orf66 is one of the four subunits of the KICSTOR scaffold
Apo-CASTOR1 sequesters GATOR2, performing for arginine the function Sestrin2 performs for leucine
CASTOR2 heterodimerises with CASTOR1; the heterodimer binds GATOR2 but CASTOR2 itself does not confer high-affinity arginine binding
CASTOR2 binds GATOR2 as part of the CASTOR1-CASTOR2 heterodimer, contributing to arginine-regulated control of the hub
Net effect of the SLC38A9-NPC1 signalling complex: lysosomal cholesterol sufficiency promotes mTORC1 activation independently of amino acids

SLC38A9 senses lysosomal cholesterol through conserved cholesterol-responsive motifs in its transmembrane region; this sterol input, separable from arginine sensing, drives Rag-dependent recruitment and activation of mTORC1.
notes: The arginine-sensing and transport roles of SLC38A9 are well established, whereas the cholesterol arm is still emerging.

mechanism: DEPDC5 is the largest of the three GATOR1 subunits and provides the principal Rag-binding surface

DEPDC5 binds GTP-loaded RagA with high affinity in an inhibitory mode that restrains, rather than stimulates, GATOR1-mediated GTP hydrolysis; catalysis is executed through weaker NPRL2-NPRL3 contacts, and the DEPDC5 mode is proposed to keep GATOR1 from becoming hyperactive.
notes: DEPDC5 is the main Rag-binding subunit of GATOR1 but not its catalytic subunit; the role of the inhibitory binding mode in cells is still being defined.

mechanism: Folliculin supplies the longin GAP domain of the FLCN-FNIP heterodimer
FLCN-FNIP is the GAP for RagC, driving it to the GDP state required for the active heterodimer; unlike GATOR1 this GAP activity is positive for mTORC1
FLCN-FNIP acts with the same polarity on RagD, the RagC paralogue, promoting the GDP state that supports mTORC1 recruitment

FLCN-FNIP loads RagC/D with GDP, which is specifically required for mTORC1 to phosphorylate TFEB at Ser211 and keep it cytoplasmic; FLCN loss therefore leaves TFEB nuclear while S6K1 and 4E-BP1 phosphorylation are preserved.
notes: The effect on TFEB is indirect, exerted through the Rag heterodimer, and explains the tissue-dependent rather than uniform mTORC1 phenotype of FLCN loss.

mechanism: FNIP1 was identified through its interaction with both folliculin and AMPK, suggesting the FLCN-FNIP module also reads energy status
notes: The functional consequence of the FNIP1-AMPK interaction is not settled.

mechanism: FNIP1 heterodimerises with folliculin to form the catalytically competent RagC/D GAP
FNIP2 is the paralogue of FNIP1 and forms an equivalent FLCN-FNIP2 GAP complex
GATOR1 is the GTPase-activating protein for RagA, driving GTP hydrolysis and so releasing mTORC1 from the lysosome; it is active when amino acids are scarce
GATOR1 acts with equivalent GAP polarity on RagB, the RagA paralogue, making it a negative regulator of mTORC1 recruitment
GATOR2 is a positive regulator of mTORC1 that acts by inhibiting GATOR1; the molecular basis of that inhibition remains incompletely defined
notes: The mechanism by which GATOR2 inhibits GATOR1 is not fully resolved.

mechanism: RagC/D must be GDP-loaded for the asymmetric, mTORC1-competent configuration; RagC.GTP yields the inactive heterodimer
RagD-GDP, generated by FLCN-FNIP GAP activity, is the configuration that together with RagA/B-GTP makes the heterodimer competent to recruit mTORC1
notes: RagD is the RagC paralogue and carries the same GDP requirement.

mechanism: Glutaminase hydrolyses glutamine to glutamate and ammonia, the first step of glutaminolysis; glutamate is then converted to alpha-ketoglutarate by GLUD1 or transaminases, so GLS is required for, but does not itself produce, alpha-ketoglutarate from glutamine.
notes: Blocking glutaminolysis was reported to prevent RagB GTP loading and mTORC1 activation by glutamine and leucine (Duran 2012); that downstream link rests on one laboratory.

mechanism: Glucose starvation induces OGT-dependent O-GlcNAcylation of LARS1 at Ser1042, which blocks LARS1 binding to RagD and promotes ULK1 phosphorylation of its leucine-binding site, so LARS1 relays leucine to mTORC1 only when glucose is available.
Glutamate dehydrogenase catalyses the glutamate-to-alpha-ketoglutarate step that makes glutaminolysis an input to lysosomal mTORC1 activation
Glutaminolysis converts glutamine via glutamate to alpha-ketoglutarate, the metabolite that links anaplerotic flux to Rag loading

Glutamine activates mTORC1 through an Arf1-dependent route that persists in RagA/B-deficient cells and requires the v-ATPase; this arm runs in parallel with Rag-dependent glutamine inputs such as glutaminolysis.
notes: Reported by one laboratory lineage (Jewell 2015; Meng 2020) and not yet independently reproduced.

mechanism: GTP loading of RagA/B is the nucleotide state that confers Raptor binding on the heterodimer; the reciprocal state releases mTORC1 to the cytosol
GTP loading of RagB (the RagA paralogue) generates the signalling-competent RagB-GTP state that binds the Raptor claw
notes: RagB is the RagA paralogue and carries the same GTP requirement.

mechanism: ITFG2 is one of the four subunits of the KICSTOR scaffold
KICSTOR recruits GATOR1 to the lysosomal surface; without it GATOR1 cannot reach its Rag substrate and nutrients fail to regulate mTORC1
The KICSTOR scaffold localises to the lysosomal surface and is the platform that positions GATOR1 there
KPTN is one of the four subunits of the KICSTOR scaffold
N-terminal myristoylation and palmitoylation of LAMTOR1 anchor Ragulator, and with it the Rag heterodimer, to the lysosomal membrane
notes: LAMTOR1 is lipid-anchored; the specific modified residues are reported in the primary literature.

mechanism: LAMTOR1 wraps around the LAMTOR2-5 roadblock heterodimers and supplies the membrane anchor of the pentameric complex

LAMTOR1 (p18) binds the v-ATPase directly, contacting V0 subunit d1 and V1 subunit D, and so physically couples the proton pump to the Ragulator-Rag module; amino acids weaken the Ragulator interaction with the V1 sector.
LAMTOR2 forms a roadblock heterodimer with LAMTOR3 within Ragulator
LAMTOR3 partners LAMTOR2 in the Ragulator roadblock core
LAMTOR4 forms a roadblock heterodimer with LAMTOR5 that directly contacts the Rag roadblock domains
LAMTOR5 partners LAMTOR4 in the Ragulator roadblock core
LARS1 was reported to act as a leucine-dependent GAP for RagD, driving it to the GDP state that supports mTORC1 recruitment
notes: Contested: the yeast orthologue acts on Gtr1, the RagA/B counterpart, with the opposite activity [51]; the mammalian and fungal models are unreconciled.

mechanism: Leucine allosterically activates glutamate dehydrogenase (GLUD1), increasing conversion of glutamate to alpha-ketoglutarate during glutaminolysis.
notes: Classical allosteric regulation that also underlies leucine-stimulated insulin secretion; the link from alpha-ketoglutarate to Rag GTP loading rests on a single laboratory (Duran 2012).

mechanism: Leucyl-tRNA synthetase was proposed to act as an intracellular leucine sensor, coupling leucine charging status to mTORC1
notes: The model is contested: the yeast orthologue acts on the RagA/B counterpart with opposite polarity, and the two models have never been reconciled [51].

mechanism: Leucine binds SAR1B and causes it to dissociate from GATOR2, relieving SAR1B-mediated inhibition of mTORC1; without leucine, SAR1B binds GATOR2 and inhibits mTORC1.
notes: Single-laboratory finding awaiting independent replication.

mechanism: Sestrin1 binds leucine to a similar extent as Sestrin2, through the C-terminal pocket conserved between them, and leucine releases endogenous Sestrin1 from GATOR2.
notes: Sestrin3 binds leucine very weakly and its GATOR2 binding is leucine-insensitive (Wolfson 2016).

mechanism: Free leucine binds Sestrin2 with a dissociation constant of approximately 20 uM through a C-terminal pocket, disrupting its grip on GATOR2
notes: The binding is established in vitro and structurally, while its physiological primacy is contested.

mechanism: mTORC1 is activated on the cytosolic face of the lysosomal membrane, which is the point at which nutrient, growth-factor and stress information is spatially integrated
notes: Lysosomal dysfunction in ageing and in lysosomal storage disease is a plausible upstream cause of mTOR dysregulation, not only a consequence.

mechanism: Rheb resides on lysosomal/endomembrane surfaces, so mTORC1 can only meet GTP-loaded Rheb after Rag-dependent recruitment; cytosolic mTORC1 is effectively Rheb-free

MAT2A converts methionine and ATP into S-adenosylmethionine, the metabolite bound by SAMTOR, and acute MAT2A loss attenuates methionine sensing by mTORC1 in cultured cells; MAT2A is the extrahepatic isoform, whereas MAT1A predominates in adult liver.
Methionine is converted to S-adenosylmethionine, so SAM concentration reports dietary methionine availability to the SAMTOR arm
notes: Methionine is a well-established longevity-modifying nutrient, linked to mTORC1 by this route.

mechanism: MIOS is a beta-propeller subunit of the octameric GATOR2 assembly
NPC1 associates with SLC38A9 and exports lysosomal cholesterol; loss of NPC1 traps cholesterol in the lumen and hyperactivates mTORC1 through this complex
notes: The inhibitory sign reflects NPC1 removing the activating sterol; the cholesterol arm remains an emerging mechanism.

mechanism: NPRL2 contributes the longin domain that carries the catalytic residue for GAP activity toward RagA/B
NPRL2 is the catalytic subunit of the GATOR1 GAP: its Arg78 acts as the arginine finger, inserting into the RagA nucleotide pocket to stimulate GTP hydrolysis.
notes: DEPDC5 provides the high-affinity Rag-binding surface of GATOR1 but is not catalytic; hydrolysis is driven through weaker NPRL2-NPRL3 contacts with RagA (Shen 2018).

mechanism: NPRL3 bridges NPRL2 and DEPDC5 to complete the trimeric GATOR1 assembly

OGT O-GlcNAcylates LARS1 at Ser1042 during glucose starvation, which blocks LARS1 binding to RagD and promotes ULK1 phosphorylation of its leucine-binding site, lowering leucine-induced mTORC1 activity.
notes: OGT knockdown or inhibition suppresses LARS1 O-GlcNAcylation; why glucose starvation increases this modification is unresolved. Reported by a single laboratory.

mechanism: Rab1A is required for amino-acid-stimulated mTORC1 activation and interacts with Rheb on Golgi membranes; it is amplified and oncogenic in colorectal cancer
notes: Independent replication of the Golgi Rheb-Rab1A interaction remains limited.

mechanism: Rag-Ragulator provides the lysosomal docking site for FLCN-FNIP; during starvation FLCN is held inactive on RagA.GDP until amino acids are resupplied
Structural work defines the Ragulator-Rag assembly as the platform onto which mTORC1 docks at the lysosomal surface
The pentameric Ragulator clamps the Rag roadblock domains against the lysosomal membrane, providing the anchor without which the Rags cannot deliver mTORC1

Ragulator was reported to act as a guanine nucleotide exchange factor for RagA/B (Bar-Peled 2012), but later reconstitution found that it chiefly triggers GTP release from RagC, with SLC38A9 acting as the GEF for RagA.
notes: Shen and Sabatini (2018) attribute the original RagA/B result to assay limitations, including possibly copurifying SLC38A9, while noting that Ragulator still alters the GTP affinity of RagA.

mechanism: During amino-acid starvation Rag-Ragulator traps FLCN-FNIP2 in the inactive lysosomal folliculin complex (LFC), holding FLCN's catalytic arginine finger away from the RagC nucleotide pocket; amino-acid refeeding releases the complex and licenses RagC/D GTP hydrolysis. This checkpoint explains why FLCN GAP activity is nutrient-gated.
notes: Two independent cryo-EM structures (Lawrence 2019; Shen 2019) show FLCN-FNIP2 bound to RagA-GDP with the FLCN catalytic arginine away from the RagC nucleotide; Shen 2019 interprets this state as an on-pathway intermediate rather than an inhibitory trap.

mechanism: The active Rag configuration tethers mTORC1 to the lysosomal surface; cryo-EM defines how mTORC1 docks onto the Rag-Ragulator assembly
RagA/B.GTP-RagC/D.GDP binds Raptor directly; this interaction is the physical basis of amino-acid-dependent mTORC1 localisation
The Rag GTPases recruit TFEB (and MITF family members) to the lysosomal surface, which is the prerequisite for their phosphorylation by mTORC1

GTP-loaded Rheb binds the N-HEAT, M-HEAT and FAT regions of mTOR, distal to the catalytic cleft, and allosterically realigns the FAT and kinase domains into a catalytically competent active site; lysosomal recruitment alone is insufficient for activation.

The lysosomal E3 ligase RNF152 attaches K63-linked ubiquitin chains to RagA in an amino-acid-sensitive manner, creating a docking site that recruits GATOR1 and so promotes RagA GTP hydrolysis and mTORC1 inactivation.
notes: Reported by a single laboratory (Deng 2015).

mechanism: RagA forms the obligate heterodimer with RagC or RagD through paired roadblock domains
Intersubunit crosstalk: the nucleotide state of one Rag biases the nucleotide state and GAP accessibility of its partner, enabling rapid switching with amino-acid availability
notes: Crosstalk is reciprocal.

mechanism: RagB is the functional paralogue of RagA and occupies the same position in the obligate heterodimer
RagC pairs with RagA/B through roadblock-domain contacts to form the obligate heterodimer
Phosphorylation of TFEB by mTORC1 requires RagC/D in its GDP state, making TFEB a substrate-specific output of the FLCN arm rather than of Rheb-driven mTORC1 activity
notes: Substrate-selective output: TFEB phosphorylation depends on the nucleotide state of RagC/D rather than on bulk mTORC1 activity toward S6K1 and 4E-BP1.

mechanism: RagD is the functional paralogue of RagC within the obligate heterodimer

RUVBL1 (Pontin) binds the Tel2-Tti1-Tti2 module as part of the R2TP co-chaperone, whose PIH1D1 subunit recognises CK2-phosphorylated Tel2. The ATP-dependent TTT-RUVBL1/2 assembly is needed for mTOR stability, mTORC1 dimerisation and mTORC1 binding to the Rag GTPases.
notes: RUVBL1 is not a subunit of TTT itself, which comprises Tel2, Tti1 and Tti2; energy depletion disassembles the TTT-RUVBL1/2 complex.

mechanism: RUVBL2 (Reptin) binds the Tel2-Tti1-Tti2 module together with RUVBL1 as part of the R2TP co-chaperone, whose PIH1D1 subunit recognises CK2-phosphorylated Tel2. The ATP-dependent TTT-RUVBL1/2 assembly is needed for mTOR stability, mTORC1 dimerisation and mTORC1 binding to the Rag GTPases.
notes: RUVBL2 is not a subunit of TTT itself, which comprises Tel2, Tti1 and Tti2; energy depletion disassembles the TTT-RUVBL1/2 complex.

mechanism: SAM binds SAMTOR with a Kd of approximately 7 uM; binding relieves SAMTOR-promoted GATOR1 activity
Unlike Sestrin2 and CASTOR1, apo-SAMTOR acts directly on GATOR1, promoting its activity and so inhibiting mTORC1 when SAM is low
SAMTOR engages the GATOR1-KICSTOR assembly rather than GATOR2, which is why the methionine arm bypasses the Sestrin/CASTOR hub
In the absence of leucine SAR1B binds GATOR2 and blocks its inhibition of GATOR1, keeping mTORC1 off; leucine binding to SAR1B dissociates the SAR1B-GATOR2 complex.
notes: Single primary report; the leucine-sensing role of SAR1B awaits independent replication.

mechanism: Leucine-bound SAR1B was reported to regulate mTORC1 activity; the downstream connection to the Rag machinery is not firmly established
notes: Net effect of the SAR1B arm; the molecular step is the binding of apo-SAR1B to GATOR2, and the route from GATOR2 to the Rag GTPases was not defined in the primary report.

mechanism: SEC13, also a COPII and nuclear-pore component, is a structural subunit of GATOR2
SEH1L, a WD40 protein shared with the nuclear pore complex, is a structural subunit of GATOR2
Sestrin1 interacts with GATOR2 in the same way as Sestrin2, contributing to negative regulation of the amino-acid sensing pathway
notes: SESN1/2/3 differ in tissue expression, so which sensing mechanism dominates is expected to vary between tissues.

mechanism: Sestrins have been reported to activate AMPK and so to inhibit mTORC1 through TSC2, a route independent of GATOR2 sequestration; the molecular basis is undefined and Sestrin2 still suppresses mTORC1 in AMPK-null cells.
notes: The AMPK arm is reported rather than reproduced; the best-supported route from Sestrin2 to mTORC1 is sequestration of GATOR2.

mechanism: Apo-Sestrin2 binds GATOR2 across the WDR24 and SEH1L beta-propellers, with auxiliary contacts to MIOS, preventing GATOR2 from inhibiting GATOR1 so RagA/B remain GDP-bound and mTORC1 leaves the lysosome; leucine binding (Kd approximately 20 microM) releases GATOR2.
notes: Established in vitro and structurally, while the physiological primacy of Sestrin2 as a leucine sensor is contested. Sestrin2 is itself induced by p53 and ATF4, so stress input converges on this step.

mechanism: Alternative model in which Sestrin2 acts as a guanine-nucleotide dissociation inhibitor for RagA/B, locking them in the GDP state, rather than acting only by sequestering GATOR2. Published results conflict with the GATOR2-sequestration-only model.
notes: Contested: the guanine-nucleotide dissociation inhibitor model and the GATOR2-sequestration model of Sestrin action are in direct conflict and have not been reconciled.

mechanism: Sestrin2 binds the WDR24-SEH1L region of GATOR2; MIOS is the principal CASTOR1-binding subunit.
Sestrin3 also binds GATOR2 and negatively regulates the amino-acid sensing pathway upstream of mTORC1
Under amino-acid starvation SH3BP4 binds the inactive Rag heterodimer and prevents formation of the active, mTORC1-recruiting configuration
notes: Single primary report; not independently replicated or shown in vivo.

mechanism: SCF-SKP2 attaches K63-linked ubiquitin chains to RagA and promotes GATOR1 recruitment, a negative feedback that limits amino-acid-dependent mTORC1 hyperactivation.
notes: Single primary report; the acceptor lysines on RagA are not defined.

mechanism: SLC1A5 (ASCT2) is an obligatory sodium-dependent antiporter for glutamine; in the original model its uptake supplies the intracellular glutamine that LAT1 effluxes to drive leucine import, although later work finds ASCT2 dispensable for glutamine accumulation and mTORC1 activation when SNAT1 and SNAT2 are expressed.
notes: The transport step itself is firmly established; the role of ASCT2 as the driver of leucine-dependent mTORC1 activation is disputed.

mechanism: Arginine-activated SLC38A9 effluxes essential amino acids from the lysosomal lumen into the cytosol, which is how protein taken up by macropinocytosis or autophagy becomes usable nutrient; loss of SLC38A9 traps these amino acids in the lysosome.
notes: Lysosomal efflux through SLC38A9 is well supported, but its quantitative weight relative to cytosolic amino-acid sensing is undefined.

mechanism: SLC38A9 effluxes leucine and other essential amino acids from the lysosomal lumen in an arginine-dependent manner, supplying the cytosolic pool read by Sestrin2
notes: Lysosomal leucine efflux through SLC38A9 is well supported; its quantitative weight relative to cytosolic sensing is undefined.

mechanism: Node-level summary: SLC38A9 activates mTORC1 through luminal arginine sensing and through lysosomal efflux of leucine and other essential amino acids; the cholesterol-sensing arm it shares with NPC1 is less firmly established and is carried separately.
notes: Established for the arginine-sensing and transport arms; the cholesterol arm is emerging.

mechanism: SLC38A9 and NPC1 physically associate in the lysosomal cholesterol-sensing pathway. This binding edge does not assert inhibition of NPC1 transport by SLC38A9.
notes: Reciprocal arm of the SLC38A9-NPC1 cholesterol switch; the cholesterol route is less firmly established than arginine sensing.

mechanism: SLC38A9 co-assembles with Ragulator and the Rag GTPases as part of the lysosomal amino-acid sensing machinery; this contact positions the transceptor, while the arginine-dependent activating signal is exerted on the Rag GTPases.
Arginine-bound SLC38A9 binds the Rag-Ragulator complex and signals amino-acid sufficiency, promoting mTORC1 recruitment
SLC38A9 acts as a non-canonical GEF for RagA, accelerating GDP release and favouring the GTP-loaded, Raptor-binding state
notes: Non-canonical exchange mechanism; the activity resides in the N-terminal Ram domain of SLC38A9.

mechanism: SLC3A2 (4F2hc/CD98 heavy chain) is disulphide-bonded to the SLC7A5 light chain; the heavy chain is required for surface delivery and transport function of the LAT1 heterodimer.
notes: The heavy chain is transport-inactive on its own and acts as the trafficking subunit; SLC7A5 carries the transport site.

mechanism: LAT1/4F2hc is an obligatory antiporter: it effluxes intracellular glutamine in exchange for extracellular leucine, so SLC1A5-mediated glutamine uptake is the driving force for leucine import. This coupling is why glutamine deprivation blunts leucine-driven mTORC1 activation.
notes: Obligatory antiport: leucine import is coupled to glutamine efflux, so this route depletes rather than supplies the cytosolic glutamine pool, which is why glutamine deprivation blunts leucine-driven mTORC1 activation.

mechanism: LAT1 imports leucine at the plasma membrane in obligatory exchange for efflux of intracellular glutamine, setting the cytosolic leucine concentration seen by the sensors
notes: Leucine import through LAT1 is obligatorily coupled to efflux of intracellular glutamine.

mechanism: SZT2 binds GATOR1 directly and dictates GATOR control of mTORC1 signalling, acting as the pivotal contact within the scaffold
SZT2 not only nucleates KICSTOR but also contacts GATOR2, bringing GATOR1 and GATOR2 into one lysosomal supercomplex so that the sensor branch and the GAP branch are physically coupled.
notes: SZT2 contacts both GATOR complexes; the GATOR2 arm is the less well defined of the two.

mechanism: SZT2 is the very large fourth subunit around which the KICSTOR scaffold assembles
Under nutrient sufficiency the TTT-RUVBL1/2 complex promotes mTORC1 dimerisation and its localisation to the Rag-Ragulator platform; energy stress disassembles it
notes: The lysosomal-localisation arm rests largely on one laboratory, hence the emerging grade.

mechanism: Truncating and missense DEPDC5 variants disrupt the Rag-binding subunit of GATOR1, so the complex can no longer be recruited to and act on RagA/B; missense variants are often hypomorphic rather than null.

Germline heterozygous DEPDC5 loss of function disinhibits RagA/B and produces mTORC1 hyperactivity in the cortical lesion, causing familial focal epilepsy with variable foci and elevated risk of sudden unexpected death in epilepsy.
notes: In a small open-label series, the three patients with DEPDC5 truncating variants had the largest seizure reductions on everolimus while the patient with a missense variant responded less; the evidence is open-label and very small.

mechanism: Loss of folliculin causes Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome with fibrofolliculomas, pulmonary cysts and renal tumours
Germline FLCN loss abolishes RagC/D GAP activity, dysregulating mTORC1 in a tissue-dependent rather than uniformly increased manner
notes: FLCN loss does not raise mTORC1 activity uniformly across tissues.

mechanism: Without FLCN GAP activity RagC/D remains GTP-bound, so mTORC1 cannot phosphorylate TFEB at Ser211 even though it phosphorylates S6K1 and 4E-BP1 normally, and TFEB accumulates constitutively in the nucleus; removing TFEB rescues the renal phenotype of kidney-specific Flcn-knockout mice, indicating that this substrate-selective lesion rather than global mTORC1 hyperactivity drives it.
notes: Consistent with the tissue-dependent rather than uniformly increased mTORC1 signalling seen in Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome.

mechanism: NPRL2 loss of function causes familial focal epilepsy of the GATOR1 spectrum through unopposed RagA/B-GTP loading and mTORC1 hyperactivity, with a focal cortical malformation in a minority of patients. In a small open-label series of NPRL2- and NPRL3-related epilepsy, add-on everolimus reduced seizures in all four patients treated, two of whom became seizure-free, although stomatitis led one patient to stop treatment.
notes: The therapeutic evidence is open-label and very small; a controlled trial is required before mTOR inhibition becomes standard practice in these epilepsies.

mechanism: Loss-of-function NPRL2 variants remove the catalytic arginine-finger subunit, abolishing GATOR1 GAP activity toward RagA/B.

NPRL3 loss of function causes familial focal epilepsy of the GATOR1 spectrum through unopposed RagA/B-GTP loading and mTORC1 hyperactivity in the cortical lesion. Responses to add-on everolimus have differed between series: the single NPRL3 patient in the first case series worsened, whereas all four patients in a later NPRL2- and NPRL3-related series improved, two of them becoming seizure-free.
notes: The small open-label series do not establish NPRL3 genotype as a predictor of everolimus failure, and a controlled trial is required before mTOR inhibition becomes standard practice.

mechanism: Loss-of-function NPRL3 variants destabilise the GATOR1 heterotrimer and abolish its GAP activity toward RagA/B.
Biallelic SZT2 mutations cause infantile encephalopathy with epilepsy and dysmorphic corpus callosum - the clinical proof that KICSTOR is non-redundant in humans
Biallelic SZT2 loss-of-function disables the scaffold, preventing GATOR1 recruitment and producing nutrient-insensitive mTORC1 activity

The proton gradient generated by the v-ATPase drives amino-acid efflux from the lysosomal lumen; lysosomal metabolomics shows v-ATPase- and mTOR-dependent control of lysosomal amino-acid export, placing the pump upstream of SLC38A9-dependent efflux as well as of the inside-out Ragulator signal.
notes: Transport-level role of the v-ATPase, distinct from its inside-out signalling to Ragulator.

mechanism: The v-ATPase relays luminal amino-acid content outward by regulating Ragulator GEF activity toward RagA/B - the inside-out sensing mechanism
v-ATPase function is required for amino acids to drive the Rag heterodimer into its active nucleotide configuration and recruit mTORC1
Within GATOR2, WDR24 is the subunit most strictly required for GATOR2 to inhibit GATOR1 and hence for amino-acid-dependent mTORC1 activation.
notes: Subunit-level requirement from structural and genetic work; the molecular basis of GATOR2 inhibition of GATOR1 remains incompletely defined.

mechanism: WDR24 is one of the five named subunits of the octameric GATOR2 assembly
WDR59 is a beta-propeller/RING-like subunit of the octameric GATOR2 assembly
AKT phosphorylates PRAS40 Thr246, promoting 14-3-3 binding and release of PRAS40 from Raptor; feed-forward derepression of mTORC1 by growth factors.
AKT phosphorylates BAD at Ser99, creating a 14-3-3 binding site that sequesters BAD and prevents it from neutralising BCL-XL; this survival output is favoured by Ser473-phosphorylated AKT.
AKT phosphorylation of FOXO1 creates 14-3-3 sites and excludes it from the nucleus; output markedly enhanced by mTORC2-dependent Ser473 phosphorylation.
notes: hepatic mTORC2→AKT→FOXO1 restrains gluconeogenesis (7.2).

mechanism: AKT phosphorylates FOXO3a at three sites, promoting 14-3-3 binding and cytoplasmic retention, suppressing pro-apoptotic transcription.
AKT phosphorylates GSK3β Ser9 (GSK3α Ser21), creating a pseudosubstrate that inhibits the kinase; an mTORC1-independent AKT output retained with Thr308-only phosphorylation.
AKT phosphorylates MDM2 Ser166/Ser186, promoting nuclear translocation and p53 ubiquitination; an mTORC1-independent AKT output.
notes: MDM2 is one of the mTORC1-independent AKT outputs that make distal-network lesions poor predictors of rapalog sensitivity.

mechanism: AKT phosphorylates TSC2 at five sites, Ser939 and Thr1462 being dominant, creating 14-3-3 binding sites; the demonstrated consequence is release of the TSC complex from the lysosomal membrane where Rheb resides, so Rheb·GTP accumulates. Stable dissociation of TSC1 from TSC2 remains poorly supported.
notes: Part of the double-negative AKT -| TSC -| Rheb circuit. AKT phosphorylated only at Thr308 retains substantial activity toward TSC2 [387,388].

mechanism: Insulin/AKT-dependent TSC2 phosphorylation releases the TSC complex from lysosomal membranes, physically separating the Rheb GAP from Rheb.
notes: Conversely, amino-acid starvation recruits TSC2 to the lysosome via Rag GTPases (Demetriades 2014, PMID:24529380).

mechanism: PRAS40 TOS motif occupies the Raptor substrate pocket and its N-terminal segment contacts mTOR, blocking S6K1/4E-BP1 access; substoichiometric mTORC1 component.
p110α-selective ATP-competitive inhibitor; with fulvestrant improved PFS from 5.7 to 11.0 months in PIK3CA-mutant HR+ advanced breast cancer (SOLAR-1).
Testosterone/DHT bind the androgen receptor, driving its nuclear and non-genomic activity.
Androgen/AR signalling raises mTORC1 activity and cyclin D translation in prostate cancer cells; AR and PI3K–AKT are reciprocally cross-inhibitory in PTEN-null prostate cancer.
notes: Indirect, multi-step input; the molecular intermediary (PI3K-dependent and -independent components) is not fully resolved.

mechanism: Pan-AKT ATP-competitive inhibitor; with fulvestrant improved PFS from 3.1 to 7.3 months in AKT-pathway-altered HR+ breast cancer (CAPItello-291).
DGKζ phosphorylates diacylglycerol to phosphatidic acid; the mechanically induced rise in PA and mTORC1 activity in muscle depends on DGKζ rather than on PLD.
notes: From the Hornberger laboratory; qualifies the PLD-centred model [241,683].

mechanism: Indirect. EGFR carries no high-affinity p85-binding motif of its own, so EGF-stimulated PI3K and AKT signalling is relayed through the docking protein GAB1 and, in EGFR-ERBB3 heterodimers, through the pYXXM motifs of ERBB3.
notes: this is the route by which receptor tyrosine kinase amplification raises PI3K flux.

mechanism: ERK1/2 phosphorylate Raptor at Ser8/Ser696/Ser863 (proline-directed), promoting Ras-dependent mTORC1 activation.
notes: Direct phosphorylation of Raptor at Ser8, Ser696 and Ser863 by ERK1/2 rests mainly on one laboratory; Ser863 is also phosphorylated in an insulin- and mTOR-dependent manner. ERK and RSK input to mTORC1 is more commonly routed through the TSC complex rather than through Raptor.

mechanism: ERK docks on the RSK C-terminus and phosphorylates the CTKD activation loop and linker; CTKD then autophosphorylates the hydrophobic motif (Ser380), creating the PDK1 docking site.
notes: Site numbering is RSK1 (RPS6KA1).

mechanism: ERK phosphorylates TSC2 (Ser664 principal), dissociating TSC1–TSC2 and functionally inactivating the complex; links Ras/MAPK activation to mTORC1.
Non-genomic: ligand-bound ERα binds p85α and activates PI3K–AKT; in TSC2-null cells estrogen enhances survival and pulmonary metastasis via ERK/mTORC1 signalling.
notes: Cell-type dependent; the LAM relevance is the reason this input is documented in the mTOR literature.

mechanism: 17β-estradiol binds ERα, enabling both genomic transcription and rapid non-genomic signalling to PI3K–AKT.
Farnesylation of the Rheb CAAX motif (Cys181) is required for endomembrane/lysosomal localisation and hence for mTORC1 activation.
FKBP38 was proposed to bind the mTOR FRB region and hold mTORC1 inactive until displaced by Rheb·GTP.
notes: Independent laboratories found no effect of FKBP38 depletion or overexpression on mTORC1 signalling; retained only as a flagged contested model of how Rheb·GTP activates mTORC1.

mechanism: Grb10 binds and desensitises the IGF-1 receptor in the same manner as INSR.
Stabilised Grb10 binds the activated insulin receptor kinase (SH2/BPS domains), desensitising receptor signalling to IRS/PI3K.
The GRB2 SH3 domains bind the proline-rich C-terminus of SOS1 constitutively; receptor engagement relocates the GRB2–SOS1 complex to the plasma membrane next to Ras.
HERC1 E3 ligase binds and ubiquitinates TSC2 not protected by TSC1, promoting its degradation.
notes: Single primary study; physiological contribution relative to other TSC2 turnover routes not well quantified.

mechanism: IGF-1 binding to IGF-1R induces β-subunit autophosphorylation and IRS/Shc docking; shares the IRS–PI3K–AKT route to TSC2/mTORC1 with insulin.
IGF-1R kinase tyrosine-phosphorylates IRS-1 (and IRS-2) YXXM motifs, recruiting p85–PI3K; mechanistically parallel to INSR.
Chronic inflammatory signalling activates the IKK complex (IKKβ), which besides NF-κB engages TSC1; proposed link between inflammation and anabolic dysregulation of ageing tissue.
Activated INSR kinase phosphorylates IRS-1 on multiple tyrosines in YXXM motifs, generating SH2-docking sites for p85–PI3K and GRB2.
notes: Tyrosine sites are numerous (e.g. human Tyr612/Tyr632 equivalents of rat Tyr608/Tyr628 bind p85); not listed individually to avoid numbering ambiguity.

mechanism: Insulin binds the INSR α-subunit ectodomain, triggering β-subunit trans-autophosphorylation and creating docking sites for IRS proteins and Shc.
Phospho-YXXM motifs on IRS-1 engage the SH2 domains of p85, relieving p85 inhibition of p110 and bringing PI3K to membrane PI(4,5)P2.
Stress-activated p38 MAPK phosphorylates and activates MK2.

mTORC2 selects AKT by distal docking: the basic surface of the AKT kinase N-lobe engages an acidic loop of the mSin1 CRIM domain and the C-lobe a Rictor–mSin1 mooring ~75 Å from the active site; residues flanking Ser473 are dispensable, and prior engagement of pThr450 by the same N-lobe residues builds in a proofreading step.
notes: The primary support is the 2025 enzyme-substrate structure [597]; the 'conserved tri-arginine cluster' formulation is inaccurate and should be avoided. The claim rests on this single structural study, with [74,483] as supporting cellular observations.

mechanism: MK2 phosphorylates TSC2 Ser1210, enhancing 14-3-3 binding; the net effect on Rheb-GAP activity and mTORC1 output is not firmly established.
notes: Direction of effect on mTORC1 left as 'modulates' because functional readouts were limited.

mechanism: Eccentric contraction or stretch increases DGKζ-dependent PA synthesis; DGKζ overexpression is sufficient to induce fibre hypertrophy.

Mechanical stretch and eccentric contraction were reported to raise phosphatidic acid in skeletal muscle through phospholipase D, independently of ERK and PI3K; later work from the same laboratory found that phospholipase D activity does not rise with loading and that the mechanically induced phosphatidic acid depends on diacylglycerol kinase zeta.
notes: The phospholipase D and diacylglycerol kinase zeta routes are competing accounts of the same load-induced rise in phosphatidic acid in skeletal muscle.

mechanism: Eccentric contractions increase TSC2 RxRxxS/T-motif phosphorylation and move TSC2 away from the lysosome while mTOR associates with it; responsible kinase not defined.
notes: The mechanistic link between mechanical load and TSC2 relocalisation rests on a single laboratory; phosphatidic acid/PLD and focal-adhesion routes are the alternatives [241,683].

mechanism: Dual-specificity MEK1/2 phosphorylate both residues of the ERK TEY activation-loop motif, Thr202 and Tyr204 in ERK1 and Thr185 and Tyr187 in ERK2, activating the kinases.
mTORC1 phosphorylates its own inhibitor PRAS40 (Ser183, Ser212, Ser221), weakening its binding to Raptor and reinforcing growth-factor-driven derepression.
mTORC1 phosphorylates and stabilises Grb10, increasing its abundance.
mTORC2 phosphorylates the hydrophobic motif Ser473; AKT docks on the mSin1 CRIM domain ~75 Å from the active site. Ser473 selectively enhances activity toward FOXO1/3 and BAD over GSK3β/TSC2.
notes: Recruitment of AKT through a 'tri-arginine cluster' on mSin1, common in secondary sources, lacks clear primary support; the distal-docking model rests on a single structural study [597].

mechanism: Cotranslational, constitutive turn-motif phosphorylation at Thr450 by ribosome-associated mTORC2 is required for AKT folding and stability.
Neurofibromin's GAP-related domain accelerates Ras GTP hydrolysis; NF1 loss raises Ras·GTP and ERK/RSK input to TSC2 and Raptor.
PDK1 phosphorylates the AKT activation loop at Thr308 once both are PIP3-bound; required for activity and, with Ser473, for full activation.
After mTORC1 phosphorylates the S6K1 hydrophobic motif (Thr389), PDK1 phosphorylates the activation loop at Thr229 (p70 numbering), completing S6K1 activation.
context: requires prior mTORC1 phosphorylation of S6K1 Thr389

mechanism: PDK1, recruited to the phospho-Ser386 hydrophobic motif, phosphorylates the NTKD activation loop, completing RSK activation.
notes: Site numbering is RSK2 (RPS6KA3).

mechanism: PHLPP1/2 directly dephosphorylate the AKT hydrophobic motif Ser473, terminating mTORC2-dependent activation and promoting apoptosis.

Phosphatidic acid binds the mTOR FRB domain, the surface also engaged by the FKBP12-rapamycin complex, and stimulates mTORC1; the Arg2109 dependence rests on mutagenesis in the original report, and displacement of DEPTOR has been described by one group.
notes: Mechanical activation of this route is ERK-independent. The quantitative contribution of phosphatidic acid relative to the other mechanical inputs to mTORC1 is unresolved.

mechanism: PA is reported to be required for assembly/stability of both mTORC1 and mTORC2 and to oppose rapamycin at the FRB domain.
Class I PI3K phosphorylates the 3-OH of PI(4,5)P2 to generate PI(3,4,5)P3 at the plasma membrane.
p85 nSH2 and iSH2 contact the p110α helical and C2 domains to restrain basal lipid-kinase activity; pY-peptide binding to nSH2 releases this (the contacts disrupted by E545K/H1047R).
p85α (nSH2–iSH2–cSH2) constitutively binds the p110 adaptor-binding domain, stabilising the catalytic subunit and forming the class IA heterodimer.
PI(4,5)P2 is 3-phosphorylated by PI3K to PI(3,4,5)P3; the reaction is reversed by the 3-phosphatase PTEN.
PIP3 (and PI(3,4)P2) binding to the AKT PH domain recruits AKT to the membrane and relieves PH–kinase autoinhibition, exposing Thr308 to PDK1.
PIP3 binding to the mSin1 C-terminal PH domain relieves its autoinhibitory fold-back onto mTOR and recruits mTORC2 to the plasma membrane where AKT resides.

The PDK1 PH domain binds PIP3 and PI(3,4)P2, holding PDK1 at the plasma membrane where PIP3-recruited AKT becomes accessible. PDK1 is catalytically active without stimulation and its own distribution changes little on growth-factor treatment, so the lipid governs substrate access, although phosphoinositide binding also promotes PDK1 trans-autophosphorylation.
PLD1 hydrolyses phosphatidylcholine to phosphatidic acid and choline.
The B55α-containing PP2A holoenzyme dephosphorylates AKT Thr308, opposing PDK1 and restraining AKT output to TSC2/PRAS40.
After DNA double-strand breaks DNA-PKcs phosphorylates AKT Ser473 independently of mTORC2, promoting survival signalling.
notes: A context-restricted alternative route to AKT Ser473 phosphorylation after DNA damage; mTORC2 remains the physiological hydrophobic-motif kinase for AKT.

mechanism: PTEN 3-phosphatase hydrolyses PIP3 back to PI(4,5)P2, terminating PDK1/AKT membrane recruitment; the dominant negative regulator of the PI3K–AKT–mTORC1 axis.
RAF phosphorylates MEK1 Ser218/Ser222 (MEK2 Ser222/Ser226) in the activation segment.
notes: MEK2 is phosphorylated at the equivalent residues Ser222 and Ser226. Phosphorylation of either serine is sufficient for maximal activation.

mechanism: GTP-bound H-Ras and K-Ras (predominantly KRAS4A) bind the atypical Ras-binding domain of mSin1. Oncogenic Ras was reported to promote mTORC2 activity at the plasma membrane, but a Sin1 mutant unable to bind Ras supports normal mTORC2 assembly and activity in cells and mice, and Sin1 overexpression was reported to suppress Ras signalling.
context: shown chiefly with oncogenic KRAS/HRAS in cultured cells
notes: The consequence of Ras binding for mTORC2 activity is disputed between laboratories. The Ras-binding domain is one of the defined mSin1 regions, but no function has been firmly assigned to it.

mechanism: Ras·GTP binds the p110α Ras-binding domain, allosterically activating PI3K and coupling RTK/Ras signalling to PIP3 production.
Ras·GTP binds the RAF Ras-binding and cysteine-rich domains, recruiting RAF to the membrane where dimerisation and phosphorylation activate it.
Rheb·GTP was proposed to bind FKBP38 and release it from mTOR, de-repressing mTORC1.
notes: Paired with FKBP8 → mTORC1; both contested.

mechanism: Rheb·GTP binds the mTOR N-HEAT/FAT region, realigning FAT and kinase domains (DFG motif, αC helix) into a catalytically competent state; needed after Rag-mediated lysosomal recruitment.
notes: Recruitment by Rags is necessary but not sufficient; Rheb binding supplies activation [364].

mechanism: Rheb·GTP binds and stimulates PLD1 in a GTP-dependent manner, providing a parallel phosphatidic-acid route to mTORC1 activation.
notes: Limited independent replication; relative contribution versus direct Rheb–mTOR binding unclear.

mechanism: Rheb·GTP binds the N-terminal region of B-Raf/C-Raf, reducing kinase activity and B-Raf–C-Raf heterodimerisation; an mTOR-independent crosstalk that dampens ERK output when TSC is lost.
notes: Reported by more than one group but with variable magnitude; graded emerging.

mechanism: The lysosomal E3 ligase RNF152 mono-ubiquitinates Rheb at Lys8, increasing its affinity for the TSC complex and suppressing mTORC1; EGF stimulation acts through AKT-phosphorylated USP4, which deubiquitinates Rheb and releases it from the complex.
notes: Reported by a single laboratory and not independently replicated in vivo; the same group identified RNF152 as the E3 ligase for RagA.

mechanism: S6K1 phosphorylates IRS-1 on inhibitory serines, uncoupling it from INSR/PI3K and promoting its degradation — blunting PI3K–AKT output (negative feedback).
notes: Sites are human IRS-1 numbering: Ser307 corresponds to mouse Ser302 and Ser636/Ser639 to rat Ser632/Ser635. Human Ser312 (mouse Ser307) is phosphorylated by JNK and IKK rather than by S6K1. This feedback explains the rebound AKT activation seen on acute mTORC1 inhibition [500].

mechanism: RSK phosphorylates Raptor at Ser719/721/722, increasing mTORC1 kinase activity downstream of oncogenic Ras/MAPK independently of TSC2.
RSK phosphorylates TSC2 C-terminal Ser1798 (and in vitro Ser939/Thr1462), inhibiting GAP function; the route by which phorbol esters and activated Ras raise mTORC1.

Receptor autophosphorylation creates phosphotyrosine docking sites bound by the GRB2 SH2 domain (directly on EGFR; via SHC or IRS-1 for the insulin and IGF-1 receptors), bringing the GRB2–SOS1 complex to the membrane.
Ligand-activated RTKs autophosphorylate; pYXXM sites (directly or via IRS/GAB adaptors) recruit p85–p110 to the membrane, activating class I PI3K.
notes: Receptor tyrosine kinase engagement activates PI3K [72,260,386]; RTK amplification converges on PI3K [375,624].

mechanism: SOS1 catalyses GDP→GTP exchange on membrane-anchored Ras; Ras·GTP then engages RAF and the p110α Ras-binding domain.
One TBC1D7 subunit bridges the TSC1 coiled-coils in the 2:2:1 TSC1-TSC2-TBC1D7 assembly, which is the form that carries Rheb-GAP activity.

TBC1D7 binding to the TSC1 coiled-coil stabilises the TSC1-TSC2 association that presents the Rheb-GAP domain; its depletion weakens that association and reduces Rheb-GAP activity, raising mTORC1 signalling, without lowering TSC2 levels or altering TSC2 localisation to the lysosome.

TNF-alpha engagement of TNFR1 activates the IKK complex, including IKK-beta, through the receptor-proximal adaptors TRADD, TRAF2 and TAK1; the relationship is indirect rather than a direct contact between TNF-alpha and IKK-beta.
TCTP was proposed as a Rheb guanine-nucleotide exchange factor in Drosophila; subsequent biochemical studies found no GEF activity.
notes: Rheb's high intrinsic GTP loading makes a guanine-nucleotide exchange factor dispensable, and TSC2 GAP activity is treated as the sole regulator of its nucleotide state. Graded contested because the original Drosophila report is directly contradicted by later biochemistry.

mechanism: TSC1 binding blocks HERC1-mediated ubiquitination of TSC2, stabilising tuberin; TSC2 protein is unstable without hamartin.
Two TSC1 (hamartin) copies form the coiled-coil scaffold of the 2:2:1 arch-shaped TSC1–TSC2–TBC1D7 complex.
TSC2 GAP domain accelerates Rheb GTP hydrolysis ~100-fold via an asparagine-thumb mechanism, converting Rheb·GTP to inactive Rheb·GDP; Rheb has no established GEF.
notes: GAP polarity: TSC2 is the GAP (negative regulator); loss of TSC1/TSC2 gives constitutive Rheb·GTP and mTORC1 activation.

mechanism: Two TSC2 (tuberin) copies supply the Rheb-GAP domains presented at the apex of the arch.

The TSC1–TSC2–TBC1D7 complex (2:2:1) presents the TSC2 GAP domain at its apex to lysosomal Rheb and accelerates GTP hydrolysis ~100-fold; in the absence of insulin the complex is held on the lysosome through Rheb and is released when AKT phosphorylates TSC2.
notes: The complex is the GAP and inactivates Rheb; loss of TSC1 or TSC2 leaves Rheb GTP-loaded and mTORC1 constitutively active. Lysosomal retention of the complex and its insulin-dependent release were shown by Menon and colleagues.

mechanism: AKT1 E17K in the PH domain increases PIP3-independent membrane association and constitutive Thr308/Ser473 phosphorylation.
notes: AKT1 gain-of-function belongs to the distal-network lesions, without a specific primary citation.

mechanism: Somatic mosaic activating AKT3 variants confined to malformed cortex drive mTORC1 hyperactivation causing hemimegalencephaly / focal cortical dysplasia type II.
Loss of neurofibromin removes Ras-GAP activity, raising Ras·GTP and MAPK/RSK input to TSC2 and Raptor.
notes: Neurofibromin is a Ras-GAP; its loss raises Ras-GTP and increases ERK and RSK input to the TSC complex and Raptor.

mechanism: Helical-domain mutations escape p85 nSH2 inhibition; kinase-domain H1047R increases membrane binding; both raise PIP3 and AKT–mTORC1 flux (distal-network lesion).
context: breast (30–40%), endometrial (30%) cancer; somatic mosaic in FCD II/HME
notes: A distal-network lesion: mTORC1 is only one effector among several, so this is a poor predictor of rapalog benefit (BOLERO-2 benefit was independent of PIK3CA genotype).

mechanism: PTEN loss removes PIP3 hydrolysis and raises AKT activity; it is a frequent distal-network lesion in prostate, glioblastoma and endometrial cancer.
notes: The commonly quoted prevalence figures for PTEN loss require a primary epidemiological source before they are restated.

mechanism: Receptor tyrosine kinase gene amplification increases ligand-dependent and -independent PI3K recruitment; distal-network lesion converging on PI3K.
Biallelic truncating TBC1D7 variants destabilise the TSC complex and increase mTORC1 activity, causing macrocephaly/megalencephaly with intellectual disability.
notes: Two independent families

mechanism: TSC1 loss destabilises TSC2 and abolishes Rheb-GAP activity → constitutive mTORC1 activation; basis of tuberous sclerosis; proximal-brake lesion predicting rapalog sensitivity.
context: tuberous sclerosis; urothelial carcinoma exceptional responders

mechanism: TSC2 loss abolishes the asparagine-thumb GAP activity toward Rheb → constitutive mTORC1 activation; basis of TSC, LAM and PEComa (AMPECT response enriched in TSC2-mutant tumours).
notes: AMPECT enrichment [633].

mechanism: Canonical Wnt signalling (Dishevelled/LRP6–Axin) inhibits GSK3, preventing TSC2 Ser1337/1341 phosphorylation and thereby activating mTORC1 independently of β-catenin.
pThr246-PRAS40 binds 14-3-3, which displaces PRAS40 from Raptor/mTORC1 and so derepresses substrate access.
notes: Binding requires prior AKT phosphorylation of Thr246; inhibiting PRAS40 in this way amounts to net activation of mTORC1.

mechanism: 14-3-3 binds AKT-phosphorylated TSC2 at Ser939 and Thr1462, with Ser981 and the MK2-generated site Ser1210 also contributing, and partitions TSC2 into the cytosol away from the membrane compartment where it acts on Rheb; whether TSC1-TSC2 association is lost or the intact complex is displaced from the lysosomal surface remains unresolved.
notes: REDD1 has been reported to displace 14-3-3 from TSC2 under hypoxia, but direct displacement remains disputed.

mechanism: A-769662 binds the ADaM site between the alpha kinase domain and beta1 carbohydrate-binding module, allosterically activating AMPK and protecting pThr172; beta1-selective, no AMP mimicry.
notes: Prototype of ADaM-site activators (MK-8722, PF-739).

mechanism: ADP binds the AMPK gamma-subunit nucleotide sites and protects phospho-Thr172 from dephosphorylation without causing allosteric activation.
notes: Several laboratories have reproduced ADP protection of Thr172, but ADP is about ten-fold less potent than AMP. Whether ADP also promotes Thr172 phosphorylation, and whether it contributes substantially to AMPK activation in vivo, is disputed.

mechanism: AICAR is taken up and phosphorylated to ZMP, an AMP mimetic that binds the AMPK gamma subunit, allosterically activating AMPK and promoting Thr172 phosphorylation; has AMPK-independent effects.

sites: Ser487 (human AMPK alpha1; Ser485 in rat)
mechanism: AKT phosphorylates the AMPK alpha1 ST-loop at human Ser487, reducing subsequent Thr172 phosphorylation by upstream kinases.
notes: Human alpha2 Ser491 is not assigned to AKT: Hawley et al. found alpha2 autophosphorylation at that site.

mechanism: FBP-unoccupied aldolase alters v-ATPase-Ragulator conformation, permitting AXIN-LKB1 docking and lysosomal AMPK Thr172 phosphorylation without an AMP rise; FBP-bound aldolase blocks the assembly.
notes: The sensed ligand is fructose-1,6-bisphosphate; the signal starts when it dissociates from aldolase as glucose falls. Reported mainly by one laboratory, which later showed that TRPV channels relay the aldolase signal (Li et al. 2019).

mechanism: Uncharged tRNAs accumulating during amino-acid deprivation bind the GCN2 HisRS-like domain, relieving autoinhibition and activating the kinase.
AMP binds CBS sites 1 and 3 of the gamma subunit, allosterically activating AMPK (2-5 fold), promoting Thr172 phosphorylation by LKB1 and protecting pThr172 from phosphatases.

Activated AMPK inhibits mTORC1 by two routes: phosphorylation of TSC2, which enhances its GAP activity toward Rheb, and direct phosphorylation of Raptor at Ser722 and Ser792, which creates 14-3-3 binding sites and imposes a metabolic checkpoint.
notes: Net effect of the TSC2 and Raptor phosphorylation routes rather than a separate molecular event.

mechanism: During acute energetic stress AMPK phosphorylates mTOR and Rictor within mTORC2, increasing mTORC2 activity toward AKT Ser473 and promoting cell survival, independently of its inhibition of mTORC1.
notes: Single-laboratory study. In vitro, AMPK phosphorylated mTOR at Ser1261 and Rictor at unmapped sites, but Ser1261 was not required for AMPK-induced mTORC2 signalling, so the functionally relevant sites are unknown.

mechanism: AMPK directly phosphorylates Raptor at two conserved serines, creating 14-3-3 binding sites that reduce mTORC1 kinase activity; imposes a metabolic checkpoint (G2/M arrest) independent of TSC2.
notes: Both Raptor sites, including Ser792, are needed for the full checkpoint.

mechanism: Glucose deprivation-activated AMPK phosphorylates p53 Ser15, initiating a p53-dependent metabolic checkpoint (cell-cycle arrest) and transcription of sestrins, REDD1, PTEN and TSC2 that feed back on mTORC1.

Under energy stress AMPK phosphorylates TSC2 at Thr1271 and Ser1387, enhancing its GAP activity toward Rheb and lowering Rheb-GTP; this is required for energy-stress inhibition of mTORC1 and protects cells from apoptosis during energy deprivation.
notes: Standard human TSC2 numbering (1807 residues); Inoki et al. 2003 [262] reported these residues as Thr1227 and Ser1345. AMPK phosphorylation at Ser1387 primes GSK3 phosphorylation at Ser1383 and Ser1379 (Ser1341 and Ser1337 in the Inoki numbering).

mechanism: AMPK associates with ULK1 in a nutrient-dependent manner; the association is required for AMPK-mediated activating phosphorylation of ULK1 and is disrupted when mTORC1 phosphorylates ULK1 at Ser757 (mouse numbering; Ser758 in human ULK1).
notes: Phosphorylation at Ser757 acts by disrupting the ULK1-AMPK interaction.

mechanism: Under glucose starvation AMPK binds and phosphorylates ULK1 at multiple sites, activating it to initiate autophagy/mitophagy; this is prevented when mTORC1 phosphorylates ULK1 Ser757.
notes: Ser317/Ser777 from Kim 2011 [309]; Egan 2011 [157] additionally mapped Ser467, Ser555, Thr574 and Ser637.

mechanism: ATF4, induced through eIF2alpha phosphorylation, is necessary and sufficient for transcriptional induction of REDD1 (DDIT4) during ER stress, and together with C/EBP-beta drives REDD1 expression during oxidative stress; REDD1 then suppresses mTORC1 through TSC2.

ATF4 induces SESN2 transcription downstream of GCN2 during amino-acid deprivation and during ER stress; the induced Sestrin2 is required to sustain mTORC1 repression by keeping mTORC1 off the lysosome.

Indirect relay: ROS-activated cytoplasmic ATM acts through LKB1 to increase AMPK Thr172 phosphorylation, and AMPK then phosphorylates TSC2, represses mTORC1 and induces autophagy; the response is lost in ATM-deficient cells, and no direct phosphorylation of AMPK by ATM has been shown.
notes: Reported by one laboratory; the proposed ATM-LKB1 step is phosphorylation of LKB1 at Thr366.

mechanism: ATM phosphorylates LKB1 at Thr366 (Thr363 in mouse) in response to ionising radiation and oxidative stress; the modification does not change LKB1 catalytic activity in vitro, but a non-phosphorylatable LKB1 mutant failed to restore ROS-induced mTORC1 repression in LKB1-deficient cells.
notes: Two laboratories have reported ATM phosphorylation of Thr366, but its requirement for mTORC1 repression rests on a single study.

mechanism: ATM phosphorylates p53 Ser15 (and CHK2, which phosphorylates Ser20), weakening MDM2 binding and stabilising/activating p53 after DNA damage.
Mg-free ATP competes with AMP/ADP for the gamma-subunit CBS sites; at high energy charge ATP occupancy keeps AMPK in the inactive, phosphatase-accessible state.

AMP binding to the AMPK gamma subunit drives AXIN to tether LKB1 to AMPK, and under glucose starvation the AXIN-LKB1-AMPK complex docks on the lysosomal v-ATPase-Ragulator, allowing LKB1 to phosphorylate AMPK Thr172.
notes: AXIN1 is a scaffold and does not itself phosphorylate Thr172. Evidence comes mainly from one laboratory.

mechanism: Under low energy, AMP-bound AMPK, AXIN and LKB1 assemble into a complex in which AXIN tethers LKB1 to AMPK, enhancing Thr172 phosphorylation; AXIN knockdown in mouse liver impairs AMPK activation after starvation.
Hypoxia-induced BNIP3 binds Rheb directly and lowers Rheb-GTP levels in a manner requiring its N-terminal domain, contributing to mTORC1 inhibition in hypoxia.
notes: Reported by one group; mechanism of Rheb nucleotide change not fully defined.

mechanism: MO25-alpha (or MO25-beta) is the scaffold subunit of the LKB1 heterotrimer.
MO25-alpha binds the STRADA C-terminal WEF motif and the LKB1 kinase domain, stabilising the heterotrimer and increasing LKB1 activity about 10-fold beyond STRADA alone.
Ca2+/calmodulin binding relieves CaMKK2 autoinhibition, enabling it to phosphorylate AMPK (and CaMKI/IV).

Reduced energy intake lowers cellular energy charge and insulin, reported to increase AMPK activity in liver and muscle, converging with metformin and exercise on the AMPK-TSC2/Raptor brake on mTORC1.
context: liver, skeletal muscle; rodent CR regimens
notes: Caloric restriction is held to converge on AMPK, but direct in vivo evidence of AMPK activation by caloric restriction is inconsistent across tissues and protocols.

mechanism: CaMKK-beta phosphorylates AMPK Thr172 in response to rises in cytosolic Ca2+ (e.g. ionophores, hormones), independently of LKB1 and without a change in AMP:ATP.
REDD1-dependent mTORC1 inhibition requires TSC2 in the cited models. This functional relationship does not establish direct REDD1 binding to 14-3-3 or direct stimulation of TSC2 catalysis.
Direct REDD1 binding to 14-3-3 and displacement of TSC2 were proposed, but a subsequent structural and biochemical study did not detect REDD1-14-3-3 binding.
notes: The direct binding mechanism is disputed; this does not negate REDD1-dependent suppression of mTORC1.

mechanism: DNA double-strand breaks recruit MRN, which activates ATM by intermolecular autophosphorylation (Ser1981) and dimer dissociation.

Genotoxic stress activates ATM/ATR and CHK2, which phosphorylate p53 at Ser15 and Ser20, weakening MDM2 binding and stabilising p53; p53 then induces mTORC1-suppressing target genes, including SESN1 and SESN2.
notes: support comes from the primary p53 literature.

mechanism: In normoxia PHD2 hydroxylates HIF-1α at Pro402 and Pro564 using O2 as co-substrate, creating the pVHL-binding degron; the reaction rate is limited by oxygen tension, which is what makes HIF-1α an oxygen sensor.
notes: Pro402 and Pro564 lie in two independent oxygen-dependent degradation domains, each of which recruits pVHL once hydroxylated; PHD1 and PHD3 can hydroxylate the same residues.

mechanism: PERK phosphorylates eIF2alpha Ser51, trapping eIF2B and reducing ternary-complex formation; global initiation falls while ATF4 translation rises.
GCN2 phosphorylates eIF2alpha Ser51 during amino-acid starvation, reducing global translation initiation and inducing ATF4, which transcribes SESN2 to sustain mTORC1 suppression.
Phospho-eIF2alpha lowers ternary-complex availability; delayed reinitiation after uORF1 bypasses the inhibitory uORF2 so the ATF4 coding sequence is translated (integrated stress response).
notes: Phosphorylation of eIF2alpha (an inhibitory event for eIF2) paradoxically increases ATF4 output.

mechanism: When ATP consumption exceeds production, adenylate kinase (2 ADP <-> ATP + AMP) amplifies the AMP rise so AMP:ATP changes roughly as the square of ADP:ATP, making AMP the sensitive low-energy signal.
Energy stress (rising AMP/ADP:ATP) activates AMPK through gamma-subunit nucleotide binding and LKB1-dependent Thr172 phosphorylation; AMPK then inhibits mTORC1 via TSC2 and Raptor.
Energy stress (2-deoxyglucose, glucose deprivation) induces REDD1 through ATF4; REDD1 is required for mTORC1 inhibition in this setting, partly independently of AMPK.
Unfolded-protein load releases BiP/GRP78 from the PERK luminal domain; PERK dimerises and autophosphorylates, launching the integrated stress response.
Contractile activity raises AMP/ADP:ATP and creatine/phosphocreatine turnover in muscle fibres, increasing LKB1-dependent AMPK Thr172 phosphorylation in an intensity-dependent manner.

Muscle contraction consumes ATP faster than oxidative phosphorylation replenishes it, so ADP and, through adenylate kinase, AMP rise, and this energy-stress state activates AMPK in proportion to exercise intensity.
notes: Exercise converges on AMPK through the contraction-induced shift in adenylate charge.

mechanism: FBP occupancy of aldolase prevents the apo-aldolase conformation; on glucose withdrawal FBP falls, apo-aldolase forms and nucleates the lysosomal v-ATPase–Ragulator–AXIN–LKB1 platform that activates AMPK before any measurable change in the AMP:ATP ratio.
Glycolytic flux converts glucose to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate, so FBP concentration tracks glucose availability and serves as the proximal signal in the aldolase-dependent glucose-sensing route.

Glucose sufficiency is relayed to mTORC1 through the Rag GTPases largely independently of AMPK (constitutively active RagA mice lose glucose sensing); glycolytic DHAP has been proposed as the sensed metabolite.
notes: The direct glucose/DHAP sensor upstream of the Rags is unknown.

mechanism: Withdrawal of glucose activates AMPK through LKB1-dependent phosphorylation of Thr172: the canonical route follows the fall in ATP and the rise in AMP and ADP, while a parallel route in which unoccupied aldolase senses the loss of fructose-1,6-bisphosphate has been reported to act before adenine nucleotide ratios change.
notes: The aldolase route is reported by a single laboratory, whereas activation of AMPK by glucose withdrawal itself is reproduced widely.

mechanism: Glucose withdrawal suppresses mTORC1 even in AMPK-null cells, so an AMPK-independent arm operates in parallel with the LKB1-AMPK route; the proposed effectors, Rag-GTPase-dependent release of mTORC1 from the lysosome and hexokinase-II binding to Raptor, each rest on a single report.
notes: The existence of an AMPK-independent arm is well supported; the molecular identity of that arm is not.

mechanism: Glucose withdrawal shifts the Rag heterodimer to its inactive nucleotide state, releasing mTORC1 from the lysosomal surface; mice expressing GTP-locked RagA cannot execute this switch and die of neonatal glucose-starvation failure.
notes: The in vivo genetic evidence comes from mice expressing GTP-locked RagA, which cannot inactivate the heterodimer and die of neonatal starvation.

mechanism: The carbohydrate-binding module of the AMPK β-subunit binds glycogen, and branched glycogen with exposed α-1,6 branch points inhibits AMPK activity and Thr172 phosphorylation, so cellular carbohydrate reserves restrain the energy-stress arm independently of the AMP:ATP ratio.
notes: Glycogen reserves restrain AMPK independently of the AMP:ATP ratio, which is why glycogen depletion is a determinant of AMPK activation during exercise.

mechanism: After AMPK priming at Ser1345, GSK3 phosphorylates TSC2 Ser1341/Ser1337, further activating TSC2; Wnt inhibits GSK3 and thereby relieves TSC2 to activate mTORC1, integrating Wnt and energy signals.
notes: GSK3 phosphorylation requires prior AMPK phosphorylation of TSC2 at Ser1345. The numbering follows the original report; the same residues are Ser1379, Ser1383 and the priming site Ser1387 in the 1807-residue human sequence.

mechanism: HIF-1 binds a hypoxia-response element in the BNIP3 promoter, strongly inducing BNIP3 under hypoxia (mitophagy, Rheb binding).
HIF-1 binds hypoxia-response elements in the REDD1/RTP801 (DDIT4) promoter, rapidly inducing REDD1 mRNA and protein under hypoxia.

During glucose deprivation hexokinase-II, lacking bound glucose-6-phosphate, binds Raptor through a TOS-like motif and inhibits mTORC1, promoting protective autophagy; G6P binding prevents the interaction.
notes: Single primary study; HK2 is itself an mTORC1/HIF-1 output (feedback).

mechanism: Limited oxidative phosphorylation lowers ATP and raises AMP/ADP, activating LKB1-AMPK, which phosphorylates TSC2 and Raptor; a REDD1-independent arm of hypoxic mTORC1 inhibition.
notes: the REDD1-TSC route acts without AMPK or LKB1. Mitochondrial ROS have also been proposed to activate AMPK in hypoxia independently of the AMP:ATP ratio.

mechanism: Hypoxia induces REDD1 (via HIF-1 and, under severe hypoxia/ER stress, ATF4); REDD1 is required for hypoxic mTORC1 inhibition, which is lost in REDD1-/- and TSC2-/- cells.

Falling O2 tension limits the prolyl-hydroxylase reaction, inactivating PHD2 and allowing HIF-1α to escape hydroxylation and degradation; this is the molecular basis of the HIF-1α stabilisation that drives REDD1 and BNIP3 induction.
Low O2 blocks PHD-mediated prolyl hydroxylation of HIF-1alpha; VHL no longer binds, ubiquitination ceases and HIF-1alpha accumulates to drive hypoxia-responsive genes including DDIT4 and BNIP3.
notes: HIF-1alpha is itself a translational output of mTORC1, so hypoxic signalling through HIF-1alpha closes a feedback loop onto the pathway.

mechanism: Hypoxia suppresses mTORC1 by two indirect routes: HIF-1alpha-dependent induction of REDD1 with consequent TSC activation, which proceeds without AMPK or LKB1, and, when hypoxia is severe enough to lower ATP, activation of AMPK.
notes: A summary of two indirect routes rather than a direct interaction.

mechanism: IKK-beta phosphorylates and suppresses TSC1, disinhibiting Rheb and therefore raising mTORC1 activity; this is one plausible molecular link between chronic inflammation and the anabolic dysregulation of ageing tissue.
notes: Rests on a single laboratory's work (Lee DF et al., Cell 2007;130:440-455); the TSC1 Ser487/Ser511 assignment has not been independently replicated.

mechanism: IKK-beta phosphorylates TSC1 Ser487/Ser511, suppressing TSC1 and the TSC complex so Rheb-GTP and mTORC1 activity rise; links inflammation to tumour angiogenesis and anabolic dysregulation.
notes: The Ser487/Ser511 assignment derives from a single laboratory (Lee DF et al., Cell 2007;130:440-455) and has not been independently replicated at site level.

mechanism: The constitutively active LKB1–STRADα–MO25 heterotrimer is the upstream kinase that phosphorylates the AMPK activation loop at Thr172; STRADα and MO25 are required for LKB1 catalytic competence and cytoplasmic localisation.
notes: The LKB1-STRADalpha-MO25 heterotrimer is the physiological AMPK kinase; STRADalpha and MO25 are required for LKB1 catalytic competence and cytoplasmic localisation.

mechanism: Metformin activates AMPK indirectly: inhibition of mitochondrial complex I raises AMP and ADP relative to ATP, and at low, clinically relevant concentrations a lysosomal route through PEN2, the v-ATPase, AXIN and LKB1 has been reported by a single laboratory. LKB1 is required for the hepatic effect.
notes: Metformin also inhibits mTORC1 independently of AMPK, through the Rag GTPases and through p53-REDD1.

mechanism: Metformin accumulates in mitochondria and mildly inhibits complex I (NADH dehydrogenase), lowering ATP production and raising AMP/ADP:ATP, the proximal trigger for AMPK activation.
Low-dose metformin binds PEN2, which then engages ATP6AP1 to inhibit v-ATPase, triggering AXIN-LKB1 recruitment to Ragulator and lysosomal AMPK activation without a change in AMP:ATP.
notes: Recent single-group discovery; independent replication limited.

mechanism: Metformin inhibits mTORC1 independently of AMPK and TSC2 in a Rag GTPase-dependent manner; constitutively active Rag mutants blunt the effect, suggesting interference with Rag-mediated lysosomal recruitment.
notes: the Rag step is inferred from constitutively active Rag mutants rather than demonstrated directly.

mechanism: Complex I oxidises NADH and pumps protons, sustaining the proton-motive force that ATP synthase uses, so complex I activity is required for maximal oxidative ATP production rather than converting a substrate into ATP. Biguanide inhibition of complex I therefore lowers ATP and raises AMP and ADP, the classical high-dose route to AMPK activation.
mTORC1 phosphorylates AMPK alpha2 Ser345 (Raptor-dependent) under nutrient stress, suppressing AMPK activity and promoting proliferation: a reciprocal brake opposing AMPK inhibition of mTORC1.
notes: Single-laboratory finding awaiting independent replication; a reciprocal brake opposing AMPK inhibition of mTORC1.

mechanism: In nutrient sufficiency mTORC1 phosphorylates ULK1 at Ser757 (mouse numbering; human Ser758), disrupting the ULK1-AMPK interaction and preventing AMPK-mediated activating phosphorylation at Ser317, Ser555 and Ser777; AMPK and mTORC1 therefore toggle autophagy initiation.
H2O2/mitochondrial ROS increase AMPK Thr172 phosphorylation; proposed direct oxidation of AMPK alpha Cys299/Cys304 versus indirect activation through ATP depletion and AMP/ADP rise.
notes: Direct redox activation at AMPK alpha Cys299/Cys304 is disputed; the opposing account holds that mitochondria-derived reactive oxygen species act indirectly through the cellular energy state.

mechanism: H2O2 oxidises ATM Cys2991, forming disulfide-linked active dimers independently of DNA breaks and MRN; this cytoplasmic ATM pool drives the LKB1-AMPK-TSC2 response to ROS.
ROS act on a peroxisome-localised TSC1-TSC2 pool, activating TSC2 GAP activity to suppress Rheb-GTP and mTORC1 and to induce autophagy (pexophagy).

Metformin-bound PEN2 binds the v-ATPase accessory subunit ATP6AP1 and inhibits the lysosomal v-ATPase, triggering AXIN–LKB1-dependent activation of lysosomal AMPK at clinically relevant metformin concentrations and without a fall in cellular ATP.
notes: Completes the low-dose metformin route from PEN2 through v-ATPase inhibition to lysosomal AMPK activation; reported by a single laboratory (Ma T et al., Nature 2022;603:159-165).

mechanism: PEX5, the peroxisomal targeting-signal receptor, binds TSC2 and localises a pool of the TSC complex to the peroxisome, where it suppresses Rheb in response to reactive oxygen species; TSC1 is recognised by the partner receptor PEX19.
notes: Pathogenic TSC2 mutations reduce PEX5 binding and abolish peroxisomal localisation, Rheb-GAP activity and reactive-oxygen-species-dependent suppression of mTORC1; reported by a single laboratory.

mechanism: PP2C-family phosphatases dephosphorylate AMPK Thr172 and switch the kinase off; AMP, and roughly ten-fold less potently ADP, binds the gamma-subunit CBS sites and protects Thr172 from dephosphorylation. This protection is distinct from the direct allosteric activation of the already phosphorylated kinase and is the main route by which a falling energy charge sustains AMPK activity.
notes: Graded emerging because protection from dephosphorylation is established for the PP2C class while the physiological phosphatase isoform (PPM1A, PPM1B, PPM1E or PPM1F) remains unresolved.

mechanism: Scaffolding beta subunit (beta1 or beta2) bridging alpha and gamma; its C-terminus binds both, its CBM binds glycogen and contributes to the ADaM drug site.

Regulatory gamma subunit (gamma1/2/3) whose four tandem CBS motifs form two Bateman domains with three occupied adenine-nucleotide sites: one holds AMP almost permanently, two exchange AMP, ADP and ATP, and one site remains unoccupied, conferring energy sensing on the heterotrimer.

Under glucose starvation v-ATPase-Ragulator recruits AXIN-LKB1 to the lysosomal surface next to lysosomal AMPK; AXIN simultaneously blocks Ragulator GEF activity toward RagA/B, releasing mTORC1 from the lysosome.

Resistance exercise and mechanical overload activate mTORC1 in skeletal muscle, and rapamycin blocks the contraction-induced rise in human muscle protein synthesis. The proximal mechanism involves a rise in phosphatidic acid together with membrane perturbation and focal-adhesion signalling, but the enzyme generating that phosphatidic acid is disputed, with early work implicating phospholipase D and later work diacylglycerol kinase zeta.
notes: The net activation of mTORC1 by loading is reproducible while the proximal lipid step is unsettled; opposite in sign to the endurance-exercise input to AMPK, so exercise modality determines the net effect.

mechanism: Sestrin1, like sestrin2, promotes AMPK activation and downstream TSC2 phosphorylation, forming the p53-dependent feedback loop that suppresses mTORC1 after genotoxic stress.
notes: Whether AMPK mediates the effect of Sestrin1 on mTORC1 is disputed; later work places sestrin action primarily through GATOR2 and the Rag GTPases.

mechanism: Sestrin1/2 were reported to bind AMPK (and TSC2) and promote AMPK-mediated TSC2 phosphorylation, mediating p53-dependent mTORC1 inhibition after genotoxic stress.
notes: Later work (Chantranupong 2014, Peng 2014 Cell) shows sestrins inhibit mTORC1 primarily through GATOR2 and the Rag GTPases, independently of AMPK; the physiological contribution of the AMPK route is disputed.

mechanism: LKB1 (with STRADA/MO25) phosphorylates the AMPK alpha activation-loop Thr172; AMP bound to the gamma subunit makes AMPK a better substrate and protects pThr172, so net phosphorylation rises with AMP/ATP.
notes: LKB1 is constitutively active; regulation is at the substrate (AMPK) level.

mechanism: LKB1 is the catalytic subunit of the LKB1-STRADA-MO25 heterotrimer, the constitutively active upstream kinase of AMPK.
STRAD-alpha (or STRAD-beta) is the pseudokinase subunit of the LKB1 heterotrimer required for its activity and cytoplasmic localisation.

The pseudokinase STRAD-alpha binds the LKB1 kinase domain and, together with MO25, stabilises the catalytically active conformation and anchors LKB1 in the cytoplasm where AMPK is phosphorylated; STRAD-alpha alone gives only partial activation.
notes: Reported activation of LKB1 refers to the LKB1-STRADalpha-MO25 heterotrimer rather than to STRADalpha binding alone.

mechanism: p53 (and p63) bind the DDIT4/REDD1 promoter and induce it after DNA damage; REDD1 then releases TSC2 from 14-3-3 to suppress mTORC1.
p53 transcriptionally induces the AMPK β1 regulatory subunit, raising AMPK heterotrimer abundance as part of the same transcriptional programme that induces sestrins, TSC2 and PTEN.
notes: The AMPK-subunit arm of the p53 transcriptional programme; induction is stress-, cell-type- and tissue-specific rather than general.

mechanism: p53 binds a PTEN promoter element and induces PTEN; higher PTEN lowers PIP3-AKT, relieving AKT inhibition of TSC2 and reducing mTORC1 as one arm of the coordinated p53-mTOR response.
p53 binds response elements in SESN1 (PA26) and induces it after DNA damage; Sestrin1 contributes to p53-dependent mTORC1 suppression via GATOR2 binding and AMPK.
notes: SESN1 (PA26) carries a functional p53-responsive element and is induced by genotoxic stress in a p53-dependent manner.

mechanism: p53 induces SESN2 (Hi95) after genotoxic stress; Sestrin2 then inhibits mTORC1, principally by sequestering GATOR2, linking DNA damage to growth arrest.
notes: Induction by DNA damage is p53-dependent, whereas induction by prolonged hypoxia or oxidative stress is largely p53-independent.

mechanism: p53 transcriptionally induces TSC2 in a stress-, cell-type- and tissue-specific manner, raising Rheb-GAP capacity and reinforcing mTORC1 suppression after genotoxic stress.
context: DNA damage; mouse tissues and cell lines
notes: Induction is conditional rather than general; the dominant p53 route to mTORC1 runs through sestrins and AMPK. Induction of the AMPK beta1 subunit is documented in the same studies.

mechanism: ULK1 phosphorylates all three AMPK subunits (several Ser/Thr sites on alpha1, beta2, gamma1), reducing AMPK activity: a negative feedback loop terminating the autophagy-inducing signal.
notes: Single primary study with limited independent replication.

mechanism: Loss-of-function STK11/LKB1 lesions abolish energy-stress-induced Thr172 phosphorylation of AMPK, removing both the TSC2-GAP and the Raptor Ser792 brakes, so mTORC1 is no longer restrained when ATP falls; Ca2+-driven Thr172 phosphorylation by CaMKK2 is retained, and growth-factor and amino-acid control of mTORC1 persists.
notes: A single-arm trial of everolimus in advanced solid tumours selected for TSC1, TSC2, NF1, NF2 or STK11 mutations showed no meaningful single-agent activity, so such a lesion marks an enriched population rather than demonstrated dependence on the kinase.

mechanism: Germline (Peutz-Jeghers) or somatic STK11 inactivation abolishes AMPK Thr172 phosphorylation under energy stress; the TSC2/Raptor checkpoints fail and mTORC1 is deregulated in LKB1-null cells and tumours.

Autosomal recessive STRADA loss causes polyhydramnios, megalencephaly and symptomatic (intractable) epilepsy through impaired LKB1-AMPK signalling and mTORC1 hyperactivation; rapamycin reduces seizures.
notes: Rapamycin efficacy in PMSE rests on preclinical work together with small clinical studies.

mechanism: Biallelic STRADA loss removes the pseudokinase subunit required for LKB1 activity and cytoplasmic localisation, so the LKB1–STRADα–MO25 heterotrimer cannot assemble and LKB1–AMPK signalling is impaired.
notes: Impaired LKB1-AMPK signalling is the complex-level consequence of losing the pseudokinase subunit.

mechanism: Loss of LKB1-AMPK restraint in STRADA-null neurons produces constitutive mTORC1 hyperactivity, the shared mechanism of the mTORopathies; rapamycin rescues aberrant cortical lamination and heterotopia in STRADA-depleted preclinical models, and the human experience is a small open-label series reporting reduced seizure frequency.
notes: Evidence for benefit in affected patients is preclinical together with a small uncontrolled series, not a controlled trial.

mechanism: Biallelic STRADA (LYK5) deletion removes the LKB1 pseudokinase activator; LKB1 is mislocalised/inactive, AMPK Thr172 phosphorylation falls and neuronal mTORC1 becomes hyperactive.

pVHL, the substrate-recognition subunit of a CUL2–elongin BC E3 ligase, binds prolyl-hydroxylated HIF-1α and polyubiquitinates it for proteasomal degradation; VHL loss in clear-cell renal carcinoma produces constitutive HIF signalling.
notes: The normoxic degradation arm, relieved by hypoxia and by inhibition of the prolyl hydroxylases; VHL loss in clear-cell renal carcinoma produces constitutive HIF signalling.

mechanism: 14-3-3 docks onto AMPK-phosphorylated Raptor (pSer722/pSer792), suppressing mTORC1 activity toward S6K1/4E-BP1 under energy stress.
notes: 14-3-3 binding was tested by mutating Ser722 and Ser792 together, and the 14-3-3-motif epitope depended mainly on Ser722.

mechanism: AKT phosphorylates PRAS40 at Thr246, releasing it from Raptor and derepressing mTORC1 - the feed-forward arm of growth-factor input, parallel to AKT inactivation of TSC2.
