AKT phosphorylates mSin1 at Thr86, which one laboratory found to enhance mTORC2 activity toward AKT Ser473 and so create positive feedback. Another laboratory found that Thr86 and Thr398 phosphorylation, triggered by S6K or AKT depending on cell context, dissociates mSin1 from mTORC2 and suppresses its activity.
notes: The sign of Thr86 phosphorylation is unresolved between the two laboratories. The 2015 study identified AKT, not S6K, as the main Thr86 kinase in every cell line tested.

mechanism: Akt phosphorylates mTOR on Ser2448 downstream of PI3K; the site is a widely used activity biomarker but its functional consequence is disputed, and S6K1 phosphorylates the same residue, so the kinase assignment itself is contested.
Structural work on the Rheb-bound complex shows PRAS40 occupying the substrate path, lowering mTORC1 output in the basal, growth-factor-deprived state.
PRAS40 is a substoichiometric mTORC1 subunit, associating through Raptor rather than contributing structurally to the dimer.
PRAS40 presents its own TOS motif to the Raptor substrate pocket and competes with S6K1 and 4E-BP1 for access, acting as a direct inhibitor of substrate binding.
AMPK phosphorylates Raptor at Ser722/Ser792, directly inhibiting mTORC1 in parallel with its action on TSC2 and imposing a metabolic checkpoint.
SCF-betaTrCP binds the phosphorylated DEPTOR degron and polyubiquitinates it, committing the inhibitory subunit to proteasomal degradation.
beta-TrCP1 is the F-box substrate-receptor subunit of the SCF ligase that destroys DEPTOR.
Cdc37 binds the N-terminal nucleotide-binding domain of Hsp90, holds its lid open and inserts an arginine into the ATP pocket. This arrests the ATPase cycle while a client kinase is loaded.

The mSin1 CRIM domain is a ubiquitin-like fold whose acidic loop binds AGC-kinase substrates at a site distal to the catalytic cleft; the basic surface of the AKT kinase N-lobe engages this loop about 75 Å from the mTOR active site. CRIM-dependent recruitment also applies to SGK and PKC, although different AGC kinases differ in their sensitivity to perturbation of mSin1.
The CRIM domain is the central substrate-recruitment module of mSin1.
Cullin-1 is the scaffold of the SCF(beta-TrCP) ligase.
DEPTOR engages the FAT region of mTOR through its PDZ domain, suppressing kinase output toward substrates of both complexes.
DEPTOR binding restrains mTORC1; its loss raises S6K1 and 4E-BP1 phosphorylation, and its overexpression in myeloma suppresses mTORC1 while relieving feedback onto PI3K-AKT.
DEPTOR associates substoichiometrically with mTORC1 as an inhibitory subunit.
DEPTOR is a substoichiometric inhibitory subunit of mTORC2 as well as of mTORC1.

ETV7 is reported to interact with mTOR in the cytoplasm and to assemble a putative third complex, mTORC3, that lacks core mTORC1 and mTORC2 subunits and keeps mTOR activity in the presence of rapamycin. Tumour cells that lose this complex become rapamycin-sensitive.
notes: Reported by a single laboratory and not widely replicated; mTORC3 remains an emerging concept.

mechanism: The ETS repressor ETV7 is reported to nucleate the putative third complex and to confer rapamycin insensitivity on it.
notes: Not independently replicated.

mechanism: The C-terminal FATC motif is integral to the kinase domain and packs against the activation loop and the mLST8-binding element. Deleting the conserved C-terminal residues, or substituting a conserved tryptophan within them, nearly abolishes mTOR kinase activity.
Extreme C-terminal FATC domain, the last structural element of mTOR, packing against the catalytic core.

The FAT clamp holds the kinase domain in a partially closed, low-activity conformation by distorting the active site; hyperactivating cancer mutations cluster at this FAT-kinase interface and Rheb binding relieves the restraint.
The FAT (FRAP-ATM-TRRAP) alpha-helical domain wraps around the kinase domain and is a defining feature of the PIKK family.
beta-TrCP2 (FBXW11) is redundant with BTRC as the receptor for the DEPTOR phosphodegron.

FKBP12, a peptidyl-prolyl isomerase, is the intracellular receptor for rapamycin and contributes one half of the composite surface that binds FRB. Inhibition of mTOR is a gain of function of the drug-immunophilin complex, not a consequence of blocking isomerase activity.

The composite FKBP12-rapamycin surface wedges into the FRB domain adjacent to the catalytic cleft, narrowing substrate access; this gain-of-function mechanism explains why rapamycin is an allosteric, substrate-selective inhibitor rather than an ATP-competitive one.
The FKBP12-rapamycin binary complex engages the four-helix FRB bundle, forming the ternary complex resolved crystallographically.

FRB sits at the entrance of the deep catalytic cleft and acts as a gatekeeper: its rapamycin-binding surface contacts substrates and gives them access to the recessed active site. FKBP12-rapamycin bound at FRB therefore restricts substrate access without occupying the ATP site.
The ~100-residue four-helix FRB bundle lies between the FAT and kinase domains of the mTOR polypeptide and forms the drug-binding surface.
During ER stress, GSK-3beta phosphorylates Rictor at Ser1235, which interferes with binding of AKT to mTORC2 and lowers AKT Ser473 phosphorylation.
notes: Single-laboratory report. Ser1235 is distinct from Thr1135, the Rictor site phosphorylated by S6K1.

mechanism: The N-terminal HEAT repeats, arranged as N-HEAT (horn) and M-HEAT (bridge) segments, fold into an elongated alpha-solenoid. The solenoid contributes to the dimer interface and provides the docking surface for Raptor in mTORC1 and Rictor in mTORC2.
notes: Domain-level decomposition of mTOR

mechanism: Hsp90 acts with TTT/R2TP in maturing newly synthesised mTOR; Hsp90 inhibition destabilises mTOR and reduces mTORC1 signalling.
notes: Second external ref removed: journal/volume did not match the claim (the geldanamycin/mTOR-raptor paper is Ohji et al. 2006, J Biochem 139:129-135, not BBRC 340:1125).

mechanism: PI3K-like catalytic domain carrying the ATP site in a deeply recessed cleft; it is the catalytic unit shared by mTORC1, mTORC2 and the putative mTORC3.
The basic surface of the Akt kinase N-lobe engages an acidic loop of the mSin1 CRIM domain ~75 A from the catalytic site; specificity is structural, not local sequence around Ser473.
notes: Primary support is a single 2025 structural study; the widely repeated 'tri-arginine cluster' formulation should be treated with caution.

mechanism: mSin1 is a defining mTORC2 subunit; its N-terminal segment binds Rictor and it is required for complex integrity and kinase activity toward Akt.
Sin1-dependent recruitment delivers PKC isoforms to mTORC2; mSin1 interface changes shift the balance of AGC substrates phosphorylated.
The N-terminal region of mSin1 binds Rictor; the interface maintains complex integrity and its subtle variation modulates which AGC kinase is preferred.
The mSin1 CRIM domain recruits AGC-kinase substrates generally; different AGC kinases are differentially sensitive to perturbation of mSin1.
mLST8 docks onto the LBE (mLST8-binding element) of the kinase domain, adjacent to the active site, in both mTORC1 and mTORC2.
The mLST8 WD40 beta-propeller docks on the kinase domain near the activation loop and stabilises the catalytic conformation.
mLST8 is present at two copies per mTORC1 dimer, its WD40 propeller abutting the kinase domain near the activation loop.
mLST8 deletion phenocopies Rictor rather than Raptor loss: mTORC2 signalling to Akt-FOXO and PKCalpha fails while S6K1 signalling is preserved.
mLST8 is a stoichiometric mTORC2 subunit contacting the kinase domain; unlike in mTORC1 its loss abolishes complex function.
mTOR self-associates through the N-terminal HEAT repeat region, producing the obligate head-to-head dimer seen in both mTORC1 and mTORC2 cryo-EM reconstructions.
notes: Self-loop representing homodimerisation of the catalytic subunit.

mechanism: mTOR autophosphorylates Ser2481 in the C-terminal region adjacent to FATC; the mark reports intrinsic catalytic activity of assembled mTORC1 and mTORC2 rather than driving it.
Two mTOR protomers form the catalytic core of the ~1.1 MDa mTORC1 homodimer, facing one another across a dimer interface with the kinase domains at the obtuse vertices.
mTOR supplies the catalytic subunit of the ~1.0 MDa mTORC2 homodimer, resolved by cryo-EM at 3.2 A.
mTOR is reported to form an ETV7-containing assembly lacking Raptor and Rictor that retains activity in the presence of rapamycin.
notes: Single-laboratory description; the existence and composition of mTORC3 remain contested.

mechanism: mTOR phosphorylates Raptor at Ser863 within the complex, a rapamycin-sensitive intracomplex event that primes further multisite phosphorylation and supports mTORC1 activity.

Active mTOR phosphorylates DEPTOR in the linker between its DEP and PDZ domains. This primes the degron for CK1alpha and marks DEPTOR for betaTrCP-dependent degradation, so active mTOR removes its own brake.
notes: Zhao et al. 2011 attributed degron phosphorylation to S6K1 and RSK1 rather than to mTOR directly.

mechanism: Ribosome-associated mTORC2 phosphorylates the turn motif of nascent AKT cotranslationally, which is required for folding and stability of the newly synthesised polypeptide.
notes: This cotranslational activity is a defining output of the ribosome-associated mTORC2 pool.

mechanism: mTORC2 is the hydrophobic-motif kinase for Akt: phosphorylation of Ser473 completes activation-loop-dependent activation and sets Akt substrate selectivity (notably toward FOXO).
notes: AKT phosphorylated only at Thr308 retains substantial activity toward GSK3beta and TSC2, whereas Ser473 phosphorylation markedly enhances activity toward FOXO1, FOXO3a and BAD.

mechanism: DEPTOR is phosphorylated by mTORC2 as well as mTORC1, which likewise promotes its degradation and relieves inhibition of the complex.
mTORC2 supports PKC maturation by priming selected isoforms; subsequent hydrophobic-motif phosphorylation can be autophosphorylation.
In the basal state the mSin1 PH domain folds back onto the mTOR kinase domain and suppresses catalysis; this is the autoinhibited resting conformation of mTORC2.
notes: The mSin1 PH domain is not resolved in published mTORC2 cryo-EM maps, so the autoinhibited conformation rests on biochemical and mutational evidence [360].

mechanism: C-terminal PH domain of mSin1, the PIP3-binding and autoinhibitory element.
The C-terminal PH domain of mSin1 binds PIP3, which releases the PH domain from mTOR and derepresses the kinase.
notes: PIP3-dependent relief of mSin1 autoinhibition is reproduced across laboratories.

mechanism: PIP3 binding by mSin1 simultaneously relieves autoinhibition and recruits mTORC2 to the plasma membrane, co-localising it with membrane-targeted AKT.

PtdIns(3,4,5)P3 generated by PI3K binds the mSin1 PH domain and pulls it off the kinase domain, relieving autoinhibition and simultaneously anchoring mTORC2 at the plasma membrane where Akt is recruited.
Protor-1 joins mTORC2 substoichiometrically through Rictor; it is accessory rather than required for assembly.
Protor-1 was identified as a Rictor-binding protein and enters mTORC2 through that contact rather than through mTOR.
Protor-1 knockout mice show reduced mTORC2-dependent SGK1 activation and NDRG1 phosphorylation in kidney, with AKT signalling preserved.
notes: Protor-1 loss leaves AKT and PKCalpha hydrophobic- and turn-motif phosphorylation intact, so the requirement is restricted to SGK1 and has been shown only in kidney.

mechanism: Protor-2, the PRR5 paralogue, associates substoichiometrically with mTORC2 via Rictor.

Protor-2 (PRR5L), the paralogue of Protor-1, binds Rictor and thereby associates with mTORC2 without being required for complex integrity or kinase activity; a binding site shared with Protor-1 and strictly exclusive binding of the two paralogues have not been mapped.
Rag-mediated docking tethers mTORC1 to the lysosomal surface where Rheb-GTP is available; without it the complex remains diffusely cytosolic and cannot be activated.
RagA/B-GTP with RagC/D-GDP binds Raptor directly; the reciprocal nucleotide configuration releases it. The Rag-Raptor contact is a docking point, not an allosteric activator.

4E-BP1 contains an N-terminal RAIP motif (Arg-Ala-Ile-Pro) that, together with the C-terminal TOS motif, is required for efficient mTORC1-dependent multisite phosphorylation; NMR places its contact on Raptor at a site separate from the TOS pocket.
notes: Whether the RAIP motif contacts Raptor directly is disputed: Beugnet et al. 2003 (J Biol Chem 278:40717-40722) found that the RAIP-containing N-terminal fragment of 4E-BP1 does not bind Raptor.

mechanism: NMR shows that the N-terminal RAIP motif of 4E-BP1 binds Raptor at a site separate from the TOS-binding pocket, so that the two motifs tether 4E-BP1 by avidity and orient its phosphoacceptor region toward the kinase site; mutation of either motif abolishes Raptor co-immunoprecipitation of 4E-BP1.
notes: Beugnet et al. 2003 (J Biol Chem 278:40717-40722) found no Raptor binding by the RAIP-containing N-terminal fragment and concluded that RAIP promotes phosphorylation independently of Raptor binding; a direct RAIP-mTOR contact has not been demonstrated.

mechanism: Rapamycin has no direct activity on mTOR; it first binds the immunophilin FKBP12 and the binary complex is the active species. The yeast FPR1 screen established this genetically.
Rapamycin is the drug half of the composite inhibitor; neither partner alone binds FRB with meaningful affinity.

GTP-bound H-Ras and K-Ras (predominantly KRAS4A) bind the atypical Ras-binding domain of mSin1. Oncogenic Ras was reported to promote mTORC2 activity at the plasma membrane, but a Sin1 mutant unable to bind Ras supports normal mTORC2 assembly and activity in cells and mice, and Sin1 overexpression was reported to suppress Ras signalling.
notes: The consequence of Ras binding for mTORC2 activity is disputed between laboratories. The Ras-binding domain is one of the defined mSin1 regions, but no function has been firmly assigned to it.

mechanism: mSin1 contains a Raf-like, atypical Ras-binding domain between its CRIM and PH domains that binds GTP-loaded H-Ras and K-Ras.

GTP-loaded Rheb binds the N-terminal portions of the N-HEAT, M-HEAT and FAT domains about 60 Å from the kinase active site; the resulting movement twists the FAT clamp and realigns the DFG motif and alphaC helix into a catalytically competent active site.

Rheb-GTP binds across the mTOR N-HEAT, M-HEAT and FAT regions rather than at the catalytic cleft and activates the kinase allosterically [672]; earlier biochemical mapping localised the interaction to the kinase region [364].
Rheb-GTP binding realigns the N-HEAT, FAT and kinase domains, correcting the misaligned active site; this allosteric step is the proximate activation of lysosomal mTORC1.
A minor subset of mTORC2 associates with ribosomes; the association is PI3K- and growth-factor-responsive and constitutes an activating input to the complex.
The Akt kinase C-lobe engages an N-terminal mooring formed jointly by mSin1 and Rictor, completing the distal docking surface that selects the substrate.
notes: Supported by a single structural study using semisynthetic trapping probes [597]; not yet independently reproduced.

mechanism: In the assembled mTORC2 cryo-EM structures Rictor packs against the FRB bundle, sterically denying access to the FKBP12-rapamycin complex.

Rictor binds the mTOR N-HEAT solenoid and is required for mTORC2 assembly and integrity; with mSin1 it occludes the FRB domain and forms the N-terminal mooring that docks the AKT C-lobe, whereas the mSin1 CRIM domain provides the principal substrate-docking surface.
Rictor is the defining stoichiometric subunit of mTORC2, binding the mTOR solenoid and bridging to mSin1.

Rictor, with mSin1, occupies a surface on the mTOR N-HEAT solenoid that overlaps the Raptor footprint, so Raptor and Rictor binding to mTOR are mutually exclusive and the two complexes partition a common mTOR pool.

S6K1, together with RSK1, was reported to phosphorylate the DEPTOR betaTrCP degron (Ser286, Ser287, Ser291) after growth-factor stimulation, promoting SCF-betaTrCP-dependent DEPTOR degradation. Another laboratory found that S6K inhibition or knockdown does not change DEPTOR turnover and attributed degron phosphorylation to mTOR and CK1alpha.
notes: Opposing evidence: Gao et al. 2011, Mol Cell 44:290-303 (PMID 22017875).

mechanism: S6K1 phosphorylates mSin1 at Thr86 and Thr398, impairing mTORC2 complex integrity and suppressing downstream AKT signalling.
notes: Yang et al. 2015 (Cell Rep 12:937-943; PMID 26235620) reported that AKT-mediated phosphorylation of mSin1 Thr86 enhances mTORC2 activity, the opposite sign at the same residue.

mechanism: S6K1 phosphorylates mTOR at Ser2448 in the negative regulatory domain; the site is a convenient activity marker but has no demonstrated effect on catalysis.
notes: Established as a phosphorylation event; its functional consequence for mTOR activity is not established.

mechanism: mTORC1-activated S6K1 directly phosphorylates Rictor at Thr1135, creating a 14-3-3 binding site without altering mTORC2 assembly or in vitro kinase activity. Two studies found that a T1135A mutant raises AKT Ser473 phosphorylation, indicating feedback inhibition, whereas two others saw no major change in mTORC2 activity or AKT phosphorylation.
notes: Boulbès et al. 2010 [53] detected Thr1135 phosphorylation in mTORC2-deficient cells, suggesting that it may also regulate functions of Rictor outside mTORC2.

mechanism: PRAS40 carries a bona fide TOS motif read by the same Raptor pocket as substrate TOS motifs, which is why it behaves as a competitive rather than allosteric inhibitor.

Raptor binds the C-terminal TOS motif of 4E-BP1 and, according to NMR data, the N-terminal RAIP motif at a separate site, tethering 4E-BP1 so that its phosphoacceptor region is presented to the mTOR active site.
notes: A direct RAIP-Raptor contact is disputed: Beugnet et al. 2003 (J Biol Chem 278:40717-40722) found no Raptor binding by the RAIP-containing N-terminal fragment of 4E-BP1.

mechanism: HIF-1alpha carries a TOS motif recognised by Raptor, coupling mTORC1 directly to hypoxia-responsive transcription.
notes: The HIF-1alpha TOS motif and its Raptor binding were characterised by a single laboratory (Land and Tee 2007).

mechanism: Raptor wraps the N-HEAT solenoid and projects a substrate-recognition surface outward; because the mTOR cleft is deep and partially occluded, recruitment by Raptor is obligatory, not incidental.
Raptor is the defining stoichiometric subunit of mTORC1, two copies per dimer, wrapped around the N-HEAT solenoid of each mTOR protomer.
Raptor recognises the S6K1 TOR signalling motif, consensus Phe-Asp/Glu-Phi-Asp/Glu-Phi, and this binding is required for mTORC1 to phosphorylate the kinase.
Raptor binds ULK1 in a nutrient-dependent manner, incorporating mTORC1 into the ULK1-ATG13-FIP200 complex and presenting ULK1 for inhibitory phosphorylation at Ser758 (Ser757 in mouse).
notes: manual override: Raptor binds the ULK1 TOS motif to present ULK1 for inhibitory Ser757 phosphorylation by mTORC1; the net effect of the Raptor-ULK1 interaction on ULK1 activity is inhibitory, so a positive sign would mislead sign-aware path queries.

mechanism: RSK1, activated downstream of ERK, was reported to phosphorylate the DEPTOR betaTrCP degron after growth-factor stimulation, promoting DEPTOR degradation and relieving mTOR inhibition.
notes: RSK1 involvement rests on a single study; other work assigns degron phosphorylation to mTOR and CK1alpha.

mechanism: RSK phosphorylates Raptor at an activating serine cluster downstream of oncogenic MAPK signalling, raising mTORC1 output independently of TSC.
notes: Ser722 is also an AMPK target; the effect depends on the kinase and phosphorylation context.

mechanism: Energy-replete conditions drive TTT-RUVBL1/2 assembly, which promotes mTORC1 dimerisation and lysosomal localisation; energy stress dissociates the module and the dimer, coupling nutrient state to the oligomeric state of the complex.

mTOR phosphorylates DEPTOR at Ser293 and Ser299 (and Thr295), priming CK1alpha to phosphorylate the Ser286/Ser287/Ser291 degron, which SCF(beta-TrCP) binds, polyubiquitinates and sends for proteasomal degradation. Active mTOR thereby removes its own inhibitor in a positive-feedback loop.
notes: Ser293 and Ser299 are mTOR priming sites outside the beta-TrCP degron. One study attributes degron phosphorylation instead to S6K1 and RSK1.

mechanism: SKP1 adapts the F-box protein beta-TrCP to the CUL1 scaffold.
Tel2 binds Tti1 (and Tti2) to form the TTT module; loss of any subunit destabilises the others and lowers the steady-state level of all PIKKs including mTOR.

Tel2 binds the Tti1-Tti2 subcomplex through a conserved surface patch to form the TTT co-chaperone, which works with Hsp90 on newly synthesised PIKKs, including mTOR, to support their assembly into functional complexes.

PRAS40 carries its own TOS motif (FVMDE, Phe129), which is required for Raptor binding and lets PRAS40 occupy the Raptor substrate-docking site in competition with S6K1 and 4E-BP1. PRAS40 is also itself an mTORC1 substrate at Ser183.
4E-BP1 carries a C-terminal TOS motif (FEMDI) required for Raptor binding and for efficient multisite phosphorylation by mTORC1.
HIF-1alpha is reported to carry an N-terminal TOS motif (Phe99) through which it binds Raptor. Mutating this motif impairs hypoxic HIF activity and p300/CBP binding.
notes: The HIF-1alpha TOS motif has been studied by one research group only, and mTORC1 also raises HIF-1alpha through 4E-BP1- and S6K1-dependent translation.

mechanism: S6K1 carries an N-terminal TOS motif (FDIDL) that is necessary for Raptor binding and for Thr389 phosphorylation.

Raptor recognises the five-residue TOS motif of its clients; point mutation of the motif's phenylalanine abolishes binding to Raptor and mTORC1-dependent phosphorylation, which is the molecular basis of substrate selection by mTORC1.
Tti1 binds Tel2 and Tti2 to form the TTT module and, with Tel2, is required for mTOR stability and for assembly of mTORC1 and mTORC2.
loss of any one subunit destabilises the others.
The TTT module binds nascent mTOR and, with R2TP/Hsp90, supports its folding; TTT depletion lowers mTOR protein and collapses signalling through both complexes.

Knockdown of Tti1 or Tel2 disassembles mTORC1 and mTORC2 as well as lowering mTOR levels, and Tel2 with Hsp90 is required to incorporate newly made mTOR into both complexes. This indicates a role in complex assembly beyond protein stabilisation.
The same TTT-dependent assembly requirement applies to mTORC2, whose integrity falls on Tti1-Tel2 depletion.
ULK1 phosphorylates Raptor strongly at Ser855 and Ser859 and moderately at Ser792, which hinders 4E-BP1 docking on Raptor and lowers mTORC1 output toward S6K1 and 4E-BP1.
notes: The rise in Raptor Ser863 phosphorylation after ULK1 overexpression is mTORC1-dependent, so Ser863 is not a direct ULK1 site.

mechanism: TFIIIB (Brf1-containing) recruits Pol III to TFIIIC-bound tRNA and 5S genes and is the main target of growth-regulated Pol III control.
SCF-betaTrCP recognises the phospho-Ser67 degron of PDCD4 and ubiquitinates it for proteasomal degradation after growth-factor stimulation.
mTORC1-dependent translation is selective (structured-5'UTR and TOP mRNAs) rather than global, so mTORC1 inhibition only partly reduces bulk protein synthesis.
mTORC1-driven translation of IL1A and MAPKAPK2 mRNAs is required for the senescence-associated secretory phenotype; rapamycin suppresses SASP without clearing senescent cells.
Cyclin D1 partners CDK4/6 to phosphorylate RB and drive the G1/S transition, linking eIF4F-dependent cyclin D1 translation to cell-cycle entry.
eEF2 catalyses GTP-dependent ribosomal translocation; relief of eEF2K by S6K1 therefore increases elongation rate.
eEF2K phosphorylates eEF2 at Thr56 in the GTP-binding domain, preventing eEF2 from binding the ribosome and halting translocation.
Inactive S6K1 is bound to eIF3; Thr389 phosphorylation by eIF3-recruited mTORC1 releases S6K1 to phosphorylate rpS6 and eIF4B at the preinitiation complex.
eIF4A is the DEAD-box helicase subunit of eIF4F that unwinds 5'UTR secondary structure for 43S scanning.
Ser422-phosphorylated eIF4B shows increased association with eIF3, integrating it into the 43S preinitiation complex.
eIF4B is a cofactor that stimulates eIF4A ATPase and RNA-helicase activity, promoting unwinding of structured 5' untranslated regions during scanning.

eIF4B stimulates eIF4A helicase activity on structured 5'UTRs. Its depletion selectively reduces translation of c-Myc mRNA, together with other structured-5'UTR mRNAs such as Cdc25C, ODC, Bcl-2 and XIAP.
notes: S6K1-eIF4B-dependent control of c-Myc translation and glutamine metabolism was reported in a study that has since been retracted (Csibi et al. 2014, Curr Biol).

mechanism: Binding to eIF4E protects hypophosphorylated 4E-BP1 from ubiquitination by the KLHL25-CUL3 ligase. When eIF4E is depleted, hypophosphorylated 4E-BP1 is degraded while hyperphosphorylated 4E-BP1 is spared, so 4E-BP1 levels track eIF4E abundance.
eIF4E binds the m7G cap and nucleates eIF4F assembly by recruiting eIF4G.

eIF4E recruits the eIF4G scaffold through the canonical YXXXXLΦ eIF4E-binding motif, nucleating eIF4F assembly on the cap. The 4E-BPs carry the same motif and engage the same dorsal surface of eIF4E, so their binding excludes eIF4G.

Released eIF4E drives the proliferative translational programme (cyclin D1, c-Myc, Mcl-1); eIF4E overexpression is transforming in vivo and the proliferative output of mTORC1 is specifically 4E-BP/eIF4E-dependent rather than S6K-dependent.

Hypophosphorylated 4E-BP1 binds the dorsal surface of eIF4E through the canonical YXXXXLΦ motif shared with eIF4G and through a secondary site, sequestering eIF4E from eIF4F. Multisite phosphorylation releases eIF4E; in the paralogue 4E-BP2, phosphorylation of Thr37 and Thr46 folds the protein into a β-domain that buries this motif.
4E-BP1 and eIF4G share the eIF4E-binding motif, so 4E-BP1 binding to eIF4E is mutually exclusive with eIF4G and blocks eIF4F assembly on the cap.
4E-BPs mediate mTORC1 control of proliferation but not cell size: 4E-BP1/2-null cells are resistant to the antiproliferative effect of mTORC1 inhibition.
Ribosome profiling attributes TOP mRNA sensitivity to mTORC1 largely to 4E-BPs, whereas LARP1 studies show 4E-BP-independent repression; both arms likely contribute.
notes: Relative contribution of 4E-BP versus LARP1 to TOP repression remains debated.

mechanism: 4E-BP2, the predominant brain 4E-BP, restrains eIF4F formation; its loss enhances LTP, impairs memory and produces autism-like behaviour via excess eIF4E-dependent translation.
Assembled eIF4F recruits the 43S complex to capped mRNAs; its availability is rate-limiting for cap-dependent initiation.
Cyclin D1 mRNA has a structured 5'UTR whose translation is preferentially sensitive to eIF4E availability and 4E-BP status.

Release of eIF4E from the 4E-BPs downstream of mTORC1 increases eIF4F-dependent translation of HIF-1α mRNA. This raises expression of the HIF-1 glycolytic targets GLUT1, hexokinase 2, PFKFB3, PKM2 and LDHA.
mTORC1 promotes survival through 4E-BP/eIF4E-dependent translation of Mcl-1 mRNA.
c-Myc mRNA (structured 5'UTR) is translated in an eIF4F/eIF4A-dependent manner downstream of mTORC1-4E-BP signalling.
VEGF mRNA translation is eIF4E-sensitive, linking the 4E-BP arm to angiogenesis.
eIF4G-eIF3 interaction bridges cap-bound eIF4F to the 43S preinitiation complex; insulin stimulates this association in an mTOR-dependent manner.
eIF4G is the eIF4F scaffold binding eIF4E, eIF4A, eIF3, PABP and MNK.
MNK docks on the C-terminus of eIF4G to phosphorylate eIF4E; 4E-BP sequestration of eIF4E therefore also prevents Ser209 phosphorylation.
ERK phosphorylates TIF-IA at Ser633, required for Pol I transcription and cell growth; an mTORC1-independent input to rRNA synthesis.

ERK1/2 phosphorylates UBF at Thr117 and Thr201 within HMG boxes 1 and 2, which prevents these boxes from binding DNA and alters UBF-induced rDNA architecture. This mediates the immediate activation of Pol I transcription by growth factors such as EGF.

TFIIIC bound to the internal promoter recruits TFIIIB (BRF1-TBP-BDP1) to the upstream region, and TFIIIB in turn loads Pol III. tRNA genes use a type 2 A-box/B-box promoter, whereas 5S rRNA genes use a type 1 promoter at which TFIIIC binding also requires TFIIIA.

The C-terminal DM15 region of LARP1 binds the m7G cap and the adjacent 5'TOP pyrimidine tract at the same time. This occludes the cap from eIF4E and excludes eIF4F from TOP mRNAs when mTORC1 is inactive.
Cap occupancy by LARP1 sterically excludes eIF4E/eIF4F from TOP mRNAs.
LARP1 associates with PABP and poly(A) tails, linking 3' and 5' ends of TOP mRNAs and contributing to their stability and mTORC1-responsive translation.

LARP1 represses TOP mRNAs, which encode the ribosomal proteins and several elongation factors, and so indirectly limits the protein arm of ribosome biogenesis. Relief of this repression on mTORC1 activation lets ribosomal-protein supply scale with the Pol I rRNA and Pol III tRNA and 5S arms.
When mTORC1 is inactive, the LARP1 DM15 domain binds the m7G cap and adjacent 5'TOP motif, repressing translation of ribosomal-protein and elongation-factor mRNAs.
Independently of translational repression, LARP1 (with 40S subunits) protects TOP mRNAs from decay; LARP1 depletion lowers TOP mRNA abundance.
notes: Dual repressor/stabiliser role of LARP1.

mechanism: MAF1 binds the TFIIIB subunit BRF1 and inhibits de novo assembly of TFIIIB-DNA complexes on Pol III promoters, which impairs Pol III recruitment.
notes: Direct Maf1-Brf1 co-immunoprecipitation was shown in yeast. In mammalian cells, MAF1 associates with TFIIIB and Pol III and represses transcription through BRF1 and BRF2.

mechanism: Mammalian MAF1 also represses Pol I transcription, at least partly indirectly, by repressing transcription of TBP, the TATA-binding protein that Pol I initiation complexes require. No direct contact between MAF1 and Pol I has been shown.
Dephosphorylated MAF1 binds the Pol III clamp, rearranging the enzyme to prevent TFIIIB-dependent recruitment and closed-complex formation on tRNA and 5S promoters.
ERK/p38-activated MNK1/2 phosphorylate eIF4E Ser209; dispensable for global translation but promotes tumorigenesis and translation of select mRNAs.
mTOR associates with TFIIIC and is detected at tRNA and 5S rRNA genes, positioning it to target the repressor MAF1 at Pol III promoters.
notes: Chromatin association shown by one laboratory; MAF1 phosphorylation itself is established.

mechanism: Chromatin immunoprecipitation detects a nuclear pool of mTOR at rDNA and tRNA gene promoters, in a manner that depends on growth signals and is sensitive to rapamycin. This suggests chromatin-level control of Pol I and Pol III transcription, but a direct contact between mTOR and the polymerase has not been shown.
notes: Single-laboratory ChIP finding.

mechanism: Through 4E-BP phosphorylation and the S6K1-eIF4B/PDCD4/eEF2K axis, mTORC1 stimulates cap-dependent initiation and elongation. The effect is selective rather than global, and the most mTORC1-sensitive mRNAs, mainly TOP and TOP-like transcripts, depend chiefly on the 4E-BPs.
Rapamycin-sensitive phosphorylation of eEF2K at Ser78 (adjacent to the calmodulin-binding site) impairs calmodulin binding and eEF2K activity; direct kinase not definitively identified.
notes: Site is mTOR-dependent; whether mTORC1 phosphorylates it directly is unresolved.

mechanism: Growth factors and nutrients recruit mTOR-Raptor to the eIF3 preinitiation complex, where mTORC1 phosphorylates S6K1 and 4E-BP1 through dynamic protein interchange.
mTORC1 first phosphorylates priming sites Thr37/Thr46; these are largely rapamycin-resistant, which is the structural reason rapalogs incompletely suppress cap-dependent translation.
notes: Priming step of the hierarchical mechanism.

mechanism: After Thr37/46 priming, mTORC1 phosphorylates Thr70 then Ser65 in a TOS-dependent, rapamycin-sensitive manner, lowering eIF4E affinity by orders of magnitude and releasing eIF4E.
notes: Ser65 phosphorylation additionally requires Ser101 (Wang 2003).

mechanism: mTORC1 phosphorylates 4E-BP2 at Thr37, Thr46, Ser65 and Thr70, the residues equivalent to the 4E-BP1 sites, in a rapamycin-sensitive manner that releases eIF4E. Loss of both 4E-BP1 and 4E-BP2 makes TOP and TOP-like mRNA translation resistant to mTOR inhibition.
Serum-stimulated, rapamycin-sensitive phosphorylation of the eIF4GI C-terminal region; direct kinase and functional consequence not firmly established.
notes: mTOR-dependent but may be indirect.

mechanism: mTORC1 phosphorylates a C-terminal cluster of LARP1 sites adjacent to the DM15 region, weakening cap/TOP binding and releasing TOP mRNAs for eIF4F-dependent translation.
notes: mTORC1 phosphorylates at least 26 rapamycin-sensitive serine and threonine residues on LARP1, arranged in seven clusters. The cluster next to the DM15 region is the most rapamycin-sensitive.

mechanism: mTORC1 directly phosphorylates the Pol III repressor MAF1 at Ser60/68/75 in a rapamycin-sensitive manner, inactivating it and derepressing tRNA and 5S rRNA transcription.
mTORC1 coordinates Pol I (TIF-IA/UBF), Pol III (MAF1) and Pol II/TOP-mRNA (LARP1) outputs so that rRNA, tRNA and ribosomal-protein pools scale together.
mTOR phosphorylates the S6K1 turn motif at Ser371 in vitro. Ser371 phosphorylation is required for Thr389 phosphorylation and for intrinsic kinase activity.
notes: In cells, GSK3 also phosphorylates Ser371, and mTOR maintains phosphorylation of this site partly by restraining its dephosphorylation.

mechanism: Raptor-TOS-recruited S6K1 is phosphorylated by mTORC1 on hydrophobic-motif Thr389, creating the docking site that permits PDK1 activation-loop phosphorylation.
notes: Thr389 phosphorylation is fully rapamycin-sensitive.

mechanism: mTORC1 drives rapamycin-sensitive phosphorylation of Thr388 in the S6K2 hydrophobic motif, the equivalent of S6K1 Thr389. A phosphomimetic Thr388Glu substitution makes S6K2 fully active and resistant to rapamycin.
c-Myc binds TFIIIB through BRF1 and is recruited to tRNA and 5S rRNA genes, directly activating Pol III transcription independently of its Pol II target genes.
c-Myc, itself translated in a 4E-BP/eIF4B-dependent manner, transcriptionally induces ribosomal-protein genes, Pol I/III cofactors (UBF, TIF-IA, Brf1) and rRNA processing factors.
Poly(A)-binding protein bound to the 3' poly(A) tail binds the N-terminal region of eIF4G. This circularises the mRNA and stimulates 43S recruitment and cap-dependent initiation.
PDCD4 MA3 domains bind eIF4A, blocking its helicase activity and its interaction with eIF4G, thereby suppressing translation of structured-5'UTR mRNAs.
The tandem MA3 domains of PDCD4 bind eIF4A at the surface that eIF4G uses. PDCD4 therefore both inhibits eIF4A helicase activity and prevents eIF4A from being incorporated into eIF4F through eIF4G.
notes: PDCD4 also binds the middle region of eIF4G (residues 635-1039) and prevents eIF4A from binding the eIF4G C-terminal region (residues 1040-1560).

mechanism: PDCD4 suppresses neoplastic transformation and inhibits eIF4A-dependent translation of mRNAs with structured 5'UTRs. Its S6K1- and βTrCP-dependent degradation after mitogenic stimulation is required for the full rise in protein synthesis and cell growth after mTORC1 activation, so its effect on proliferation is indirect.
After Thr389 priming, PDK1 phosphorylates the S6K1 activation loop at Thr229, completing kinase activation.
Pol I transcribes the rDNA repeats into the 47S pre-rRNA, the rate-limiting step of ribosome biogenesis coordinated by mTORC1.
Pol III transcribes 5S rRNA genes under MAF1/mTORC1 control, supplying the 60S subunit component.
Pol III transcribes tRNA genes; output rises when mTORC1 phosphorylates and inactivates MAF1.
PP2A associates with S6K1 and dephosphorylates it when mTORC1 is inhibited by rapamycin; mTORC1 activity restrains PP2A action on S6K1.
notes: Identity of the physiological S6K1 phosphatase remains debated (PP2A vs PHLPP).

mechanism: PP2A dephosphorylates the activating Ser44 site of TIF-IA/RRN3, reducing Pol I transcription; phosphatase inhibition attenuates rapamycin-induced Ser44 dephosphorylation.
notes: PP2A treatment inactivates TIF-IA in vitro, and calyculin A or okadaic acid prevents rapamycin-induced Ser44 dephosphorylation in cells. Because these inhibitors also act on PP1, PP2A is the most likely cellular phosphatase but not a proven one, and no phosphatase has been identified for Ser199.

mechanism: 47S pre-rRNA is processed into 18S, 5.8S and 28S rRNAs and assembled with ribosomal proteins in the nucleolus into 40S and 60S subunits.
Net protein accumulation from enhanced initiation, elongation and ribosome supply drives increase in cell mass.

Rapalogs suppress cap-dependent translation only partially. With FKBP12-rapamycin bound to the FRB domain, phosphorylation of 4E-BP1 at Ser65 and Thr70 is blocked while Thr37 and Thr46 remain largely phosphorylated, so eIF4F assembly continues at a substantial rate. The limitation is structural rather than a matter of dose.
notes: ATP-competitive and bi-steric inhibitors suppress cap-dependent translation far more completely.

mechanism: Rapamycin blocks phosphorylation of the late 4E-BP1 sites Ser65 and Thr70 while largely sparing the priming sites Thr37 and Thr46, so binding of 4E-BP1 to eIF4E is only partly restored and cap-dependent translation continues. The limitation is structural rather than a matter of dose.
notes: The degree of resistance varies with cell type, and 4E-BP1 phosphorylation can recover during prolonged exposure.

mechanism: Rapamycin lowers activating Ser44 phosphorylation of TIF-IA/RRN3 and raises the inhibitory Ser199 site, blocks the S6K1-dependent phosphorylation of the UBF carboxy-terminal activation domain, and relieves mTORC1 repression of MAF1 — collapsing Pol I 47S pre-rRNA synthesis and Pol III tRNA/5S output together.
notes: Rapamycin acts on both polymerase arms: phosphorylation of TIF-IA and of the UBF carboxy-terminal activation domain falls rapidly, while MAF1 escapes mTORC1-dependent inactivation and continues to repress RNA polymerase III.

mechanism: FKBP12-rapamycin bound to the mTORC1 FRB domain abolishes S6K1 Thr389 phosphorylation completely, in contrast to its partial effect on 4E-BP1. This makes Thr389 the pharmacodynamic marker of mTORC1 engagement and the readout against which partial pathway inhibition is judged in dosing studies.
Ribosome abundance sets translational capacity; mTORC1-driven ribosome biogenesis is therefore a prerequisite for sustained anabolic protein synthesis.
Coordinated rRNA transcription/processing, ribosomal-protein translation and nucleolar assembly produce mature 40S/60S subunits.

RMC-5552 tethers an FKBP12-rapamycin moiety to an ATP-site moiety; FKBP12-mediated avidity confers mTORC1 selectivity while the ATP-site moiety blocks catalysis. Phosphorylation of 4E-BP1 at all four sites, including the rapamycin-resistant priming sites Thr37 and Thr46, is therefore suppressed, and hypophosphorylated 4E-BP1 binds eIF4E. The activation of the repressor is indirect, through inhibition of mTORC1 kinase activity.
notes: Whether complete suppression of 4E-BP1 phosphorylation translates into genotype-dependent clinical benefit is not yet established.

mechanism: The bi-steric design tethers an FKBP12-rapamycin moiety to an ATP-site moiety; FKBP12-mediated avidity confers mTORC1 selectivity while the ATP-site moiety delivers complete catalytic inhibition, so both S6K1 Thr389 and 4E-BP1 are fully suppressed while mTORC2 is relatively spared.
notes: RMC-5552 suppresses both S6K1 and 4E-BP1 phosphorylation fully while relatively sparing mTORC2. The effect on S6K1 is indirect, through inhibition of mTORC1 kinase activity.

mechanism: rpS6 phosphorylation is a determinant of cell size: phospho-null rpS6 knock-in mice have smaller cells (notably beta-cells) and impaired glucose homeostasis.
rpS6 (eS6) is a 40S small-subunit ribosomal protein located near the mRNA/tRNA binding site.
S6K1 deletion yields small mice and cells; S6Ks control cell size (growth) whereas 4E-BPs control proliferation downstream of mTORC1.
S6K1 phosphorylates eEF2 kinase at Ser366, reducing its activity at physiological Ca2+ and thereby lowering eEF2 Thr56 phosphorylation and accelerating elongation.
S6K1 phosphorylates eIF4B at Ser422 in a rapamycin-sensitive manner, enhancing eIF4B recruitment to the preinitiation complex and eIF4A helicase stimulation on structured 5'UTRs.

S6K1 phosphorylates CBP80, the large subunit of the nuclear cap-binding complex, at residues that are also phosphorylated in cells in a growth-factor-dependent, rapamycin-sensitive manner, and S6K1 is found together with SKAR on CBP80-bound spliced mRNAs.
notes: The phosphorylated residues of CBP80 have not been mapped, and the consequence for cap binding and splicing remains undetermined.

mechanism: S6K1 phosphorylates PDCD4 at Ser67, creating a phosphodegron for betaTrCP-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, relieving eIF4A inhibition.

Phosphorylation of the S6K1 hydrophobic motif at Thr389 by mTORC1 creates a docking site for the PIF pocket of PDK1, which then phosphorylates the S6K1 activation loop at Thr229. The mTORC1 and PDK1 inputs to S6K1 are therefore sequential rather than independent.
notes: Thr389 lies in the hydrophobic motif of S6K1, the docking partner; PDK1 itself is not phosphorylated in this interaction.

mechanism: S6K activity controls a ribosome-biogenesis transcriptional programme (rRNA processing factors, Pol I/III cofactors) in addition to rDNA transcription.
notes: The mammalian evidence comes mainly from liver and cells lacking both S6K1 and S6K2, in which the feeding-induced ribosome-biogenesis transcriptional programme fails. The requirement for S6K1 in UBF-dependent rDNA transcription is a separate and better-supported arm.

mechanism: Active S6K1 phosphorylates 40S ribosomal protein S6 in ordered fashion (Ser236 first); phosphorylation influences cell size and glucose homeostasis.
notes: Ser247 is phosphorylated by CK1 after priming.

mechanism: The C-terminal autoinhibitory pseudosubstrate domain restrains S6K1; proline-directed phosphorylation (Ser411/Thr421/Ser424) relieves it, allowing Thr389/Thr229 phosphorylation.

S6K1, but not S6K2, binds SKAR and phosphorylates it at Ser383 and Ser385 in response to insulin and other mitogens, in a rapamycin-sensitive manner. Depletion of SKAR reduces cell size, but the functional consequence of these two phosphorylations has not been determined.

S6K1 activity is required for mTOR-dependent phosphorylation of the UBF carboxy-terminal activation domain, which enhances UBF binding to SL1 and Pol I transcription of rDNA. Rapamycin causes rapid dephosphorylation of this domain, and a constitutively active, rapamycin-resistant S6K1 reverses it. Direct phosphorylation of UBF by S6K1 has not been shown, so the relationship is S6K1-dependent rather than a proven kinase-substrate interaction.
notes: Rapamycin-sensitive; whether S6K1 phosphorylates UBF directly or via an intermediate kinase is not fully resolved.

mechanism: S6K2 phosphorylates rpS6 redundantly with S6K1 and is the principal rpS6 kinase in S6K1-null cells; residual Ser235/236 in double knockouts derives from RSK.
LARP1 co-purifies with Raptor/mTORC1; the interaction positions LARP1 for mTORC1-dependent phosphorylation and is sensitive to mTORC1 activity.
TIF-IA binds initiation-competent Pol I and bridges it to the SL1 promoter-selectivity factor at the rDNA promoter.

RRN3/TIF-IA binds both Pol I and the TAF1B subunit of promoter-bound SL1/TIF-IB, bridging initiation-competent polymerase to the rDNA promoter. This bridging step is the point at which the mTORC1 input on TIF-IA Ser44 is converted into pre-initiation complex formation.
5S rRNA is incorporated with RPL5/RPL11 into the 60S large subunit central protuberance.
p90RSK1 phosphorylates eEF2K at the same Ser366 site as S6K1, providing ERK-pathway control of elongation.
notes: Supported by the same primary paper as the S6K1 claim [636].

mechanism: RSK phosphorylates the same eIF4B Ser422 site as S6K1, so mTORC1 and Ras-ERK pathways converge on eIF4B.
Ras-ERK-activated RSK phosphorylates rpS6 at Ser235/236 independently of mTORC1, promoting cap-binding-complex assembly.
RSK phosphorylates TIF-IA at Ser649, cooperating with ERK Ser633 phosphorylation to activate Pol I transcription.
SKAR (Aly/REF-like) is deposited with the exon junction complex on newly spliced mRNAs.

SKAR recruits activated S6K1 to newly spliced messenger ribonucleoproteins carrying the exon junction complex, which was reported to raise the translation efficiency of spliced relative to unspliced transcripts.
notes: Reported by a single laboratory and not independently reproduced. The model of a distinct cap-binding-complex-dependent pioneer round of translation, on which the proposed mechanism rests, is itself debated.

mechanism: SL1/TIF-IB (TBP plus TAF1A/TAF1B/TAF1C) binds the rDNA core promoter and, together with UBF, nucleates the Pol I pre-initiation complex; no Pol I initiation occurs without it.
TOP mRNAs encode essentially all ribosomal proteins plus eEF1A, eEF2 and PABP; their mTORC1/LARP1-controlled translation scales ribosomal-protein supply with rRNA synthesis.

ATP-competitive occupancy of the mTOR kinase cleft suppresses the rapamycin-resistant 4E-BP1 Thr37/Thr46 sites, so 4E-BP1 remains eIF4E-bound, eIF4F does not assemble, and cap-dependent initiation is blocked far more completely than with rapamycin.

By occupying the ATP site of mTOR, Torin1 blocks phosphorylation of 4E-BP1 at all four sites, including the priming sites Thr37 and Thr46 that resist rapamycin, and cellular phosphatases then remove the existing phosphates. Hypophosphorylated 4E-BP1 sequesters eIF4E, so the activation of the repressor is indirect, through inhibition of the mTOR kinase.
notes: Complete suppression of 4E-BP1 phosphorylation requires catalytic-site rather than allosteric inhibition. Other ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitors act the same way, among them PP242, KU-0063794 and AZD8055; sapanisertib and vistusertib belong to the same class.

mechanism: ATP-competitive mTOR inhibition abolishes S6K1 Thr389 phosphorylation together with the rapamycin-resistant outputs of mTORC1, so mTORC1 signalling is suppressed completely rather than partially. The effect on S6K1 is indirect, through inhibition of the mTOR kinase.
tRNA supply, scaled with ribosome production via mTORC1-MAF1, is required for elongation capacity.
UBF binds the rDNA promoter and enhancer, recruits SL1 and stabilises Pol I preinitiation complexes; its activity is mTOR/S6K1-dependent.
Acetyl-CoA carboxylase 1 supplies malonyl-CoA, the rate-limiting substrate for fatty acid synthase.

AMBRA1 binds Beclin-1 and promotes the activity of the autophagy-specific class III PI3K complex I; it is a regulatory partner of the complex rather than one of its core subunits, which are VPS34, VPS15, Beclin-1 and ATG14L.
Released AMBRA1 recruits TRAF6 to catalyse K63-linked ULK1 ubiquitylation, promoting ULK1 self-association, stability and activity
notes: External reference not independently verified.

mechanism: Autophagy-derived amino acids reactivate mTORC1, so the autophagy-mTORC1 system oscillates rather than behaving as a switch
notes: Kinetic consequence: readouts of autophagic flux depend strongly on sampling time after an intervention.

mechanism: Energy-stress-activated AMPK phosphorylates ULK1 at activating sites, initiating autophagy and mitophagy; blocked when mTORC1 has marked Ser757
context: mouse ULK1 site numbering; energy-stress models
notes: Mouse Ser555 corresponds to human Ser556; mouse Ser777 is not conserved in human ULK1. The effect of AMPK on autophagy depends on stress and timing.

mechanism: mTORC1-driven ATF4 promotes glutathione synthesis alongside protein synthesis, coupling anabolic signalling to redox buffering
ATF4 induces the mitochondrial folate-cycle enzyme MTHFD2, the step through which mTORC1 couples one-carbon metabolism to purine supply
ATF4 (CREB2) drives SIRT4 transcription; mTORC1 represses SIRT4 indirectly by promoting proteasome-dependent degradation of ATF4.
notes: ATF4 (CREB2)-driven SIRT4 transcription and its loss under high mTORC1 activity have been reported in one study; this contrasts with the mTORC1-dependent translational induction of ATF4 that drives purine and glutathione synthesis.

mechanism: ATG101 binds ATG13 through HORMA-domain interaction, stabilising it within the initiation complex
ATG13 bridges ULK1 and FIP200 and is required for complex integrity and ULK1 activity
ATG14L is the subunit that targets the VPS34 complex to the autophagy initiation site, defining complex I
The ATG12–ATG5–ATG16L1 complex acts as the E3-like ligase that conjugates LC3/GABARAP proteins to phagophore phosphatidylethanolamine, a step required for autophagosome expansion and closure.
Autophagic lysosome reformation regenerates the lysosomal pool consumed during autophagy, closing the amino-acid/mTORC1 oscillatory loop.
Completed autophagolysosomal degradation of cytoplasmic protein replenishes free amino acid pools
Beclin-1 is the core coiled-coil subunit of the autophagy-specific class III PI3K complex
Beclin-1 is shared between VPS34 complexes I and II; complex II substitutes UVRAG for ATG14L and functions in autophagosome maturation and endosomal trafficking.

Growth-factor-induced phosphorylation of the DEPTOR degron, primed by mTOR (or by S6K1 and RSK1) and completed by casein kinase 1 alpha, creates a betaTrCP binding site; SCF-betaTrCP then ubiquitinates DEPTOR and targets it for proteasomal degradation, so active mTOR removes its own inhibitor.
CAD catalyses the committed early steps of de novo pyrimidine synthesis, producing dihydroorotate from glutamine and bicarbonate
Local lysosomal Ca2+ binds calmodulin and activates calcineurin adjacent to the lysosomal surface
CLEAR target genes include core autophagy genes, so TFEB activation raises autophagic flux as well as lysosomal capacity
Coordinate induction of lysosomal hydrolases, membrane proteins and v-ATPase subunits expands lysosomal number and degradative capacity
After mTOR-mediated priming, CK1alpha phosphorylates DEPTOR to complete the phosphodegron recognised by the SCF-betaTrCP ubiquitin ligase.
notes: Gao and Duan (2011) place mTOR priming before CK1alpha phosphorylation of the degron, whereas Zhao (2011) attributes degron phosphorylation to S6K1 and RSK1.

mechanism: Hypophosphorylated 4E-BP1 sequesters eIF4E and suppresses translation of the structured-5'UTR HIF1A mRNA; mTORC1 phosphorylation relieves this
4E-BPs restrain translation of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial mRNAs including TFAM and mitochondrial ribosomal proteins; mTORC1 phosphorylation relieves this

Hypophosphorylated 4E-BP1 binds eIF4E and restrains cap-dependent translation of MYC mRNA, whose structured 5′ untranslated region makes it highly dependent on eIF4F; mTORC1 phosphorylation of 4E-BP1 releases eIF4E and raises c-Myc protein.
4E-BP restrains translation of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial mRNAs including TFAM and respiratory chain components; mTORC1-dependent 4E-BP phosphorylation relieves this.
notes: The primary evidence is translational profiling showing that mTOR inhibition lowers synthesis of TFAM and other nucleus-encoded mitochondrial proteins in wild-type cells but not in cells lacking 4E-BP1 and 4E-BP2.

mechanism: Hypophosphorylated 4E-BP1 sequesters eIF4E and suppresses translation of VEGFA mRNA, which has a long structured 5′ untranslated region; mTORC1 phosphorylation of 4E-BP1 relieves this, adding a translational arm to HIF-1alpha-dependent VEGFA transcription.
p300-mediated acetylation of ATG proteins (ATG5, ATG7, ATG12, LC3) suppresses autophagosome formation; p300 depletion induces autophagy
notes: External reference not independently verified.

mechanism: p300 acetylates lipogenic regulators to promote de novo lipid synthesis, providing an acetylation-dependent limb of mTORC1 lipid output
notes: External reference not independently verified.

mechanism: ERK2 phosphorylates TFEB at Ser142 under nutrient-replete conditions, favouring cytoplasmic retention of TFEB and limiting expression of its lysosomal and autophagy target genes.
notes: Ser142 is also phosphorylated by mTORC1, which is regarded as the main Ser142 kinase in amino-acid signalling; the contribution of ERK varies with cell type and stimulus.

mechanism: Fatty acid synthase performs the iterative condensation producing palmitate, the committed output of de novo lipogenesis.

Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase catalyses the first and rate-limiting oxidative step of the pentose phosphate pathway, reducing NADP+ to NADPH. This is the specific enzymatic step by which the SREBP–G6PD arm supplies reducing equivalents.
G6PD catalyses the rate-limiting oxidative step, supplying NADPH for reductive biosynthesis and ribose-5-phosphate for nucleotides
Glutaminase converts glutamine to glutamate, the entry step that permits GDH-dependent anaplerosis
Glucose supplies carbon for glycolysis after phosphorylation to glucose-6-phosphate.
Glutamate dehydrogenase converts glutamate to alpha-ketoglutarate, feeding glutamine carbon into the TCA cycle
Glutamine supplies carbon, via glutamate and alpha-ketoglutarate, and nitrogen for TCA-cycle anaplerosis in proliferating cells.
Grb10 binds and desensitises the IGF-1 receptor, extending the feedback brake to IGF-1 signalling
Stabilised Grb10 binds the insulin receptor and desensitises downstream signalling, independently of the S6K1-IRS-1 arm
HIF-1alpha induces hexokinase 2, committing imported glucose to glycolysis as glucose-6-phosphate
HIF-1alpha induces LDHA, regenerating NAD+ and sustaining high glycolytic flux with lactate export
HIF-1alpha induces PFKFB3, raising fructose-2,6-bisphosphate and allosterically activating PFK1
HIF-1alpha raises PKM2 expression; the M2 isoform supports the biosynthetic rather than purely catabolic use of glycolytic carbon
HIF-1alpha binds hypoxia-response elements in the SLC2A1 promoter, raising GLUT1 expression and glucose uptake
HIF-1alpha, with HIF-1beta (ARNT), binds a hypoxia-response element in the VEGFA 5′-flanking region and induces VEGFA transcription.
notes: VEGF-A is also controlled translationally through 4E-BP1–eIF4E, so mTORC1 raises VEGF-A both through HIF-1alpha-driven transcription and through cap-dependent translation.

mechanism: Hexokinase 2 converts glucose to glucose-6-phosphate at the entry to glycolysis; glucose-6-phosphate can also feed other pathways.
HMG-CoA reductase catalyses the rate-limiting conversion of HMG-CoA to mevalonate, committing carbon to sterol synthesis.
Cell-surface IL-1alpha signals through IL1R-NF-kB to sustain the pro-inflammatory secretory programme of senescent cells

Indirect effect: insulin signalling through IRS-1, PI3K and AKT is a required positive input to hepatic SREBP1c expression and processing. In liver-specific Tsc1-deficient mice, S6K1-mediated inhibitory phosphorylation of IRS-1 suppresses this input and SREBP1c, protecting against diet-induced steatosis despite constitutive mTORC1 activity.
notes: Genetic activation of hepatic mTORC1 and its pharmacological inhibition are therefore not mirror images for liver lipid phenotypes.

mechanism: LDHA converts pyruvate to lactate with NAD+ regeneration, permitting sustained aerobic glycolytic flux

When mTORC1 is inactive, dephosphorylated lipin 1 enters the nucleus and lowers nuclear SREBP protein abundance, SREBP promoter activity and SREBP target-gene expression; mTORC1 phosphorylation keeps lipin 1 cytoplasmic and relieves this inhibition. Direct binding or sequestration of SREBP by lipin 1 has not been shown.

Lysosomal stress, including oxidative stress sensed directly by TRPML1 (MCOLN1), opens this lysosomal Ca2+ channel; the released Ca2+ activates calcineurin, which dephosphorylates TFEB and drives its nuclear translocation independently of mTORC1 inhibition.
MK2 phosphorylates ZFP36L1, inactivating its degradation of AU-rich-element-containing cytokine transcripts
TRPML1 releases lysosomal Ca2+ into a local microdomain on mTORC1 inhibition or lysosomal stress
TRPML1 is a channel resident in the lysosomal membrane, placing the Ca2+-calcineurin-TFEB step on the lysosomal surface
MTHFD2 drives the mitochondrial tetrahydrofolate cycle, generating formyl units used for nucleotide synthesis
Formyl-tetrahydrofolate produced by the MTHFD2-dependent cycle supplies carbon to the purine ring, demonstrated by metabolic tracing
Adipocyte Raptor deletion impairs adipogenesis and reduces fat mass with enhanced mitochondrial respiration, placing mTORC1 upstream of the storage programme
Through S6K1-IRS-1 and Grb10, active mTORC1 restrains PI3K-AKT; relief of both brakes on mTORC1 inhibition produces rebound AKT activation
mTORC1 phosphorylates AMBRA1, preventing AMBRA1-TRAF6-mediated ULK1 ubiquitylation, self-association and activation
notes: Ser52 of human AMBRA1 is the mapped mTOR site; its dephosphorylation on mTOR inhibition allows AMBRA1 and TRAF6 to drive Lys63-linked ubiquitylation of ULK1.

mechanism: In proliferating cells with high mTORC1 activity, ATF4 (CREB2) protein has been reported to undergo proteasome-dependent degradation, lowering SIRT4 transcription and thereby relieving SIRT4-mediated inhibition of glutamate dehydrogenase.
context: glutamine metabolism and SIRT4 repression in proliferating cells
notes: This is opposite in sign to the mTORC1-dependent translational induction of ATF4 reproduced in several laboratories for purine, one-carbon and glutathione synthesis; the degradation arm rests on a single study and the conditions that reconcile the two are unknown.

mechanism: mTORC1 raises ATF4 protein by translational control independent of eIF2alpha phosphorylation, balancing amino-acid supply against demand
mTORC1 phosphorylates ATG13 within the ULK1 initiation complex, contributing to layered repression of phagophore initiation
notes: Ser258 has been identified as a direct mTOR site on ATG13; how much ATG13 phosphorylation contributes to autophagy repression relative to ULK1 phosphorylation remains debated.

mechanism: mTOR phosphorylates ATG14 at five mapped sites, suppressing the ATG14-containing VPS34 complex; mutation of all five sites reduces this inhibition.
notes: The five residues were mapped by in vitro kinase assays and mutagenesis; ATG14 lacking all five sites escapes mTORC1-mediated inhibition of the associated VPS34 activity.

mechanism: Amino acids released by completed autolysosomal degradation reactivate mTOR, and this reactivation is required for autophagic lysosome reformation, the tubulation and scission of autolysosomal membranes that regenerates functional lysosomes and terminates the autophagic cycle.
context: late phase of a completed autophagic cycle

mechanism: Through phosphorylation of ULK1 at Ser758 (Ser757 in mouse) and of ATG13, ATG14L and AMBRA1, mTORC1 imposes layered repression of phagophore initiation.
mTOR is required for expression of the sterol biosynthetic gene programme through SREBP2
mTORC1 directly phosphorylates the acetyltransferase p300, increasing its activity toward autophagy and lipogenic substrates

mTORC1 represses SIRT4 transcription by promoting proteasomal degradation of CREB2 (ATF4), relieving SIRT4-mediated inhibition of glutamate dehydrogenase and increasing entry of glutamine-derived alpha-ketoglutarate into the TCA cycle.
notes: A proposed second arm, S6K1–eIF4B-dependent translation of c-Myc driving glutaminase expression, rested on a study that has since been retracted.

mechanism: Glycolytic flux rises through cap-dependent translation of HIF-1alpha and consequent induction of GLUT1, HK2, PFKFB3, PKM2 and LDHA
Direct mTORC1 phosphorylation stabilises Grb10 protein; identified by unbiased phosphoproteomics as a core mTORC1 substrate
notes: Site numbering follows the phosphoproteomic reports; the stabilisation, not the exact residues, is the established claim.

mechanism: mTORC1-dependent phosphorylation of Grb10 stabilises the protein against degradation and raises its steady-state level; stabilised Grb10 binds and desensitises the insulin and IGF-1 receptors, forming one of the negative-feedback brakes on upstream signalling.

mTORC1 raises HIF-1alpha synthesis through 4E-BP1/eIF4E- and S6K1-dependent cap-dependent translation of HIF1A mRNA, including under normoxia in TSC-deficient cells. Separately, a TOR signalling (TOS) motif in HIF-1alpha binds Raptor and is required for full HIF-1alpha transcriptional activity, a protein-level mechanism distinct from translational control.
mTOR-dependent translation raises IL-1alpha, which drives NF-kB-dependent amplification of the senescence-associated secretory phenotype

mTORC1 has been reported to phosphorylate IRS-1 directly at Ser636/Ser639, with Raptor acting as a scaffold, in a rapamycin-sensitive manner; phosphorylation of these serines next to the Tyr632 PI3K-binding motif impairs IRS-1-associated PI3K activation and contributes to nutrient-induced insulin resistance.
notes: Other studies attribute Ser636/Ser639 phosphorylation to S6K1, so the relative contributions of mTORC1 and S6K1 at these residues are unresolved.

mechanism: De novo lipogenesis proceeds through SREBP1, with mTORC1 acting both by phosphorylating Lipin1 and by promoting SREBP processing
context: growth-factor and nutrient sufficiency; in liver, contributes to steatosis under hyperinsulinaemic conditions
notes: Hepatic mTORC1 is required for insulin-induced SREBP1c and lipogenesis but is not sufficient on its own, because parallel AKT signalling is also needed.

mechanism: mTORC1 phosphorylates Lipin1 and retains it in the cytoplasm, preventing its nuclear entry; Lipin1 is a direct mTORC1 substrate
notes: Site numbering follows the mouse Lipin1 phosphosites reported in the primary study.

mechanism: mTORC1 reactivation during prolonged starvation terminates autophagy and drives autophagic lysosome reformation, regenerating the lysosomal pool
By holding TFEB and TFE3 out of the nucleus, mTORC1 suppresses CLEAR-driven expansion of the lysosomal compartment
Mitochondrial biogenesis is supported through 4E-BP-dependent translation of mitochondrial mRNAs and the YY1-PGC-1alpha axis
mTORC1 raises c-Myc protein by phosphorylating 4E-BP1 and releasing eIF4E for cap-dependent translation of MYC mRNA, whose structured 5′ untranslated region makes it highly eIF4F-dependent.
The oxidative pentose phosphate pathway is activated through SREBP-driven G6PD expression downstream of mTORC1

Amino-acid-dependent, rapamycin-sensitive mTOR kinase activity is required for the transactivation activity of PPARgamma during adipocyte differentiation; rapamycin disrupts the C/EBPalpha–PPARgamma positive feedback loop, and the PPARgamma ligand troglitazone reverses this block.
Purine synthesis is driven through ATF4-dependent induction of MTHFD2 and control of the mitochondrial tetrahydrofolate cycle
Pyrimidine synthesis is stimulated acutely by the mTORC1-S6K1-CAD Ser1859 axis, coupling growth signalling to nucleotide supply
mTORC1 phosphorylates Pacer, blocking its engagement of HOPS and STX17 and thereby autophagosome-lysosome fusion; also couples to lipid metabolism
notes: Single-group finding External reference not independently verified.

mechanism: mTORC1-driven translation is required for the senescence-associated secretory phenotype; rapamycin suppresses the SASP without eliminating senescent cells
notes: Intervention efficacy alone does not establish causal primacy of mTOR in ageing.

mechanism: mTORC1 represses SIRT4 expression by promoting proteasomal degradation of CREB2, de-repressing glutamate dehydrogenase
notes: Rests on a single principal study, which attributes SIRT4 repression to mTORC1-dependent destabilisation of CREB2 (ATF4) rather than to a defined S6K1 step; this repression underlies the glutamate dehydrogenase limb of glutamine anaplerosis.

mechanism: mTORC1 promotes SREBP1 processing and nuclear accumulation, both by phosphorylating Lipin1 and by supporting proteolytic maturation
mTOR activity is required for SREBP2-dependent sterol biosynthetic gene expression; part of this transcriptional profile is rapamycin-resistant
Rapamycin-sensitive, mTOR-dependent phosphorylation of the STAT3 transactivation domain at Ser727 enhances STAT3 transcriptional output
notes: Whether mTOR acts directly or through an intermediate kinase is not fully settled.

mechanism: mTORC1 phosphorylates TFE3 at the site equivalent to TFEB Ser211, creating a 14-3-3 site and enforcing cytoplasmic retention
notes: External reference not independently verified.

mechanism: Phosphorylation at Ser142 acts with Ser211 to restrain TFEB nuclear translocation and CLEAR-network output
notes: Ser142 is also an ERK2 site (assigned in ref [543]), so this residue integrates more than one input; the mTORC1-dependent assignment rests on ref [544].

mechanism: Phosphorylation at Ser211 creates a 14-3-3 binding site that retains TFEB in the cytoplasm and prevents nuclear import
notes: Ser122 has also been reported as an mTORC1 site contributing to cytoplasmic retention.

mechanism: mTORC1 also phosphorylates TFEB at Ser122; a phosphomimetic Ser122 substitution keeps TFEB cytoplasmic after mTORC1 inhibition even when Ser211 is dephosphorylated, and blocks Torin1-induced lysosomal biogenesis.
notes: The Ser122 site has been reported by a single laboratory (Vega-Rubin-de-Celis 2017).

mechanism: ULK1 Ser637 (mouse numbering; human Ser638) is dephosphorylated during nutrient starvation and its phosphorylation falls with mTOR inhibition, but the same site is also assigned to AMPK, so the responsible kinase is unresolved.
context: mouse site numbering; human experiments in Shang 2011
notes: The kinase assignment for this site conflicts between studies, and the consequences for ULK1-AMPK binding differ between experimental systems.

mechanism: mTORC1 phosphorylates UVRAG at Ser498, enhancing RUBCN binding and suppressing UVRAG-dependent autophagosome and endosome maturation
mTORC1 phosphorylation of WIPI2 promotes its HUWE1-dependent ubiquitination and degradation, limiting recruitment of the ATG16L1 conjugation machinery
notes: Single principal report External reference not independently verified.

mechanism: mTOR associates with YY1 and is required for the YY1-PGC-1alpha interaction at mitochondrial gene promoters; rapamycin disrupts the complex
c-Myc transcriptionally represses miR-23a and miR-23b, relieving their repression of the glutaminase transcript and raising glutaminase protein, which increases conversion of glutamine to glutamate.
notes: mTORC1-dependent c-Myc translation supports glutamine anaplerosis. The miR-23a/b route to glutaminase was established in human B-cell and prostate cancer cells.

mechanism: De novo fatty acid and sterol synthesis consume NADPH as the reductant, which couples the pentose phosphate arm to the lipogenic arm.
NRF1 induces TFAM expression, coupling the nuclear transcriptional programme to mitochondrial DNA replication and transcription.
The oxidative arm of the pentose phosphate pathway, activated by SREBP-driven G6PD expression downstream of mTORC1, generates NADPH.
notes: The oxidative pentose phosphate pathway supplies NADPH and ribose-5-phosphate.

mechanism: The pentose phosphate pathway generates ribose-5-phosphate, the pentose backbone for nucleotide synthesis.
Fructose-2,6-bisphosphate produced by PFKFB3 allosterically activates PFK1, the principal flux-controlling step
WIPI2 is a PROPPIN-family PI3P effector whose recruitment to the phagophore depends on direct PI3P binding through its beta-propeller.
VPS34 is the catalytic lipid kinase of class III PI3K complex I, generating PI(3)P at the phagophore
PI(3)P generated by complex I recruits WIPI proteins and the ATG conjugation machinery, committing the phagophore to elongation
The ATG14L-containing VPS34 complex phosphorylates phosphatidylinositol at the 3-position to generate PI3P on the nascent phagophore.

UVRAG-containing class III PI3K complex II is implicated in late autophagy, with UVRAG engaging the class C Vps/HOPS tethering complex to promote autophagosome fusion with late endosomes and lysosomes. This maturation function is genetically separable from UVRAG binding to Beclin-1, so whether it requires the lipid-kinase activity of complex II is not settled.
PKM2 catalyses the final glycolytic step; its regulated low-activity state diverts upstream intermediates into biosynthesis
PPARgamma is the master transcriptional driver of adipocyte differentiation and lipid-storage gene expression
notes: External reference not independently verified.

mechanism: PGC-1alpha coactivates the nuclear transcriptional programme for mitochondrial biogenesis and oxidative metabolism
PGC-1alpha coactivates NRF1 on the promoters of nuclear-encoded respiratory and mitochondrial biogenesis genes.
Calcineurin dephosphorylates TFEB, releasing 14-3-3 and permitting nuclear entry and CLEAR-network transcription
notes: Pharmacologically relevant: calcineurin inhibitors (tacrolimus, cyclosporine) would be expected to oppose this step.

mechanism: Amino-acid-loaded Rag GTPases recruit TFEB and MITF to the lysosomal surface, which is required for mTORC1 to phosphorylate them
FIP200 is the scaffold subunit of the ULK1 initiation complex and is required for ULK1 stability and phagophore nucleation
Ribose-5-phosphate is converted to PRPP, the committed substrate for de novo purine synthesis; links the pentose phosphate arm to the ATF4–MTHFD2 purine arm.

Ribose-5-phosphate is converted to PRPP, which UMP synthase uses to convert orotate to OMP before decarboxylating it to UMP; this step lies downstream of CAD and DHODH and links the pentose phosphate arm to the S6K1–CAD pyrimidine arm.
S6K1 phosphorylates CAD at Ser1859, promoting its oligomerisation and raising flux through the first three steps of de novo pyrimidine synthesis
notes: Demonstrated independently by two groups in the same year, one by unbiased phosphoproteomics.

mechanism: S6K1 phosphorylates IRS-1 on inhibitory serines, promoting its degradation and blunting PI3K-AKT output from the insulin receptor.
notes: Sites are human IRS-1 numbering; the primary reports use the mouse and rat equivalents Ser302 and Ser632/Ser635. Underlies mTORC1-associated insulin resistance and the paradoxical protection from steatosis seen after liver Tsc1 deletion.

mechanism: mTORC1-activated S6K1 directly phosphorylates Rictor at Thr1135, creating a 14-3-3 binding site without altering mTORC2 assembly or in vitro kinase activity. Two studies found that a T1135A mutant raises AKT Ser473 phosphorylation, indicating feedback inhibition, whereas two others saw no major change in mTORC2 activity or AKT phosphorylation.
notes: Boulbès et al. 2010 [53] detected Thr1135 phosphorylation in mTORC2-deficient cells, suggesting that it may also regulate functions of Rictor outside mTORC2.

mechanism: S6K1 is required for insulin-stimulated proteolytic processing of SREBP-1c, providing an S6K1-dependent limb of mTORC1 lipogenic output

HIF-1alpha carries a TOS motif recognised by the Raptor substrate pocket, the same surface that reads the S6K1, 4E-BP1 and PRAS40 motifs; Raptor binding through this motif is required for mTORC1-dependent HIF-1alpha activity.
notes: The HIF-1alpha TOS motif and its Raptor binding were characterised by a single laboratory (Land and Tee 2007).

mechanism: Raptor mediates the nutrient-dependent association of mTORC1 with the ULK1-ATG13-FIP200 complex, presenting ULK1 for inhibitory phosphorylation at Ser758 (Ser757 in mouse), which prevents its activation by AMPK; the net effect of the interaction on ULK1 is inhibitory.
notes: manual override: Raptor binds the ULK1 TOS motif to present ULK1 for inhibitory Ser757 phosphorylation by mTORC1; the net effect of the Raptor-ULK1 interaction on ULK1 activity is inhibitory, so a positive sign would mislead sign-aware path queries.

mechanism: Pacer (RUBCNL) promotes autophagosome maturation by engaging STX17 and the HOPS tethering complex and by relieving Rubicon-mediated inhibition of VPS34.
SIRT4 ADP-ribosylates glutamate dehydrogenase and inhibits it; its repression downstream of mTORC1 releases the enzyme
notes: External reference not independently verified.

mechanism: GLUT1 mediates facilitative glucose import across the plasma membrane, raising intracellular glucose availability
Nuclear SREBP1 induces acetyl-CoA carboxylase 1, catalysing the committed step of de novo lipogenesis.
Nuclear SREBP1 induces fatty acid synthase, one of the lipogenic target genes whose induction defines the mTORC1–SREBP1 arm.
SREBP-dependent induction of G6PD activates the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway downstream of mTORC1
Nuclear SREBP1 induces ACC, FASN and SCD1, driving de novo fatty-acid synthesis
Nuclear SREBP1 induces stearoyl-CoA desaturase 1, required for monounsaturated fatty acid supply to membrane lipid and triglyceride synthesis.
Nuclear SREBP2 induces HMGCR, HMGCS1 and LDLR, driving the sterol biosynthetic and uptake programme
Nuclear SREBP2 induces HMG-CoA reductase and other mevalonate pathway genes; mTOR activity is required for full expression of this sterol biosynthetic programme.
TFAM packages mitochondrial DNA and activates its transcription; its loss abolishes mtDNA maintenance and oxidative phosphorylation, making it a required effector of mitochondrial biogenesis.
TFE3 binds the same CLEAR elements as TFEB and drives lysosomal and autophagy gene expression, providing partial redundancy
notes: TFE3 is itself subject to mTORC1-dependent cytoplasmic retention. Its binding to CLEAR elements and induction of lysosomal and autophagy genes was shown by Martina et al. (Sci Signal 2014).

mechanism: Nuclear TFEB binds CLEAR E-box elements and drives approximately 470 lysosomal and autophagy genes coordinately
MCOLN1 is itself a CLEAR target gene, so TFEB activation raises TRPML1 expression and amplifies the Ca2+-calcineurin input back onto TFEB
notes: TRPML1-dependent calcineurin activation acts upstream of TFEB. Medina et al. (2015) describe MCOLN1 as a direct TFEB target, forming a positive feedback loop.

mechanism: TFEB drives RRAGD expression, increasing Rag-dependent lysosomal recruitment of mTORC1 - a transcriptional feed-forward loop onto mTORC1
context: renal and pancreatic tumours with MiT/TFE activation
notes: Explains how MiT/TFE activation can drive mTORC1 rather than only responding to it.

mechanism: Activated ULK1 phosphorylates its complex partner ATG13 at several sites within the initiation complex; the modification accompanies autophagy induction and promotes ATG13 recruitment to damaged mitochondria during mitophagy, but it is not known to activate ATG13 itself.
ULK1 phosphorylates ATG14L at Ser29, stimulating VPS34 activity in the autophagy-specific complex and opposing the inhibitory mTORC1 marks
notes: External reference not independently verified.

mechanism: ULK1/Atg1 phosphorylates ATG9 to control its trafficking to and from the phagophore assembly site, a required step for membrane delivery during autophagosome formation.
context: demonstrated for Atg1–Atg9 in yeast; the mammalian ULK1–ATG9A equivalent is supported but less firmly established
notes: Do not upgrade without a mammalian reference.

mechanism: ULK1 kinase activity initiates phagophore formation; it is the principal node through which nutrient and energy status gate autophagy
ULK1 phosphorylates Beclin-1 at Ser14, activating VPS34 lipid-kinase activity within autophagy-specific class III PI3K complexes

Active ULK1 phosphorylates FIP200 within the initiation complex; the modification accompanies autophagy induction, although a specific requirement for it in phagophore nucleation has not been demonstrated.
UVRAG defines VPS34 complex II, mutually exclusive with ATG14L.
WIPI2 binds ATG16L1 directly and recruits the ATG12–ATG5–ATG16L1 conjugation machinery to PI3P-positive phagophores, licensing LC3 lipidation.
Phosphorylated TFE3 is bound by 14-3-3 and held in the cytoplasm, mirroring the TFEB mechanism
14-3-3 binds phospho-Ser211 TFEB, masking its nuclear localisation signal and sequestering it in the cytoplasm
The YY1-PGC-1alpha complex drives transcription of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial genes, supporting oxidative capacity
YY1 and PGC-1alpha form a transcriptional complex on mitochondrial gene promoters whose assembly depends on mTOR activity
Active ZFP36L1 degrades SASP cytokine mRNAs; its MK2-dependent inactivation permits their accumulation
notes: mTOR-dependent translation is generally required for the SASP, but the MK2-ZFP36L1 mRNA-decay mechanism rests on a single primary study.

mechanism: Actin polymerisation, not translational control, is the mTORC2-dependent requirement for late-phase LTP.
AKT phosphorylates BAD to promote 14-3-3 binding and reduce its pro-apoptotic activity.
Ser473 phosphorylation markedly enhances AKT activity toward FOXO1; phosphorylated FOXO1 binds 14-3-3 and is excluded from the nucleus.
notes: Substrate-selective consequence of Ser473: mTORC2 biases AKT output toward survival and transcriptional programmes.

mechanism: FOXO3a phosphorylation by AKT is strongly Ser473-dependent, producing 14-3-3 binding and nuclear exclusion of a pro-apoptotic transcriptional programme.
AKT phosphorylated only at Thr308 retains substantial activity toward GSK3β, so this output is largely independent of mTORC2.
notes: Negative control for the Ser473-selective edges: it is why mTORC2 loss does not phenocopy AKT loss.

mechanism: AKT phosphorylates MDM2, promoting nuclear entry and p53 turnover; part of the mTORC1-independent AKT output retained in distal-network lesions.
notes: One of the mTORC1-independent AKT outputs that make distal-network lesions poor predictors of rapalog sensitivity.

mechanism: AKT phosphorylates the Rab GAP AS160, creating a 14-3-3 site that relieves its restraint on GLUT4 storage vesicles.
AKT phosphorylates and inactivates TSC2, permitting Rheb·GTP accumulation; this output is largely retained by Thr308-only AKT.
notes: TSC2, like GSK3beta, is a Ser473-independent AKT substrate.

mechanism: XPLN binds Rictor and suppresses mTORC2-mediated AKT Ser473 phosphorylation independently of its Rho GEF activity.
notes: Single-group finding with limited replication.

mechanism: The basolateral sodium pump sustains the electrochemical gradient that drives transepithelial reabsorption.
Unphosphorylated BAD neutralises BCL-XL and promotes apoptosis; its AKT-dependent sequestration is one arm of mTORC2-supported survival signalling.
CLC-K channels provide the basolateral chloride exit required for net salt transport.

DEPTOR binds mTORC2 and restrains its kinase activity, so DEPTOR loss increases phosphorylation of AKT Ser473 and SGK1. DEPTOR overexpression nevertheless activates AKT indirectly, by suppressing mTORC1 and relieving its feedback inhibition of PI3K.
ETV7 is reported as the defining subunit of a putative third mTOR assembly, designated mTORC3, which is rapamycin-insensitive and supports proliferation in cancer cells.
