Liver-specific Rictor deletion produces glucose intolerance and a phenotype reminiscent of type 2 diabetes, so hepatic mTORC2 is required for normal glucose handling.
Rictor loss has modest, largely transient effects; only the double mutant impairs differentiation, so mTORC2 contributes but is not rate-limiting while mTORC1 is intact.

Pharmacological activation of mTORC2 with A-443654 raises hydrophobic-motif phosphorylation of its substrates in mouse and fly; the compound is not selective for mTORC2, and no directly acting, selective mTORC2 agonist has been independently validated.
Raising mTORC2 activity enhances L-LTP and long-term memory in wild-type animals and reverses age-associated memory impairment in both mice and flies.
AMPECT established nab-sirolimus in advanced malignant PEComa, with response enriched in TSC2-mutant tumours.

Anabolic resistance is defined as a blunted muscle protein-synthesis response to amino acids and to loading; mechanism is multifactorial (reduced sensitivity of the mTORC1 machinery, impaired postprandial perfusion and amino-acid delivery, splanchnic extraction).
The SASP is the secretory programme of senescent cells; the distinction matters because rapamycin suppresses the secretome without removing the cells.

Thymic involution, contraction of the naive repertoire, accumulation of PD-1+ exhausted-like cells and inflammaging together degrade the response to vaccination, which is why vaccine response became the testing ground for geroprotective mTOR inhibition.
Phospholipase D-generated phosphatidic acid transmits mechanical activation to mTOR, by an ERK-independent mechanism consistent with direct activation.
Rac1-driven actin polymerisation is the structural arm of L-LTP, distinct from the mTORC1-dependent translational arm.
Spine density falls with loss of the mTORC2-Tiam1-Rac1 actin-polymerisation arm.
Rapamycin reduces brain amyloid-beta and improves cognition in 3xTg-AD mice, with benefit dependent on intact autophagy and on early initiation.
notes: Largely confined to treatment begun before substantial pathology accumulates.

mechanism: Pharmacological mTOR inhibition induces autophagy and accelerates clearance of misfolded aggregates in cellular and animal models; this is the whole basis of the neurodegeneration rationale.

Rapamycin reduces brain amyloid-beta and improves cognition in 3xTg-AD mice, with benefit dependent on intact autophagy and largely confined to treatment initiated before substantial pathology accumulates.
context: 3xTg-AD mice; ERAP phase IIa under way in humans
notes: No controlled human efficacy data exist.

mechanism: Sirolimus-class agents have real but largely cytostatic antitumour activity: albumin-bound sirolimus is approved for advanced malignant perivascular epithelioid cell tumour, with response enriched in TSC2-mutant tumours, while no randomised trial of a rapalog in a solid tumour has shown a significant overall survival benefit. Separately, deferral of lethal neoplasia may account for part of the lifespan extension rapamycin produces in mice.
context: advanced solid tumours; mouse lifespan studies
notes: What is disputed is the mechanism of murine lifespan extension, not the existence of antitumour activity.

mechanism: Rapamycin or CCI-779 reduces aggregates and improves outcomes in fly and mouse models of Huntington's disease.
In kidney transplant recipients without pre-existing diabetes sirolimus was independently associated with new-onset diabetes, adjusted hazard ratios roughly 1.4-1.7.
notes: Combines direct beta-cell toxicity with peripheral insulin resistance from chronic mTORC2 loss.

mechanism: Rapamycin protects dopaminergic neurons in cellular and rodent models of Parkinson disease; in those models protection tracked with blocked production of the stress protein RTP801/REDD1 and preserved AKT phosphorylation, whereas the catalytic inhibitor Torin1 was not protective. Enhanced autophagic clearance of alpha-synuclein is a separate route shown in other model systems.
Rapamycin prevents seizures after depletion of STRADA in models of PMSE, with support from preclinical work and small clinical series.
mTOR inhibition with rapamycin or CCI-779 induces autophagy and reduces polyglutamine-expanded huntingtin aggregates and toxicity in fly and mouse models.

Direct beta-cell toxicity of rapamycin: reduced insulin secretion, disturbed calcium handling and mitochondrial dysfunction; one of the two components of NODAT alongside mTORC2-dependent peripheral insulin resistance.
Rapamycin blocks L-LTP while sparing the early phase, which is the pharmacological demonstration that the late phase is protein-synthesis dependent.

mTORC1 drives the adaptive growth of cardiomyocytes, so partial inhibition blunts physiological hypertrophy; the same inhibition attenuates pathological hypertrophy in multiple models and regresses established pressure-overload hypertrophy, so the adaptive and maladaptive arms are not separable pharmacologically.
Low-dose rapamycin during acute viral infection enhances the quantity and functional quality of memory CD8 T cells, T cell-intrinsically and across infection models.
context: low dose, acute viral infection; reproduced in non-human primates
notes: The CD8 memory paradox: partial inhibition improves rather than suppresses one arm of adaptive immunity.

mechanism: Cytopenias follow from the proliferative requirement for mTORC1 in haematopoiesis.
Intermittent dosing allows mTORC2 to recover between doses; preclinical data and low-exposure human cohorts without dysglycaemia support this but no powered trial has tested it.
notes: Evidence is emerging rather than established.

mechanism: Hyperglycaemia at immunosuppressive exposures reflects hepatic, adipose and beta-cell physiology, chiefly through loss of mTORC2 signalling.
notes: Contrast RMC-5552, where hyperglycaemia occurred in only 4% despite complete mTORC1 blockade.

mechanism: Rapamycin partially corrects the hyperphagic obesity of POMC-neuron Tsc1 deletion.
Hypertriglyceridaemia and hypercholesterolaemia on mTOR inhibitors reflect altered hepatic and adipose lipid handling, with both complexes implicated.
notes: Dyslipidaemia is the adipose and hepatic consequence of mTOR inhibition.

mechanism: In PEARL, lean tissue mass increased rather than decreased in women on 10 mg weekly compounded rapamycin; a secondary, sex-restricted finding at very low exposure.
notes: Subgroup analysis; no trough concentrations measured. Reassuring but not evidence of efficacy.

mechanism: Encapsulated rapamycin begun at 600 days of age extended median and maximal lifespan of genetically heterogeneous mice at three independent sites, raising the age at 90% mortality by 9% in males and 14% in females; a threefold higher dose of 42 ppm increased median lifespan by 23% in males and 26% in females, and treatment begun at 20 months extends survival even when given for only three months or in alternating months.
notes: Continuous exposure is not required for lifespan extension, although the benefit of brief or intermittent dosing is sex-dependent.

mechanism: urinalysis monitoring is the stated mitigation.

Chronic mTORC1 inhibition is predicted to impair the anabolic response of skeletal muscle and to promote sarcopenia; acute rapamycin blocks the contraction-induced rise in human muscle protein synthesis, whereas intermittent low-dose exposure has not produced measurable muscle loss and was associated with increased lean tissue mass in one randomised trial. Whether intermittent dosing preserves the acute anabolic response while lowering chronic tone is unresolved.
notes: Human data conflict across exposures, and no trial has tested chronic dosing against a muscle-mass endpoint in older adults.

mechanism: Rapalog stomatitis follows from mTORC1 dependence of renewing oral epithelium and is substantially preventable with topical dexamethasone or tacrolimus prophylaxis.
notes: The only self-reported adverse event significantly more frequent among off-label users.

mechanism: Rapamycin expands regulatory T cells preferentially, which is the basis of its immunosuppressive use.
Rapamycin suppresses the SASP without eliminating senescent cells, so a drug can give geroprotective benefit by attenuating consequences of a process it did not cause.
notes: Suppression of the SASP by rapamycin shows that an intervention is effective, which does not by itself establish causal primacy.

mechanism: Alpha-synuclein is degraded by both macroautophagy and the proteasome, and mTOR inhibition with rapamycin induces autophagy and lowers alpha-synuclein levels in cell models; rapamycin also protects dopaminergic neurons in rodent models of Parkinson disease.
context: cellular and rodent models of Parkinson disease

mechanism: Rheb-mTORC1 is required for Th1 and Th17 differentiation, with Rheb as the upstream element of this arm.

Complete response ongoing beyond six months, with clearance of pathway variants from circulating tumour DNA, in a patient with PTEN- and PIK3CA-altered endometrial cancer; 58% of enrolled patients carried pathogenic mTOR-pathway variants.
notes: A single response is an observation rather than a result.

mechanism: Chronic mTORC1 activation in obesity contributes to insulin resistance through S6K1-mediated inhibitory phosphorylation of IRS-1, and through lipotoxic consequences of constrained storage capacity.
Germline deletion of S6K1 extends median lifespan by about 19% in female mice, with no significant effect in males, placing one mTORC1 substrate arm within the longevity mechanism.
notes: The lifespan effect comes from a single mouse cohort and has not been independently replicated; S6K1-null females also showed increased AMPK activation and a caloric restriction-like gene expression profile.

mechanism: Expression of interferon-stimulated antiviral genes rose in older adults given RTB101 with low-dose everolimus for six weeks in a 264-participant phase 2a trial, the arm in which infection rates over the following year were also lower.
context: phase 2a; 264 older adults; six weeks of dosing
notes: Antiviral transcript changes are a biomarker, not proof of clinical benefit.

mechanism: SGK1 stimulates sodium reabsorption in the distal nephron, chiefly by phosphorylating NEDD4-2 and so stabilising the epithelial sodium channel at the apical membrane, and it additionally supports Na+/K+-ATPase and CLC-K-dependent transport, with consequences for blood pressure.

Alpha-synuclein is the aggregating protein of the synucleinopathies and is cleared by macroautophagy and the proteasome, which is the route that mTOR inhibition is intended to engage in Parkinson disease models.
SREBP1c induces the lipogenic enzyme battery; this is the arm through which hepatic mTORC1 contributes to steatosis under hyperinsulinaemic conditions.
Tiam1 is the Rac1 guanine-nucleotide exchange factor through which mTORC2 drives actin polymerisation in the consolidation of long-term memory.
Activating AKT1 alteration raises AKT output, which includes mTORC1-independent signalling to GSK3beta, FOXO and MDM2.
A mosaic somatic AKT1 c.49G>A (E17K) activating variant causes Proteus syndrome, present in affected tissues and absent from unaffected tissues of the same individuals.
PIK3CA, PTEN, AKT1 and receptor tyrosine kinase amplification make up the distal-network class.
Somatic mosaic AKT3 activation raises pathway output in the affected cortical lineage.
AKT3 is among the genes of focal cortical dysplasia type II, acting through somatic mosaic activation.
Somatic mosaic AKT3 activation causes hemimegalencephaly with hemispheric enlargement and severe epilepsy.
Distal-network lesions do not predict rapalog benefit: BOLERO-2 benefit was independent of PIK3CA genotype, while selection succeeded at PI3K (SOLAR-1) and AKT (CAPItello-291).
notes: Established that benefit is genotype-independent; contested as to mechanism.

mechanism: Proximal-brake lesions identify a population enriched for mTORC1 dependency: exceptional responders in urothelial and renal carcinoma, but a negative prospective basket study.
notes: Necessary rather than sufficient; as a basis for routine biomarker selection, contested.

mechanism: Heterozygous DEPDC5 loss reduces GATOR1 GAP activity toward RagA/B, so mTORC1 remains lysosomally recruited when amino acids are scarce.

In an open-label series of five patients treated with everolimus titrated to troughs of 5-15 ng/mL, the three with DEPDC5 loss-of-function variants showed substantial seizure reduction, while a DEPDC5 missense variant gave a smaller response.
notes: Genotype within GATOR1 appears to predict response; the evidence is emerging, in contrast to the established case of everolimus in TSC.

mechanism: GATOR1 component loss removes a direct restraint on mTORC1 recruitment and so belongs to the proximal-brake class.
Loss of FLCN causes Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome, in which mTORC1 signalling is dysregulated tissue-dependently rather than uniformly increased.
FLCN loss removes the GAP for RagC/D; mTORC1 signalling is consequently dysregulated in a tissue-dependent rather than uniformly increased manner.
notes: Direction of mTORC1 change is tissue-dependent, unlike the other proximal lesions.

mechanism: Germline MTOR gain-of-function causes Smith-Kingsmore syndrome with macrocephaly, intellectual disability and seizures; E1799K accounts for roughly half of cases.

The recurrent germline E1799K substitution increases mTOR kinase activity, with raised mTOR signalling in patient-derived cells that is suppressed by rapamycin; it is the most common variant in Smith-Kingsmore syndrome, accounting for roughly half of reported cases.
Activating MTOR mutations are increasingly recognised in renal cell carcinoma, clustering in FAT and kinase domains.
Cancer-associated FAT-domain MTOR substitutions can increase mTOR signalling; the magnitude and substrate profile vary among variants.
context: cancer-associated variants; biochemical and cell models

mechanism: Activating MTOR variants act on the kinase itself and so belong to the proximal-brake class.
Somatic mosaic activating MTOR variants confined to the malformed cortex cause focal cortical dysplasia type II with drug-resistant focal epilepsy.
context: somatic mosaicism restricted to dysplastic cortex
notes: Management is surgical; mTOR inhibition remains investigational.

mechanism: Somatic mosaic MTOR activation also causes hemimegalencephaly, the more severe end of the same mosaic malformation spectrum as FCD type II.
Somatic mosaic activating MTOR variants confined to malformed cortex raise kinase activity in the affected cell lineage only.
Activating MTOR variants act at the kinase itself. Depending on the variant, they can enhance mTORC1 and/or mTORC2 outputs.
notes: Proximity to mTOR does not by itself establish tumour dependence or predict response to rapalogs.

mechanism: Activating MTOR mutations occur in renal cell carcinoma; domain assignment and functional activation must be established for each variant.

Activating kinase-domain MTOR substitutions are recognised in urothelial carcinoma; a patient with a complete response to everolimus plus pazopanib carried two concurrent activating variants, E2014K and E2419K, shown to be activating in vitro.
notes: The response occurred during combined everolimus and pazopanib treatment.

mechanism: Selected MTOR kinase-domain substitutions increase signalling. E2419K was functionally activating in a urothelial cancer exceptional responder; F2108L is an FRB resistance mutation, not a kinase-domain activating substitution.
context: somatic, renal cell and urothelial carcinoma

mechanism: Activating MTOR variants in both the FAT and kinase domains belong to the proximal-brake class and are somatic.
Loss of NF1 is listed among the recurrent alterations in the PI3K-AKT-mTOR landscape in cancer.
Loss of the Ras GAP neurofibromin raises RAS-ERK-RSK signalling, which converges on the TSC complex and so raises mTORC1 output.

An NF2 nonsense mutation co-occurred with the TSC1 lesion in the index everolimus exceptional responder, and NF2 was one of five selection genes in the prospective basket study that did not demonstrate meaningful single-agent activity.
Heterozygous NPRL2 loss impairs the GATOR1 GAP for RagA/B and raises mTORC1 activity.
GATOR1 loss (DEPDC5, NPRL2, NPRL3) belongs to the proximal-brake class and is somatic.
Heterozygous NPRL3 loss impairs the GATOR1 GAP for RagA/B and raises mTORC1 activity.
One NPRL3 participant worsened in the 2023 series; the 2025 NPRL2/NPRL3 series instead reported improvement in all four participants.
notes: Small uncontrolled samples do not establish a genotype-specific response rule.

mechanism: GATOR1 loss (DEPDC5, NPRL2, NPRL3) belongs to the proximal-brake class and is somatic.
Activating PIK3CA mutations are present in roughly 30-40% of breast cancers and define the population in which alpelisib improved progression-free survival.
Activating PIK3CA mutations occur in roughly 30% of endometrial cancers; a PTEN- and PIK3CA-altered endometrial cancer gave the first complete response to RMC-5552.
Somatic mosaic PIK3CA activation is an alternative genotype of focal cortical dysplasia type II, converging on the same mTORC1 hyperactivation.
context: somatic mosaicism restricted to dysplastic cortex

mechanism: Hemimegalencephaly is caused by de novo somatic mutations in components of the PI3K-AKT3-mTOR pathway, including PIK3CA.

Mosaic somatic PIK3CA activating variants cause the PIK3CA-related overgrowth spectrum (CLOVES, megalencephaly-capillary malformation, isolated macrodactyly), the non-neoplastic counterpart of the somatic mosaicism described for FCD type II and hemimegalencephaly.
Helical (E542K, E545K) and kinase (H1047R/L) hotspot mutations raise PI3K catalytic output and hence PIP3 production.
context: somatic; also mosaic in cortical malformation

mechanism: PIK3CA mutation raises flux into a branched network in which mTORC1 is one effector among several, the defining property of the distal-network class.

Loss-of-function PTEN alterations are among the most common lesions of prostate cancer, glioblastoma and endometrial carcinoma, and raise flux through the PI3K-AKT network without creating dependency on the mTOR node.

PTEN is one of the most frequently mutated genes in endometrioid endometrial carcinoma, and a patient with PTEN- and PIK3CA-altered endometrial cancer had a complete response to the mTORC1-selective inhibitor RMC-5552 that was ongoing beyond six months.
PTEN is one of the most frequently inactivated tumour suppressors in glioblastoma, where loss-of-function mutations and deletions are common.
Germline PTEN loss causes the PTEN hamartoma tumour syndromes, including Cowden syndrome, with hamartomas, macrocephaly and elevated breast, thyroid and endometrial cancer risk.
notes: Well-established link, supported by the primary literature.

mechanism: PTEN is frequently inactivated in prostate cancer through mutation or deletion, raising flux through the PI3K-AKT pathway.
Loss of the PIP3 3-phosphatase PTEN allows PIP3 to accumulate, raising flux through PDK1 and AKT into the branched distal network.
PTEN loss raises network flux while AKT retains mTORC1-independent output to GSK3beta, FOXO and MDM2, so no mTOR-node dependency is created.
Receptor tyrosine kinase amplification converges on PI3K, raising network flux without creating dependency on the mTOR node specifically.
Receptor tyrosine kinase amplification converges on PI3K and belongs among the distal-network alterations.
LKB1 loss removes the principal activating kinase of AMPK, withdrawing AMPK-mediated restraint of mTORC1 via TSC2 and Raptor Ser792.
Loss of STK11 is listed among the recurrent alterations in the pathway landscape, and STK11 was one of the five selection genes in the negative prospective everolimus basket study.
Germline STK11 (LKB1) loss causes Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, with hamartomatous polyposis attributable in part to withdrawn AMPK restraint of mTORC1.
notes: Supported by the primary literature. STK11 loss of function also occurs as a somatic cancer lesion.

mechanism: Autosomal recessive STRADA loss impairs LKB1-AMPK signalling and causes PMSE syndrome with megalencephaly and intractable epilepsy.
notes: Rapamycin supported by preclinical and small clinical evidence.

mechanism: Biallelic STRADA loss impairs LKB1-AMPK signalling, removing energy-stress restraint of mTORC1 in PMSE syndrome.
Biallelic SZT2 mutations cause a neurodevelopmental syndrome with epilepsy through loss of KICSTOR-dependent GATOR1 recruitment.
Biallelic SZT2 loss disables the KICSTOR scaffold required for GATOR1 lysosomal recruitment, the clinical proof that the scaffold is non-redundant in humans.
Podocyte Tsc1 deletion produces focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, the upper limb of the podocyte Goldilocks requirement for calibrated mTORC1 activity.
Germline TSC1 loss with a somatic second hit produces constitutive mTORC1 activation in lesional tissue: cortical tubers, SEGA, angiomyolipoma and epilepsy.
Whole-genome sequencing of a durable everolimus complete responder found loss-of-function TSC1; TSC1 mutations occurred in roughly 8% of 109 further bladder cancers.
notes: Correlated with everolimus sensitivity and time on treatment.

mechanism: Liver-specific Tsc1 deletion constitutively activates mTORC1 yet protects against diet-induced steatosis, because S6K1-IRS-1 feedback suppresses hepatic insulin signalling and SREBP1c.
Tsc1 deletion in POMC neurons produces hyperphagic obesity, the converse manipulation to hypothalamic leucine sensing.

Whole-genome sequencing of a durable complete responder to everolimus identified a loss-of-function TSC1 mutation; TSC1 mutations were then found in approximately 8% of a further 109 bladder cancers and correlated with everolimus sensitivity and time on treatment.
notes: This is enrichment rather than prediction: a proximal-brake lesion is necessary but not sufficient for rapalog sensitivity.

mechanism: Tsc1 deletion restricted to microglia produces severe early-onset spontaneous recurrent seizures, showing epileptogenesis is not cell-autonomous to neurons.
notes: If a glial compartment contributes, the cell type in which a drug engages target may determine efficacy.

mechanism: TSC1 loss destabilises the TSC complex and abolishes TSC2 GAP activity toward Rheb, so Rheb-GTP accumulates and mTORC1 is constitutively activated.
context: germline plus somatic second hit, or somatic

mechanism: TSC1 loss impairs the TSC complex and releases Rheb-dependent mTORC1 signalling.
notes: This classification does not establish mTORC1 as the only affected process or guarantee treatment response.

mechanism: TSC1 and TSC2 act alongside MTOR, PIK3CA and AKT3 in focal cortical dysplasia type II, through somatic mosaic activation confined to the malformed cortex.
TSC2-deficient smooth-muscle-like cells with constitutive mTORC1 activity drive the cystic lung destruction of LAM, sporadic or TSC-associated.
notes: LAM is a feature of TSC and sirolimus is approved for it; the lesion-to-LAM link comes from the primary literature.

mechanism: Germline TSC2 loss of function with a somatic second hit abolishes TSC2 GAP activity toward Rheb, producing constitutive mTORC1 activation in lesional tissue, the molecular basis of tuberous sclerosis complex.
Tsc2 acts as a molecular checkpoint controlling osteoblast development and glucose homeostasis.
In AMPECT, response to nab-sirolimus in malignant PEComa was enriched in TSC2-mutant tumours.
TSC2 loss removes the asparagine-thumb GAP that accelerates Rheb GTP hydrolysis roughly 100-fold, producing constitutive Rheb-GTP and mTORC1 activation.
context: germline plus somatic second hit, or somatic

mechanism: TSC2 loss removes the Rheb GTPase-activating function that normally restrains mTORC1.
notes: Clinical response depends on disease and treatment context.

mechanism: Everolimus is an ABCB1 substrate; brain accumulation is restricted by the transporter and rises when it is absent or pharmacologically inhibited.

Efflux at the blood-brain barrier shields the CNS from systemic exposure but equally limits target engagement wherever the brain is the therapeutic object, decoupling central from peripheral exposure.
notes: A dose titrated to a peripheral marker such as whole-blood S6K1 phosphorylation is not thereby titrated in brain.

mechanism: P-glycoprotein effluxes sirolimus at the apical membrane of enterocytes, which together with first-pass CYP3A metabolism keeps oral bioavailability low: approximately 14% for the oral solution, with tablet exposure about 27% higher and not bioequivalent to it. The same transporter handling underlies the extensive drug-interaction profile of the drug.

Temsirolimus and the sirolimus it yields are P-glycoprotein substrates, so efflux limits their distribution into tissues, most consequentially across the blood-brain barrier. Because temsirolimus is administered intravenously, intestinal efflux does not contribute to its systemic exposure.
Added to fulvestrant in a population prospectively selected for PIK3CA mutation, alpelisib improved progression-free survival from 5.7 to 11.0 months: biomarker selection succeeds at the PI3K node.
Alpelisib selectively inhibits the p110-alpha catalytic subunit at the ATP site, lowering PIP3 and hence AKT and downstream mTORC1 activation.
Apitolisib inhibits mTOR at the ATP site alongside class I PI3K, abolishing output of both complexes.

Class I PI3K inhibition lowers PIP3 and therefore both AKT recruitment and mSin1-dependent mTORC2 activation. In a randomised comparison with everolimus in renal cell carcinoma, apitolisib produced shorter progression-free survival and markedly more high-grade hyperglycaemia and rash, illustrating the toxicity ceiling that limited dual PI3K-mTOR inhibitors developed to pre-empt feedback reactivation.

The ATP-binding cleft lies in the bilobed kinase domain of mTOR and is identical in mTORC1 and mTORC2, which is why agents that occupy it inhibit both complexes, unlike allosteric agents acting at the FRB domain.
AZD8055 reduces phosphorylation of 4E-BP1 at Thr37/Thr46, thereby favouring its repressive interaction with eIF4E.
notes: Indirect activation of the translational repressor through reduced mTORC1-dependent phosphorylation; the drug does not directly activate 4E-BP1.

mechanism: AZD8055 is a potent, selective, orally bioavailable ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitor active against both complexes, with antitumour activity in vitro and in vivo.
ATP-competitive occupancy of the catalytic cleft inhibits mTORC2 as well as mTORC1, abolishing AKT Ser473 phosphorylation.
Capivasertib is an ATP-competitive pan-AKT inhibitor, blocking both the mTORC1-directed arm (through TSC2 and PRAS40) and the mTORC1-independent outputs to GSK3-beta, FOXO and MDM2.
Added to fulvestrant in AKT-pathway-altered tumours, capivasertib improved progression-free survival from 3.1 to 7.3 months: selection also succeeds at the AKT node, but not at mTOR.

Calcineurin inhibitors block calcineurin-NFAT signalling in the pancreatic beta cell, reducing insulin secretion and beta-cell mass and producing new-onset diabetes after transplantation, with tacrolimus carrying the higher risk of the two agents. This mechanism is distinct from the direct beta-cell toxicity and mTORC2-dependent peripheral insulin resistance associated with sirolimus.

Cyclosporine binds cyclophilin A rather than FKBP12; the drug-immunophilin binary complex is the active species. This is the structural reason cyclosporine does not compete with rapamycin for FKBP12 whereas tacrolimus does.
Cyclosporine acts through cyclophilin A rather than FKBP12, but the resulting complex inhibits the same calcineurin phosphatase, giving the shared NFAT-dependent beta-cell toxicity of the class.
Everolimus is likewise a CYP3A4 substrate, giving extensive interaction potential with azoles, macrolides, rifampicin and anticonvulsants and requiring exposure-guided dosing.

In mice, CYP3A acts together with plasma carboxylesterase to clear everolimus systemically and so sets the blood concentration from which central exposure derives; restriction of brain penetration itself is attributed chiefly to P-glycoprotein at the blood-brain barrier.

CYP3A4 in gut and liver demethylates and hydroxylates sirolimus, so CYP3A4 inducers and inhibitors shift its exposure several-fold; whole-blood trough monitoring, commonly in the range of 5-15 ng/mL in transplantation, is therefore standard.

Temsirolimus is cleared principally by hepatic CYP3A4, which hydroxylates and demethylates it, so CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers markedly alter its exposure. The drug is given intravenously, so no intestinal first-pass step contributes, and its principal active metabolite sirolimus arises by hydrolysis of the temsirolimus ester rather than by CYP3A4.
The imidazoquinoline scaffold occupies the ATP site of mTOR as well as of PI3K, giving simultaneous blockade of both nodes of the axis.
Dual blockade of class I PI3K was intended to pre-empt the receptor tyrosine kinase-driven AKT rebound that follows mTOR inhibition, but met the same toxicity ceiling.

Prophylactic dexamethasone mouthwash started together with everolimus reduced grade 2 or higher stomatitis far below the incidence reported in earlier everolimus trials without prophylaxis, although the comparison was with historical rates in a single-arm trial. Mucositis nevertheless remains dose-limiting for mTOR-directed agents at higher exposures.
Added to exemestane, everolimus improved median progression-free survival from 2.8 to 6.9 months; the benefit was independent of PIK3CA genotype and overall survival did not reach significance.
context: BOLERO-2, HR-positive HER2-negative, after aromatase inhibitor
notes: Genotype-independence is established; the proposed mechanism, a general brake on translational and metabolic output, remains contested.

mechanism: Small uncontrolled series reported variable responses: the 2023 series included one NPRL3 worsening; in 2025 all four NPRL2/NPRL3 participants improved, including two with seizure freedom.
notes: Clinical efficacy and genotype-based response prediction require controlled studies.

mechanism: Progression-free survival improved from 4.6 to 11.0 months in pancreatic and from 3.9 to 11.0 months in non-functional gastrointestinal and lung neuroendocrine tumours, diseases dependent on 4E-BP and TOP mRNA control.

In renal cell carcinoma progressing after VEGFR-directed therapy, everolimus extended median progression-free survival from 1.9 to 4.9 months in the final analysis of RECORD-1, without an overall survival benefit, consistent with a cytostatic effect on HIF-dependent translation and the angiogenic programme rather than on a cell-autonomous mTORC1 dependency.
In TSC, biallelic loss of a direct mTORC1 restraint makes the lesion fully mTORC1-dependent: roughly 35% achieved SEGA volume reduction, 42% angiomyolipoma reduction and 30-40% seizure reduction.
notes: The case in which the rapalog mechanistic rationale is fully borne out, and the standard against which other indications should be judged.

mechanism: Exceptional-responder literature: a durable complete remission in metastatic urothelial carcinoma with a loss-of-function TSC1 mutation alongside an NF2 nonsense mutation, with TSC1 mutations subsequently found in about 8% of 109 further bladder cancers and correlated with everolimus sensitivity; a second complete responder carried two activating MTOR mutations. A prospective basket study selected for proximal-brake lesions was nonetheless negative.
context: case-level responses; prospective biomarker selection not validated
notes: Genotype-directed rapalog therapy outside TSC remains preliminary, and as a basis for routine biomarker selection it is contested.

mechanism: Everolimus lowers mTORC1-dependent phosphorylation of 4E-BP1 and so favours sequestration of eIF4E, but suppression is site-selective: Ser65 and Thr70, which require prior priming and sustained mTORC1 activity, are suppressed, whereas the priming sites Thr37 and Thr46 remain largely phosphorylated. Cap-dependent translation of messages with structured 5' untranslated regions is therefore only partly inhibited.
notes: Indirect activation of the translational repressor through reduced mTORC1-dependent phosphorylation; the drug does not directly activate 4E-BP1.

mechanism: The 40-O-(2-hydroxyethyl) substitution alters pharmacokinetics but not mechanism: everolimus acts only as an FKBP12 binary complex engaging the FRB of mTORC1.
As the FKBP12 complex, everolimus restricts substrate access to assembled mTORC1; S6K1 Thr389 is fully suppressed while 4E-BP1 Thr37/Thr46 is not.

Kinetic rather than absolute selectivity: with prolonged exposure the FKBP12-rapalog complex captures newly synthesised mTOR before its incorporation into mTORC2, so chronic dosing inhibits mTORC2 in many cell types even though preassembled mTORC2 is spared acutely.
context: chronic or prolonged exposure only; preassembled mTORC2 spared acutely
notes: The primary data in [527] are for rapamycin; extension to everolimus is a class-level inference.

mechanism: 42% of patients achieved at least 50% angiomyolipoma volume reduction in EXIST-2, in TSC-associated or sporadic lymphangioleiomyomatosis-associated disease.
context: tuberous sclerosis complex and sporadic LAM; EXIST-2

mechanism: Hyperglycaemia under everolimus has two contributions with different complex attribution: impaired beta-cell insulin secretion, which follows mTORC1 inhibition, and peripheral insulin resistance, which follows the mTORC2 inhibition that develops with prolonged exposure. mTORC2 is the more heavily implicated of the two.

In the 218-participant vaccine trial, PD-1-positive CD4 and CD8 T cell fractions fell during six weeks of low-dose everolimus, consistent with partial mTORC1 inhibition reversing features of T cell exhaustion in immunosenescence.
context: six weeks before influenza vaccination; adults aged 65 or older
notes: Secondary immunophenotyping endpoint of one randomised trial; unreplicated, and its relation to clinical immune competence is unestablished.

mechanism: Non-infectious pneumonitis occurs in roughly 5-15% of oncology patients; the mechanism is incompletely understood and probably immune-mediated, with no clear complex attribution.
notes: The most serious and least mechanistically understood rapalog toxicity; vigilance and discontinuation are the only mitigations.

mechanism: In the 264-participant phase 2a trial, six weeks of BEZ235 plus low-dose everolimus reduced participant-reported infections during one year of follow-up.
notes: This does not isolate the contribution of either drug or establish efficacy in later trials.

mechanism: Allosteric mTORC1 inhibition in lesions with biallelic inactivation of a direct mTORC1 restraint; approximately 35% of patients achieved at least 50% SEGA volume reduction versus 0% on placebo in the EXIST programme.
notes: Covers the composite TSC indication rather than the three distinct EXIST endpoints, which set the standard against which other indications should be judged.

mechanism: Adjunctive everolimus reduced treatment-resistant focal-onset seizures, with 30-40% of patients achieving at least 50% seizure reduction in EXIST-3.
Stomatitis affects roughly 30-60% of patients depending on indication and reflects the mTORC1 dependence of the rapidly renewing oral epithelium; it is dose-limiting in several oncology regimens.
Allosteric mTORC1 inhibition abolishes phosphorylation of the S6K1 hydrophobic motif; S6K1 suppression by rapalogs is complete, in contrast to the partial suppression of 4E-BP1.
The ternary structure shows the drug sandwiched between FKBP12 and a hydrophobic FRB cleft; neither protein contacts the other substantially, so binding is strictly drug-dependent.
notes: Ternary complex structure: Choi 1996, reference [108].

mechanism: With prolonged exposure the drug-immunophilin complex captures newly synthesised mTOR before it is incorporated into mTORC2, depleting the complex rather than inhibiting the assembled one.
notes: Kinetic, not structural, selectivity: acute experiments and chronic dosing study different pharmacology.

mechanism: Docking on the exposed FRB of assembled mTORC1 sterically restricts access of substrates to the already deep catalytic cleft rather than abolishing catalysis, giving partial, substrate-selective inhibition.
The four-helix FRB domain lies between the FAT and kinase domains, above the substrate cleft, which is why an occupant of this site obstructs substrate entry.
KU-0063794 is an ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitor selective over related PI3K-family kinases, blocking both complexes; used to attribute effects to mTOR rather than to PI3K.
Specific ATP-competitive mTOR inhibition blocks both complexes, including AKT Ser473 phosphorylation by mTORC2.

Metformin lowers mTORC1 activity indirectly and does not bind mTOR. One route is AMPK-dependent, through phosphorylation of Raptor at Ser792 and enhancement of TSC2 GAP activity; a second is AMPK-independent, requires the Rag GTPases and was demonstrated in cells lacking AMPK or TSC2. Because of the second route, suppression of mTORC1 cannot be inferred from AMPK activation alone.
notes: The AMPK-independent, Rag-dependent route is dose-dependent and rests on a smaller body of work than the AMPK-dependent route.

mechanism: Albumin-bound sirolimus produced durable responses in advanced malignant PEComa, with response strongly enriched in TSC2-mutant tumours.
The albumin-bound nanoparticle alters delivery and tumour exposure only; the released sirolimus acts through FKBP12 on the FRB of mTORC1 as usual.
Nanoparticle albumin-bound sirolimus delivers sirolimus, which via FKBP12 engages the FRB domain of assembled mTORC1.
OSI-027 binds the mTOR ATP site and suppresses both mTORC1 and mTORC2 signalling, including 4E-BP1 phosphorylation resistant to rapamycin.
notes: ATP-competitive inhibitor of the mTOR kinase domain, documented in the primary literature.

mechanism: Selective ATP-competitive mTOR kinase inhibitor with activity against both mTORC1 and mTORC2.
PP242 occupies the mTOR ATP site and inhibits both complexes; it defined the rapamycin-resistant outputs of mTORC1 alongside Torin1.
Active-site inhibition blocks rapamycin-resistant outputs of mTORC1 and also inhibits mTORC2, abolishing AKT Ser473 phosphorylation.
The cyclosporine-cyclophilin A complex binds and inhibits calcineurin, converging on the same target as the tacrolimus-FKBP12 complex; neither free immunophilin inhibits the phosphatase.
The tethered ATP-site moiety delivers complete catalytic inhibition once the molecule is anchored through FKBP12, so inhibition does not depend on the allosteric effect alone.
The rapamycin end of the bi-steric molecule recruits FKBP12; the resulting avidity for the FRB-bearing complex is what confers mTORC1 selectivity on an otherwise non-selective ATP-site warhead.
FKBP12-RapaLink-1 engages the FRB domain, providing the anchoring half of the bi-steric mechanism.
Bivalent engagement of FRB and the ATP cleft on the same mTOR protomer gives an avidity-driven potency far above either moiety alone.
Bivalent engagement gives complete mTORC1 suppression and retains activity against FRB resistance mutations that abolish rapalog binding, establishing the bi-steric concept.

RapaLink-1 crosses the blood-brain barrier and accumulates in intracranial tumour tissue to a degree the first- and second-generation agents do not, which is the basis of its preclinical activity in glioblastoma models.
context: preclinical glioblastoma models; no human data
notes: Bears on the pharmacokinetic constraint that restricted CNS access limits every neurological indication.

mechanism: RapaLink-1 tethers rapamycin to an ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitor, so that FKBP12-rapamycin anchoring at the FRB domain delivers the active-site moiety with high avidity. Potency is therefore retained against FRB-domain substitutions such as A2034V and F2108L, which weaken FKBP12-rapamycin binding and confer rapalog resistance, and against the kinase-domain substitution M2327I, which confers resistance to ATP-competitive inhibitors used alone.
context: FRB-domain and kinase-domain mTOR resistance mutants

mechanism: Two opposing effects: relief of S6K1-IRS-1 feedback raises PI3K-dependent Thr308 signalling, while prolonged mTORC2 depletion lowers Ser473. Net direction depends on exposure duration and cell type.
Relieving mTORC1 repression of ULK1 and TFEB induces autophagy and accelerates clearance of amyloid-beta, alpha-synuclein and polyglutamine aggregates in cellular and animal models.
notes: No controlled human efficacy data exist in neurodegenerative disease.

mechanism: Suppression of mTORC1-dependent effector lymphocyte expansion prevents renal allograft rejection; this was the first approved indication and is given at continuous, trough-monitored exposures.

Sirolimus stabilises lung function in lymphangioleiomyomatosis, whose lesional cells carry biallelic TSC2 inactivation with constitutive mTORC1 activation as the principal driver; it also reduces serum VEGF-D and improves symptoms.
In kidney transplant recipients without pre-existing diabetes, sirolimus was independently associated with new-onset diabetes across regimens, with adjusted hazard ratios of roughly 1.4-1.7.
notes: The diabetogenic signal is clearest at high continuous exposures; extrapolation to intermittent low-dose use is not supported.

mechanism: Thr37/Thr46 phosphorylation is relatively rapamycin-resistant in many experimental settings, limiting restoration of 4E-BP1-mediated repression of eIF4E.
notes: Phosphosite sensitivity and the resulting translational response depend on cell type and exposure.

mechanism: Rapamycin binds the FKBP12 immunophilin with low-nanomolar affinity; the binary complex, not free drug, is the inhibitory species, so FKBP12 is obligatory for all rapalog action.
Rapamycin contributes the second half of the composite surface, its effector domain projecting away from FKBP12 to contact the FRB domain of mTOR.
mTORC1 phosphorylation stabilises Grb10, an inhibitor of insulin and IGF-1 receptor signalling; drug-induced loss of that stabilisation removes a second brake on upstream flux.
Inhibiting mTORC1 removes S6K1-mediated inhibitory serine phosphorylation of IRS-1, stabilising it and restoring insulin- and IGF-1-driven PI3K output: the feedback arm of AKT rebound.
Acute inhibition is complex-selective because only mTORC1 presents an accessible FRB; suppression is substrate-selective, complete for S6K1 and incomplete for 4E-BP1.
Chronic dosing lowers mTORC2 output, including AKT Ser473, in many but not all cell types, by blocking assembly of new complexes; selectivity for mTORC1 is therefore kinetic rather than absolute.
notes: Cell-type variability in mTORC2 sensitivity is itself well replicated.

mechanism: Rapamycin reduces brain amyloid-beta and improves cognition in 3xTg-AD mice, with benefit dependent on intact autophagy and largely confined to treatment initiated before substantial pathology accumulates.
context: 3xTg-AD mice; benefit requires intact autophagy and early initiation; no controlled human efficacy data
notes: No controlled human efficacy data exist.

mechanism: Low-dose rapamycin given during acute viral infection increases both the quantity and the functional quality of memory CD8 T cells, T cell-intrinsically and across infection models and in primates.
Low-dose rapamycin improved circadian reporter amplitude in engineered U2OS cells expressing SKS-associated MTOR variants.
context: engineered U2OS reporter cells; not patient-derived cells

mechanism: Haematopoietic progenitors require mTORC1 for proliferation, so suppression produces anaemia, thrombocytopenia and neutropenia; dose reduction is the standard response.
Higher-dose rapamycin precipitated delayed sleep-wake phase disorder in some Smith-Kingsmore patients, the mirror image of the low-dose benefit on circadian amplitude.
notes: Clearest human evidence that mTOR-directed therapy in the nervous system is dose- and time-dependent in direction.

mechanism: Inhibition of mTOR raises plasma cholesterol alongside triglycerides through reduced lipoprotein lipase activity, increased adipose lipolysis and impaired clearance of apolipoprotein B-containing lipoproteins; the effect is dose-related at therapeutic exposures and is managed by lipid monitoring and statin therapy.
notes: Hypercholesterolaemia and hypertriglyceridaemia arise from the same disturbance of hepatic and adipose lipid handling and usually occur together.

mechanism: Chronic exposure raises glucose through combined beta-cell dysfunction and mTORC2-dependent peripheral insulin resistance; attribution is mTORC2 greater than mTORC1.
notes: Whether intermittent low-exposure regimens avoid this effect is unresolved.

mechanism: Hypothalamic mTORC1 acts as a nutrient sensor in the arcuate nucleus: rapamycin abolishes the anorectic response to intracerebroventricular leucine and partially corrects the hyperphagic obesity produced by Tsc1 deletion in POMC neurons. This raises the possibility that part of the metabolic toxicity attributed to liver, adipose and beta cell is centrally mediated.
notes: This makes tissue-level attribution of metabolic toxicity from peripheral measurements less secure than it appears.

mechanism: Altered hepatic and adipose lipid handling under inhibition of both complexes raises triglycerides and cholesterol in a dose-related manner; monitoring and statin therapy are the usual mitigation.
Suppressed angiogenesis and fibroblast proliferation delay surgical healing, which is why planned perioperative interruption is advised before elective surgery.
Suppression of effector lymphocyte expansion raises infection risk at immunosuppressive exposures; dose, schedule and vaccination timing are the available levers.
notes: Contrasts with enhanced vaccine and CD8 memory responses at low, partial-inhibition exposures.

mechanism: Prolonged dosing disrupts mTORC2 in liver, muscle and adipose tissue, producing insulin resistance that is mechanistically separable from the longevity benefit in mice.

In the PEARL trial, lean tissue mass increased rather than decreased in women receiving 10 mg weekly compounded rapamycin, against the anabolic-resistance concern that chronic mTORC1 inhibition should reduce muscle mass in older adults.
context: women, 10 mg weekly compounded sirolimus, 48 weeks; secondary endpoint, exposure not confirmed by trough measurement
notes: Lean-mass monitoring is one of the measurements a serious geroscience trial must include; the direction of effect is unresolved, hence 'modulates'.

mechanism: Encapsulated rapamycin begun at 600 days of age raised age at 90% mortality by 9% in male and 14% in female genetically heterogeneous mice at three independent sites; a threefold higher dietary dose of 42 ppm raised median lifespan by 23% in males and 26% in females, and late-life intermittent regimens also extended survival.
context: genetically heterogeneous mice, Interventions Testing Program
notes: Genetic reduction of mTOR or S6K1 reproduces the effect, supporting on-target action; translation beyond rodents is unproven.

mechanism: Rapamycin blocks hypertrophy in response to IGF-1, mechanical overload and chronic stimulation, and blocks the contraction-induced rise in human muscle protein synthesis, showing that mTORC1 activity is required for load-induced muscle growth.
context: rodent overload models and human contraction studies
notes: Ageing muscle already responds less strongly to loading and to amino acids, so lean mass is the principal concern during chronic exposure in older adults.

mechanism: Non-infectious pneumonitis occurs in roughly 5-15% of oncology patients treated with rapalogs and is the most serious and least well understood toxicity of the class. It is probably immune-mediated rather than a direct consequence of mTORC1 blockade in lung epithelium, and management rests on vigilance, dose interruption and discontinuation.
notes: Reported for both sirolimus and everolimus; the best-characterised series come from everolimus-treated renal cell carcinoma.

mechanism: Podocytes require mTORC1 for maintenance and autophagic flux, so inhibition can produce proteinuria; urinalysis monitoring is the recommended surveillance.
Induction of macroautophagy accelerates clearance of alpha-synuclein and polyglutamine-expanded huntingtin, reducing aggregate burden and improving outcomes in fly and mouse models.
Loss of mTORC1-dependent renewal in oral epithelium produces aphthous-type ulceration in roughly 30-60% of patients, the commonest dose-limiting rapalog toxicity in oncology.
mTOR inhibition blocks Th1, Th2 and Th17 differentiation while permitting Foxp3+ regulatory T cell differentiation and expansion, which underlies the immunosuppressive use of the drug.
Acute rapamycin blocks the contraction-induced rise in human muscle protein synthesis, and mTORC1 activation is required for the response to essential amino acids.
notes: The tissue most clearly requiring mTORC1 is also the one most at risk from chronic inhibition in older adults.

mechanism: Cryo-EM shows Rictor, together with mSin1, covering the FRB surface of mTOR within mTORC2, which is the structural basis for the rapamycin insensitivity of preassembled mTORC2.
notes: mSin1 (MAPKAP1) contributes to the same occlusion

mechanism: Ridaforolimus binds FKBP12, and the binary complex engages the exposed FRB domain of assembled mTORC1, inhibiting the kinase allosterically as for the other first-generation rapalogs.
FKBP12-ridaforolimus complex binds the exposed FRB domain of assembled mTORC1 and sterically restricts substrate access.

The ATP-competitive moiety occupies the kinase cleft, delivering complete catalytic inhibition of the FRB-anchored complex and thereby full suppression of both S6K1 and 4E-BP1 while mTORC2 is relatively spared.
notes: Explains the dissociation of complete mTORC1 pathway blockade from metabolic toxicity (hyperglycaemia 4%).

mechanism: In 57 patients with advanced solid tumours, disease control was reached in 64% at active doses and one PTEN- and PIK3CA-altered endometrial cancer achieved a complete response with clearance of variants from ctDNA.
context: first-in-human phase 1, 58% with pathogenic mTOR-pathway variants
notes: A single-arm disease-control rate is not an efficacy endpoint; the genotype-dependence prediction remains preliminary.

mechanism: One patient with PTEN- and PIK3CA-altered endometrial cancer achieved a complete response ongoing beyond six months, with clearance of pathway variants from circulating tumour DNA.
context: single case within a phase 1 dose-escalation study
notes: A single response is an observation rather than a result; the evidence remains preliminary.

mechanism: The bi-steric agent carries an FKBP12-rapamycin moiety tethered by a linker to an ATP-site moiety; FKBP12 binding supplies the avidity that confers mTORC1 selectivity.
The FKBP12-bound moiety engages the exposed FRB domain of assembled mTORC1, anchoring the molecule and delivering the tethered ATP-site moiety to the kinase cleft of the same protomer.
RMC-5552 was designed for mTORC1 selectivity with complete pathway suppression, exploiting FKBP12-mediated avidity for the complex whose FRB is exposed.
mTORC2 is relatively spared because engagement depends on an accessible FRB; the clinical correlate is treatment-related hyperglycaemia in only 4% despite complete mTORC1 blockade.
notes: Sparing is relative, not absolute, and rests on a single-arm phase 1 dataset.

mechanism: Treatment-related fatigue in 42% of patients in the first-in-human dose-escalation study.
notes: The frequency comes from one uncontrolled dose-escalation cohort and has not been independently replicated.

mechanism: Treatment-related hyperglycaemia occurred in only 4% and was not dose-limiting despite complete mTORC1 pathway suppression: the dissociation of efficacy from metabolic toxicity predicted by mTORC2 sparing.
notes: The most direct available human evidence, but from a single uncontrolled study.

mechanism: Second most frequent treatment-related adverse event (44%) in the 57-patient first-in-human dose-escalation study.
context: phase 1 dose escalation, intravenous weekly dosing
notes: The frequency comes from one uncontrolled dose-escalation cohort and has not been independently replicated.

mechanism: Mucositis occurred in 49% of 57 patients and grade 3 mucositis was dose-limiting at 10 mg or above, making it the characteristic limitation of the bi-steric generation.
notes: Single-arm dose-escalation data; the direction is consistent with the oral-epithelial toxicity seen with allosteric rapalogs.

mechanism: RTB101 (BEZ235/dactolisib) is an ATP-competitive PI3K/mTOR inhibitor. At the low exposures studied in older adults, the intended pharmacodynamic effect was preferential TORC1 inhibition.
notes: The immune-function trials did not establish a lifespan benefit.

mechanism: In the 264-participant phase 2a trial, six weeks of RTB101 with low-dose everolimus reduced participant-reported infections during one year of follow-up.
notes: This does not isolate the contribution of either drug or establish efficacy in later trials.

mechanism: The 1024-participant phase 3 trial did not meet its clinically symptomatic respiratory-illness endpoint. Phase 2b had found a signal for laboratory-confirmed infections with RTB101 monotherapy, while its combination comparison was not significant.
notes: Different endpoints and study populations limit cross-trial comparisons; failure cannot be attributed to removal of everolimus.

mechanism: BEZ235 inhibits class I PI3K at sufficient concentrations; this biochemical target profile does not demonstrate substantial PI3K inhibition at the low doses used in the ageing trials.
notes: Target inhibition depends on exposure; the clinical studies described RTB101 as a TORC1 inhibitor.

mechanism: ATP-competitive mTOR inhibition regulates AKT biphasically. Catalytic blockade of mTORC2 abolishes Ser473 phosphorylation and suppresses AKT activity acutely; relief of S6K1-IRS-1 and Grb10 feedback then drives receptor tyrosine kinase-dependent PI3K signalling, so Thr308 phosphorylation and AKT activity rebound while Ser473 phosphorylation remains suppressed.
context: class effect of ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitors
notes: The rebound is a principal reason why superior pathway suppression did not translate into clinical efficacy for this class.

mechanism: ATP-competitive occupancy of the mTOR kinase cleft suppresses phosphorylation of all four principal 4E-BP1 sites, including Thr37 and Thr46, which allosteric rapalogs leave largely intact. Hypophosphorylated 4E-BP1 is the active form, so eIF4E is sequestered and cap-dependent translation of mRNAs with structured 5' untranslated regions is blocked.
notes: Indirect activation of the translational repressor through reduced mTORC1-dependent phosphorylation; the drug does not directly activate 4E-BP1.

mechanism: Occupying the ATP cleft blocks catalysis outright, suppressing all mTORC1 outputs including the rapamycin-resistant 4E-BP1 Thr37/Thr46 sites.
Because the kinase cleft is identical in both complexes and is not occluded by Rictor or mSin1, ATP-competitive agents abolish mTORC2 output including AKT Ser473.
Complete inhibition of both complexes adds mTORC2-dependent hyperglycaemia and insulin resistance to the rapalog toxicity profile, which is the toxicity ceiling that limited this generation.
notes: Attribution of the glycaemic component to mTORC2 rests chiefly on reference [325].

mechanism: Catalytic inhibition of mTORC2 removes AKT Ser473 phosphorylation in liver, adipose tissue and skeletal muscle. Reduced AKT output releases FOXO1-driven hepatic gluconeogenesis and impairs insulin-stimulated glucose uptake, so insulin resistance and hyperglycaemia are added to the metabolic profile of the allosteric agents.

ATP-competitive inhibition of the mTOR catalytic site abolishes phosphorylation of S6K1 at the Thr389 hydrophobic motif completely, in contrast with the partial and substrate-selective suppression achieved by allosteric agents.

Calcineurin inhibition in the pancreatic beta cell impairs insulin secretion and promotes beta-cell apoptosis, which is the principal mechanism of new-onset diabetes after transplantation in tacrolimus-based regimens.
notes: Sirolimus independently raises the risk of post-transplant diabetes, so the two immunosuppressant classes contribute separately.

mechanism: FK506 binds the same immunophilin as rapamycin but presents a different effector surface, so the FKBP12-FK506 complex engages calcineurin rather than the FRB of mTOR.
FK506 and rapamycin compete for the same FKBP12 binding pocket, so co-exposure antagonises formation of the mTORC1-inhibitory complex: a pharmacodynamic interaction relevant to combined regimens.
Topical tacrolimus mouthwash prophylaxis reduced mucositis from 65% to 31% in the 8-12 mg cohorts of the RMC-5552 phase 1 study; systemic exposure is not the object.
notes: Single-arm comparison within a dose-escalation study.

mechanism: The FKBP12-FK506 complex binds and inhibits the calcineurin phosphatase, blocking NFAT dephosphorylation and IL-2 transcription; this is a distinct mechanism from mTOR inhibition.
Temsirolimus improved overall survival versus interferon-alpha in the Global ARCC trial in poor-prognosis advanced renal cell carcinoma.
notes: Basis of the approved indication in poor-prognosis advanced renal cell carcinoma.

mechanism: Temsirolimus binds FKBP12, and the binary complex engages the exposed FRB domain of assembled mTORC1 by the same allosteric mechanism as the parent macrolide.

Temsirolimus binds FKBP12 and the binary complex engages the exposed FRB domain of assembled mTORC1, sterically restricting substrate access; it is given intravenously as an ester prodrug converted to sirolimus, which contributes much of the effect in vivo.
CCI-779 (temsirolimus), the soluble ester analogue of rapamycin, induces autophagy and reduces polyglutamine aggregate burden and toxicity in fly and mouse models of Huntington disease.
context: fly and mouse Huntington disease models

mechanism: Temsirolimus is given intravenously as an ester prodrug and is hydrolysed to sirolimus, which accounts for much of its systemic exposure and activity.
Torin1 inhibits mTORC1 catalysis directly at the ATP site and was the tool compound that revealed rapamycin-resistant mTORC1 functions.
Torin1 blocks mTORC2 as well, abolishing AKT Ser473 phosphorylation, and is used experimentally to separate complex-selective from pan-mTOR effects.

Torin2 occupies the mTOR ATP-binding cleft and inhibits both complexes, including the rapamycin-resistant 4E-BP1 sites. It is more potent and more orally bioavailable than Torin1 but also inhibits the related PIKK family members ATM, ATR and DNA-PK, so selectivity for mTOR is incomplete at higher concentrations.
notes: Used as a laboratory tool compound rather than a clinical agent.

mechanism: Genotype within the GATOR1 complex appears to influence everolimus response in the familial focal epilepsies: in an open-label series, patients with DEPDC5 loss-of-function variants showed substantial seizure reduction, a patient with a DEPDC5 missense variant responded less, and the single NPRL3 patient worsened, whereas a later series in NPRL2- and NPRL3-related epilepsy reported seizure reduction in all four treated patients. The evidence is open-label and very small, and a controlled trial is required before this becomes practice.

Substitution of the critical serine contact in the FRB domain of human mTOR, Ser2035, abolishes docking of the FKBP12-rapamycin complex while leaving kinase activity intact. FRB substitutions selected under prolonged rapamycin exposure, Ala2034Val and Phe2108Leu, confer rapalog resistance by the same route, whereas the kinase-domain substitution Met2327Ile confers resistance to ATP-competitive inhibitors without preventing drug docking.
notes: Bivalent agents that engage the FRB and the ATP site together retain activity against these substitutions.

mechanism: Activating FAT- and kinase-domain MTOR variants raise kinase activity two- to ten-fold and were present in exceptional responders, including concurrent E2014K and E2419K in a urothelial complete responder treated with everolimus and pazopanib.
notes: No genomic biomarker of rapalog response has been prospectively validated.

mechanism: PIK3CA hotspot mutation was the prospective selection criterion in SOLAR-1 and predicts benefit, in contrast to its failure to predict rapalog benefit in the same disease.

TSC1 loss of function was identified in an exceptional everolimus responder and correlated with sensitivity and time on treatment in 109 further bladder cancers; prospective basket testing was negative.
context: urothelial carcinoma outside tuberous sclerosis complex
notes: A proximal-brake lesion is better described as necessary than sufficient for rapalog response.

mechanism: Response to albumin-bound sirolimus in malignant PEComa was strongly enriched in TSC2-mutant tumours, the clearest somatic example of a proximal-brake lesion enriching for rapalog benefit without establishing dependency in an individual tumour.
Vistusertib competes with ATP at the mTOR kinase cleft, inhibiting mTORC1 and mTORC2; it was selected from the AZD8055 series for improved pharmaceutical properties.

Vistusertib occupies the mTOR ATP cleft, which is common to both complexes, and therefore suppresses mTORC1 output completely, including the 4E-BP1 phosphorylation sites that allosteric agents leave only partly suppressed.

Because the ATP site is shared by both complexes and is not occluded by Rictor or mSin1, vistusertib inhibits mTORC2 as completely as mTORC1, abolishing AKT Ser473 phosphorylation; this is the source of the added metabolic toxicity of the ATP-competitive class.
notes: Site is the AKT readout of mTORC2 activity.

mechanism: Complete inhibition of mTORC2 by ATP-competitive agents produces hyperglycaemia through combined beta-cell dysfunction and peripheral insulin resistance, with mTORC2 contributing more than mTORC1; this metabolic ceiling limited clinical development of the class.
context: class-level attribution; vistusertib-specific incidence not reported
notes: Hyperglycaemia is reported across ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitors; no incidence specific to vistusertib is available.
